I yoke (to your car), to bring you quickly, your two docile horses, whose speed you have of old employed : may your horses, handsome Indra, bring you hither, and drink promptly of this well-effused agreeable libation.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> गोभि॑र्मिमि॒क्षुं द॑धिरे सुपा॒रमिंद्रं॒ ज्यैष्ठा॑य॒ धाय॑से  ॒
> गृणानाः ।  
> मं॒दा॒नः सोमं॑ पपि॒वा ऋ॑जीषि॒न्त्सम॒स्सभ्यं॑ पुरु॒धा गा  ॑
> इषण्य ॥ ३ ॥

> *gobhirmimikṣuṃ dadhire supāramiṃdraṃ jyaiṣṭhāya dhāyase*  
> *gṛṇānāḥ |*  
> *maṃdānaḥ somaṃ papivā ṛjīṣintsamassabhyaṃ purudhā gā*  
> *iṣaṇya ‖ 3 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> गोभिः । मिमिक्षुं । दधिरे । सुपारं । इंद्रं ज्यैष्ठाय । धायसे । गृणानाः ।  
> मंदानः । सोमं । पपिवान् । ऋजीषिन् । सं । अस्मभ्यं । पुरुधा । गाः । इषण्य ॥

> *gobhiḥ | mimikṣuṃ | dadhire | supāraṃ | iṃdraṃ jyaiṣṭhāya | dhāyase | gṛṇānāḥ |*  
> *maṃdānaḥ | somaṃ | papivān | ṛjīṣin | saṃ | asmabhyaṃ | purudhā | gāḥ | iṣaṇya ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> गृणानाः स्तोत्रं कुर्वाणा ऋत्विजो मिमिक्षुं स्तोतृणामभिमतफलं
> वर्षितुमिच्छंतं सुपारं शोभनपारं स्तुतिभिरभिमुखीकर्तुं शक्यमित्यर्थः । तादृशमिंद्रं ज्यैष्ठाय धनादिसंपत्ता श्रेष्ठत्वाय धायसे चिरकालमायुर्धारणाय
> च गोभिर्गॊमिश्रितैः सोमैर्दधिरे । धारयंति । शेषः प्रत्यक्षः । हे ऋजेषिन्
> सोमवन्निंद्र स त्वं मंदानो मोदमानः सोमं पपिवान् सोमस्य पाता सन्
> स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यं पुरुधा बहुधा गा अग्निहोत्रादिकर्मसिद्ध्यर्थं धेनूः समिषण्य।
> सम्यक् प्रेरय ॥ गोभिः । सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते न गोश्वन्नाववर्णॆति प्रतिषेधः । मिमिक्षुं। मिह सेचन इत्यस्य सन्येकाच इतीट् प्रतिषेधे हलंताच्चेति किद्वद्भावः । सनाशंसभिक्ष उः । प्रय्ययस्वरः । ज्यैष्ठाय । ज्येष्ठस्य भाव
> इत्यर्थे ब्राह्मणादित्वात् प्यञ् । इत्त्वादाद्युदात्तः । गृणानाः । ग्य शब्दे । क्रादित्वात् श्ना । चित्वादंतोदात्तः । मंदानः । मदि स्तुत्यादिष्टित्यस्य शानचि बहुलं

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests, praising, hold (offer) Soma mixed with milk (गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*), with cows' products) to that Indra who wishes to shower on the praisers their desired fruit and who is सुपारं (*supāraṃ*), one of good passage, that is, one who can easily be turned toward them by praises. They do so for excellence (ज्यैष्ठाय (*jyaiṣṭhāya*)) in wealth and other prosperity and for holding long life (धायसे (*dhāyase*)); the remainder of the verse is plain. O Indra, rich in Soma (ऋजेषिन् (*ṛjeṣin*)), you, rejoicing and having drunk the Soma, send forth to us, the praisers, many (पुरुधा (*purudhā*)) cows, milch cattle, for the accomplishment of rites such as the Agnihotra; send them well.

### Printed p. 129
*Gist (continued):* The remainder is grammatical only; it notes that पुरुधा (*purudhā*) is formed from a numeral-word with the affix meaning "in so many ways", and that इषण्य (*iṣaṇya*) is an imperative form from the root इष (*iṣa*).

> छंदसीति शपो लुक् । पुरुधा । पुरुष शब्द इह संख्यावाची । संख्याया विधार्थे
> धेति धाप्रत्ययः । इषण्य । इष गतौ । इषणमिच्छतीति छंदसि परेच्छायां क्यच्
> तदंतादंतर्भावितण्यर्थल्लोटि रूपं ॥

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- गृणानाः (*gṛṇānāḥ*)—the priests, the praisers
- मिमिक्षुं (*mimikṣuṃ*)—who wishes to shower the desired fruit
- सुपारं (*supāraṃ*)—who can be turned toward them by praise
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- ज्येष्ठाय (*jyeṣṭhāya*)—for excellent wealth and other prosperity **NOTE**
- धायसे (*dhāyase*)—for obtaining long life
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with Soma mixed with milk
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—they hold (vessels filled)
- यजीषिन् (*yajīṣin*)—O Indra, possessor of Soma **NOTE**
- मंदानः (*maṃdānaḥ*)—rejoicing
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- पपिवान् (*papivān*)—drinking
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us, the praisers
- पुरुधा (*purudhā*)—in great abundance
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the milch cows that furnish means for the sacrifice
- सं इषण्य (*saṃ iṣaṇya*)—furnish and give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The praising priests hold vessels filled with Soma mixed with milk toward Indra, who wishes to shower the desired fruit and can be turned toward them by praise, for excellent wealth and other prosperity and for obtaining long life. O Indra, rich in Soma, rejoicing and drinking the Soma, furnish to us, the praisers, in great abundance the cows useful for the sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
His adorers support with cattle, Indra, who is willing to bestow upon them their desires, and ready to come to the sacrifice, for the sake of obtaining eminent prosperity and prolonged life : acceptor of the spiritless Soma, who are the drinker of the Soma juice, and are exhilarated (by the draught), grant to us freely cattle in abundance.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इ॒मं कामं॑ मंदया॒ गोभि॒रश्चै॑श्चं॒द्रव॑ता॒ राध॑सा  ॒॑
> प्रप्रथश्च ।

> *imaṃ kāmaṃ maṃdayā gobhiraścaiścaṃdravatā rādhasā*  
> *praprathaśca |*

### Printed p. 130

> स्वयर्वो मतिभिस्तुभ्यं विप्रा इंद्राय वाहः कुशिकासो  
> अक्रन् ॥ ४ ॥

> *svayarvo matibhistubhyaṃ viprā iṃdrāya vāhaḥ kuśikāso*  
> *akran ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इमं । कामं । मंदय । गोभिः । अश्वैः । चंद्रवता । राधसा । पप्रथः । च ।  
> स्वःयवः । मतिभिः । तुभ्यं । विप्राः । इंद्राय । वाहः । कुशिकासः । अक्रन् ॥ ४ ॥

> *imaṃ | kāmaṃ | maṃdaya | gobhiḥ | aśvaiḥ | caṃdravatā | rādhasā | paprathaḥ | ca |*  
> *svaḥyavaḥ | matibhiḥ | tubhyaṃ | viprāḥ | iṃdrāya | vāhaḥ | kuśikāsaḥ | akran ‖ 4 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र इम धनादिविषयं काममस्मदीयमभिलाषं गोभिरग्नि होत्राडिकर्मसाधनभूतैर्गवादिभिर्वाहनसाधनभूतैरश्वैश्च चंद्रवता दीप्तियुक्तेन राधसा
> धनेन च मंदय । एतानि दत्तेममभिलाषं पूरय । किंच । एतैरस्मान्पप्रथः ।
> प्रथितांश्च कुरु । पश्चात्स्यर्यवः स्वर्गादिसुखमात्मन इच्छंतो विप्राः कर्मकुशलाः
> कुशिकासः कुशिका मतिभिर्मननीयैर्मंत्रैर्वाहः स्तोत्रमिंद्राय तुभ्यमक्रन् ।
> अकार्षुः ॥ मंदय । मदि स्तुत्यादिष्ठित्यस्य लोटि रूपं । गोभिः । सावेकाच इति
> विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वे प्राप्ते न गोश्वन्साववर्णेत्यादिना प्रतिषेधः । प्रकृतिस्वरः । पप्रथः ।
> प्रथ प्रख्याने । क्विप् । छंदस्युभयथेति तस्य सार्वधातुकत्वात् शप् । तस्य बहुलं
> छंदसीति श्लुः । धातुस्वरः । अक्रन् । करोतेर्लुजि मंत्रे घसह्वरेत्यादिना लुक् ।
> निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, gratify (मंदय (*maṃdaya*)) this desire of ours, concerning wealth and the like, with cows that are the means for rites such as the Agnihotra, with horses that are the means of conveyance, and with shining wealth (राधसा (*rādhasā*)). Give these and fulfil this desire. Further, make us extended, that is, renowned, by these. Afterwards the Kuśikas, wise (विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)), skilled in rites, desiring heaven and similar happiness for themselves, have made (अक्रन् (*akran*), "have done") praise for you, Indra, with thoughtful (मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)) mantras.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- इमं कामं (*imaṃ kāmaṃ*)—this desire of ours concerning wealth
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—by furnishing cows
- अश्वैः (*aśvaiḥ*)—and by horses
- चंद्रवता (*caṃdravatā*)—shining
- राधसा (*rādhasā*)—and by wealth
- मंदय (*maṃdaya*)—satisfy
- पप्रथः (*paprathaḥ*)—make (us) renowned
- स्वरवः (*svaravaḥ*)—those who desire the happiness of heaven and the like **NOTE**
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—skilled in rites
- कुशिकासः (*kuśikāsaḥ*)—the sages born of the Kuśika family
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—with words in the form of mantras
- वाहः (*vāhaḥ*)—praise
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for you, Indra
- अक्रन् (*akran*)—they have made

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, satisfy this desire of ours concerning wealth by giving us cows, horses and shining wealth. Make us renowned. The sages born in the Kuśika family, who desire the happiness of heaven and the like and are skilled in rites, have made praise for you, Indra, with words in the form of mantras.

### Printed p. 131

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Gratify this our desire (of wealth) with cows, with horses, with shining treasure, and make us renowned: the wise Kushikas, desirous of heaven, offer praise to you, Indra, with pious (prayers).

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिंद्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ वृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सतौ ।  
> शृ॒ण्वंत॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नंतं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒  ॑
> धनानां ॥ ५ ॥

> *śunaṃ huvema maghavānamiṃdramasminbhare vṛtamaṃ vājasatau |*  
> *śṛṇvaṃtamugramūtaye samatsu ghnaṃtaṃ vṛtrāṇi saṃjitaṃ*  
> *dhanānāṃ ‖ 5 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुनं । हुवेम । मघ्नवानं । इंद्रं । अस्मिन् ! भरे । नृतवं । वाजसात् ।  
> शृण्वंतं । उग्रं । ऊतये । समत्सु । घ्नंतं । वृत्राणि । संजितं । धनानां ॥

> *śunaṃ | huvema | maghnavānaṃ | iṃdraṃ | asmin ! bhare | nṛtavaṃ | vājasāt |*  
> *śṛṇvaṃtaṃ | ugraṃ | ūtaye | samatsu | ghnaṃtaṃ | vṛtrāṇi | saṃjitaṃ | dhanānāṃ ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वाजसात् । वाजस्यान्नस्य सातिर्लाभो यस्मिन् सोऽयं वाजसातिः।
> अस्मिन्भरे । बिभ्रति जयलक्ष्मीमनेन योद्वार इति भरः संग्रामः । तस्मिन् संग्रामे
> शुनं शूनमुत्साहेन प्रवृद्धं । यद्वा शुनमिति सुखनाम । सुखकरं मघवानं
> धनवंतं अत एवेंद्रं निरतिशयैश्वर्यसंपन्नं नृतमं सर्वस्य जगतोऽतिशयेन
> नेतारं त्वां हुवेम । कुशिका वयं । यज्ञार्थमाह्वयेम । तथा शृण्वंतमस्माभिः
> क्रियमाणां स्तुतिं शृण्वंतमुग्रं शत्रूणां भयंकरं समत्तु संग्रामेषु वृत्राणि
> वृत्रोपलक्षितानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि घ्नंतं हिंसंतं धनानां शत्रुसंबंधिनां संचितं
> सम्यग्जेतारं त्वामूतये रक्षणाय वयमाह्वयेम ॥ शुनं । टुओत्ति गतिवृद्धोरित्यस्य निष्ठायां यस्य विभाषेतीट् प्रतिषेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । दीर्घाभावश्चांदसः । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हुवेम । ह्वयतेर्बहुलं छंदसीति संप्रसारणे कृते
> शपो लुकि कृते च लिजि रूपं । निघातः । भरे । भृञ् भरणे । घः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः । वाजसात् । षणु दाने । भावे क्तिन् । जनसनेत्यादिनानुनासिकस्यात्वं ।
> बहुप्रीहौ पूर्वपदस्वरः । समत्तु अद भक्षणे । संपूर्वात् क्विप् । संभक्षयंति
> योद्धणामायूंषीति समदे संग्रामाः । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । घ्नंतं । हन हिंसागत्योरित्यस्य शतरि गमहनेत्यादिनोपधालोपः । हो हंतेठिति घत्वं । संजितं ।
> जि जये । क्विप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, in this भरे (*bhare*)", a battle, so called because warriors bear (बिभ्रति (*bibhrati*)) the goddess of victory by it, the "वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)" is that in which there is gain (सातिः (*sātiḥ*)) of food (वाज (*vāja*)). In that battle we call you, शुनं (*śunaṃ*), swollen, that is, grown strong in zeal; or else शुनमिति (*śunamiti*) is a name for happiness, so, the giver of happiness. You are मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*), wealthy, hence Indra, possessed of unsurpassed lordship, and नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*), the supreme leader of the whole world. We Kuśikas call you for the sacrifice. Likewise you hear the praise made by us, you are fierce (उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)), terrifying to enemies, in battles (समत्सु (*samatsu*)) you slay all the demons marked by Vṛtra, and you are the complete conqueror of the enemies' wealth. We call you, such a one, for protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)). The rest is grammar.

### Printed p. 132

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वाजसात् (*vājasāt*)—proceeding for the sake of food
- भरे (*bhare*)—in battle
- शुनं (*śunaṃ*)—one who grows with zeal, or one who produces happiness
- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—the wealthy one
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—the one endowed with unsurpassed lordship
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—the one who is the leader; you who are such
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—we pray and call (likewise)
- शृण्वंतं (*śṛṇvaṃtaṃ*)—the one who listens to (our praises)
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—the one who is terrible to enemies
- समत्तु (*samattu*)—in battles
- वृत्राणि (*vṛtrāṇi*)—the asuras beginning with Vṛtra
- घ्नंतं (*ghnaṃtaṃ*)—the one who injures and destroys
- धनानां (*dhanānāṃ*)—the wealth (of enemies)
- संचितं (*saṃcitaṃ*)—the one who gathers and gives (to us); you who are such
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—for protection
- हुवेम (*huvema*)—I pray and call.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, you who give happiness in the battle fought for the sake of food, who are wealthy, endowed with unsurpassed lordship, a leader, who listen to our praises, who are terrible to enemies, who in battles injure and destroy asuras such as Vṛtra, and who gather the wealth of enemies and give it to us — you we pray and call for protection.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We invoke for our protection the opulent Indra, distinguished in this combat, the leader in the food-bestowing (strife), hearing (our praises), terrible in battles, the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.

## Sūkta 51 (Maṇḍala 3)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चर्षणीधृतमिति द्वादशर्चं त्रयोदशं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रमैंद्रं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । चर्षणीधृतं द्वादशाद्यांत्यौ तृचौ जागतगायत्राविति । आद्यस्तृचो
> जागतोऽंत्यस्तृचो गायत्रः शिष्टा ऋचस्त्रिष्टुभः ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ।
> उक्ते क्रत्वा मैत्रा वरुणशस्त्रेऽनुरूपतृचानंतरमाद्यस्तृ चः शंसनीयः । सूत्रितं ।
> च चर्षणीधृतमस्तभ्नाद्दामसुर इति तृचौ आ. ६-१ । इति ॥ विषुवति निष्केवल्ये नृणामु त्वैति तृचः । विषुवानिति खंडे सूत्रितं । नृणामु त्वा नृतमं गीर्भिरुक्थैरिति
> शिस्त्रः । आ. ८-६ । इति ॥ बृहस्पतिसवेऽप्ययं तृचो निष्केवल्ये निविद्वान्नीयः । सूत्रितं
> च । नृणामु त्वैति मध्यंदिनः । आ. ९-५ । इति ॥ महाव्रतेऽपि निष्केवल्येऽयं तृचः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*) has twelve Ṛks and is Vaiśvāmitra (its seer is Viśvāmitra) and Aindra (its deity is Indra). The Anukramaṇikā says: चर्षणीधृतं द्वादशाद्यांत्यौ तृचौ जागतगायत्राविति (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ dvādaśādyāṃtyau tṛcau jāgatagāyatrāviti*), i.e. the first triplet is in Jagatī, the last triplet in Gāyatrī, and the remaining Ṛks are in Triṣṭubh. The use of the sūkta is Laiṅgika (by the indication of the text). In the ukthya rite (the Kannada reading उक्ते क्रत्वा (*ukte kratvā*) is garbled) **NOTE**, in the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra, after the anurūpa triplet, the first triplet of this sūkta is to be recited. It is stated in the sūtra: चर्षणीधृतमस्तभ्नाद्दामसुर इति तृचौ (*carṣaṇīdhṛtamastabhnāddāmasura iti tṛcau*) (Ā. 6-1). At the Viṣuvat in the niṣkevalya the triplet नृणामु त्वा (*nṛṇāmu tvā*) is used; this is stated in the Viṣuvān section: नृणामु त्वा नृतमं गीर्भिरुक्थैरिति शिस्त्रः (*nṛṇāmu tvā nṛtamaṃ gīrbhirukthairiti śistraḥ*) **NOTE** (Ā. 8-6). In the Bṛhaspatisava also this triplet is used as the nivid in the niṣkevalya; the sūtra says: नृणामु त्वैति मध्यंदिनः (*nṛṇāmu tvaiti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 9-5). In the Mahāvrata also this triplet is used in the niṣkevalya.

### Printed p. 133

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दशरात्रे चतुर्थेऽहनि मरुत्वतीय इंद्र मरुत्व इति तिस्रः । षष्ठेऽहनि षष्ठस्यॆति
> खंडे सूत्रितं । इंद्र मरुत्व इति तिस्र इति मरुत्वतीयं । आ. ८-१ । इति ॥ बृहस्पतिसवेऽपि मरुत्वतीयशस्त्रेऽयं तृचो निविद्धानीयः । सूत्रितं च । इंद्र मरुत्व
> इह नृणामु तैति मध्यंदिनः । आ ९ ५ । इति । आद्या मरुत्वतीयग्रहस्यानुवाक्या ।
> सूत्रितं च । मरुत्वतीयेन ग्रहेण चरंतींद्र मरुत्व इह पाहि सोमं । आ.
> ५-१४ । इति । तृतीये पर्याये होतुः शस्त्र इदं ह्यन्नोजसेति स्तोत्रियस्तृचः ।
> सूत्रितं च । इदं ह्यन्नोजसा महा इंद्रो य ओजसा । आ. ६-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the Daśarātra, on the fourth day, at the Marutvatīya, the three Ṛks इंद्र मरुत्व (*iṃdra marutva*) are used; the Khaṇḍa on the sixth day states: इंद्र मरुत्व इति तिस्र इति मरुत्वतीयं (*iṃdra marutva iti tisra iti marutvatīyaṃ*) (Ā. 8-1). In the Bṛhaspatisava also this triplet is used as the nivid in the Marutvatīya śastra; the sūtra says: इंद्र मरुत्व इह नृणामु तैति मध्यंदिनः (*iṃdra marutva iha nṛṇāmu taiti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 9-5). The first Ṛk is the anuvākyā of the Marutvatīya cup; the sūtra says: मरुत्वतीयेन ग्रहेण चरंतींद्र मरुत्व इह पाहि सोमं (*marutvatīyena graheṇa caraṃtīṃdra marutva iha pāhi somaṃ*) (Ā. 5-14). In the third paryāya, in the Hotṛ's śastra, the triplet इदं ह्यन्नोजसेति (*idaṃ hyannojaseti*) is the stotriya triplet; the sūtra says: इदं ह्यन्नोजसा महा इंद्रो य ओजसा (*idaṃ hyannojasā mahā iṃdro ya ojasā*) (Ā. 6-4).

##### Anuvāda

The sūkta beginning चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*) is the thirteenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has twelve Ṛks. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta and Indra the deity. The Anukramaṇikā says: चर्षणीधृतं द्वादशाद्यांत्यौ तृचौ जागतगायत्राविति (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ dvādaśādyāṃtyau tṛcau jāgatagāyatrāviti*). That is, the first three Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre; the last three are in the Gāyatrī metre; the remaining Ṛks are in the Triṣṭubh metre. The use of the sūkta is Laiṅgika. In the sacrifice called Ukthya, at the time of reciting the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra mantras, after the anurūpa Ṛks (a triplet) have been recited, the first three Ṛks of this sūkta are to be recited; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: चर्षणीधृतमस्तभ्नाद्यामसुर इति तृचौ (*carṣaṇīdhṛtamastabhnādyāmasura iti tṛcau*) (Ā. 6-1). In the Viṣuvat sacrifice, for the niṣkevalya śastra mantras, three Ṛks beginning नृणामु त्वा (*nṛṇāmu tvā*) (Ṛks 3-5 of this sūkta) are used; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the Khaṇḍa called Viṣuvān: नृणामु त्वा नृतमं गीर्भिरुक्कैरिति तिस्रः (*nṛṇāmu tvā nṛtamaṃ gīrbhirukkairiti tisraḥ*) (Ā. 8-6). In the sacrifice called Bṛhaspatisava also, the same three Ṛks beginning नृणामु त्वा (*nṛṇāmu tvā*) are to be used as nivid mantras at the time of reciting the niṣkevalya śastra mantras; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: नृणामु त्वेति मध्यंदिनः (*nṛṇāmu tveti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 9-5). In the Mahāvrata also these three Ṛks are recited for the niṣkevalya śastra mantras. In the sacrifice called Daśarātra, on the fourth day, for the Marutvatīya śastra mantras, three Ṛks of this sūkta beginning इंद्र मरुत्व (*iṃdra marutva*) (Ṛks 6-8 of this sūkta) are used; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra in the Khaṇḍa षष्ठेऽहनि षष्ठस्य (*ṣaṣṭhe 'hani ṣaṣṭhasya*) by the sūtra इंद्रमरुत्व इति तिस्त्र इति मरुत्वतीया (*iṃdramarutva iti tistra iti marutvatīyā*) (Ā. 8-1). In the Bṛhaspatisava also, the three Ṛks just mentioned are to be used as nivid mantras for the Marutvatīya śastra mantras; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: इंद्र मरुत्व इह नृणामु त्वेति मध्यंदिनः (*iṃdra marutva iha nṛṇāmu tveti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 9-5). The first Ṛk of this sūkta is to be recited as the puronuvākyā mantra of the Marutvatīya cup; the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra says: मरुत्वतीयेन ग्रहेण चरंतींद्र मरुत्व इह पाहि सोमं (*marutvatīyena graheṇa caraṃtīṃdra marutva iha pāhi somaṃ*)

which sūtra explains it (Ā. 5-14). Moreover, in the third paryāya, when the Hotṛ recites the śastra mantra, three Ṛks beginning इदं ह्यन्नोजसा (*idaṃ hyannojasā*) (Ṛks 10-12 of this sūkta) are to be recited as the stotriya triplet; this is explained by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra: इदं ह्यन्नोजसा महा इंड्रो य ओजसा (*idaṃ hyannojasā mahā iṃḍro ya ojasā*) (Ā. 6-4).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> बृहतीः प्रभूता गिरोऽस्मदीयाः स्तुतिलक्षणा वाचश्चर्यणेधृतं चर्षणीनां
> मनुष्याणामभिमतफलप्रदानेन धारकं पोषकं । यद्वा । आकृषंत्यनेन सर्वमिति
> चर्षन् बलं तद्वारकं । मघवानं धनवंतमुक्त्र्यमुक्त्यैः शस्त्रैः शंसनीयं वावृधानं बलधनादिसंपत्ता प्रतिक्षणं वर्धमानं पुरुहूतु स्तोतृभिर्बहुवारमाहूतममर्त्यं मरणधर्मरहितं सुवृक्तिभिः शोभनस्तुतिवाक्यर्दिवे प्रत्यहं जरमाणं स्तूयमानं तमिमदिंद्रमभ्यनूषत । अभितः सर्वतः स्तुवंतु ॥ बृहतीः ।
> ना छंदसीति सवर्णदीर्घः। अनूषत । णू स्तवने । अस्माल्लुजु सिच् । धातोः कुटादित्वात्सिजो जित्वेन गुणाभावः । सुवृक्तिभिः । नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदांतोदात्तत्वं।
> यद्वा ! सुवृक्तय इति स्तुतिकरणभूता ऋचो व्यक्तिशब्देनोच्यंते । क्तिच्क्त्य चेति
> क्तिच् । कृत्सरेणांतोदात्तः । दिवे दिवे । नित्यवीप्सयोरिति द्विर्वचनं । परस्याम्रेडितत्पादनुदात्तत्वे पूर्वपदस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*): abundant; गिरः (*giraḥ*): our words in the form of praise. They should praise this Indra on every side (अभ्यनूषत (*abhyanūṣata*)). Indra is चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*): the upholder, nourisher, of men (चर्षणीनां (*carṣaṇīnāṃ*)) by granting the fruit they desire. Or else: that by which everything is drawn is चर्षन् (*carṣan*), strength, and he is its holder. मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*): the wealthy; the ukthya: to be praised by ukthas, by śastras; वावृधानं (*vāvṛdhānaṃ*): increasing every moment through the wealth of strength, riches and the like; पुरुहूतं (*puruhūtaṃ*): called many times by the singers; अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*): free from the nature of death; सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*): with good words of praise; दिवे दिवे (*dive dive*): every day; जरमाणं (*jaramāṇaṃ*): being praised. अभितः (*abhitaḥ*) means on all sides; "let them praise". Or else: सुवृक्तय (*suvṛktaya*) are the Ṛks, the instruments of praise, which are called by the word vṛkti.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*)—the nourisher of men
- मघवानं (*maghavānaṃ*)—the wealthy
- उक्ष्यं (*ukṣyaṃ*)—the one praised by hymns in the form of ukṣa **NOTE**
- वावृधानं (*vāvṛdhānaṃ*)—the one who grows through wealth
- पुरुहूतं (*puruhūtaṃ*)—the one called by many
- अमर्त्यं (*amartyaṃ*)—the one free from the nature of death
- सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—with excellent words of praise
- दिवे दिवे (*dive dive*)—every day
- जरमाणं (*jaramāṇaṃ*)—the one who is praised
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—abundant
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—our words of praise
- अभ्यनूषत (*abhyanūṣata*)—let them praise fully.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May our abundant words of praise praise fully Indra, who nourishes men, is wealthy, is praised by hymns in the uktha form, grows through wealth, is called by many, is free from the nature of death, and is praised every day with excellent words of praise.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Let abundant praises celebrate Indra, the stay of man, the possessor of opulence, the adorable, prospering with increase, the invoked of many, the immortal, who is daily to be propitiated with sacred hymns.

### Printed p. 136

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*)—मनुष्याणामभिमतफलप्रदानेन धारकं पोषकं (*manuṣyāṇāmabhimataphalapradānena dhārakaṃ poṣakaṃ*). यद्वा अकृषंत्यनेन सर्वमिति चर्षणि बलं तद्धारकं (*yadvā akṛṣaṃtyanena sarvamiti carṣaṇi balaṃ taddhārakaṃ*). The word चर्षणी (*carṣaṇī*) is read among the names of man (Ni. 3-7). Because Indra gives and protects the fruits that correspond to the sacrifices and other rites performed by men, he is called चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*). Or else, since everything is drawn, the word चर्षणी (*carṣaṇī*) is understood to mean strength; Indra is praised as the one who holds such strength, that is, as mighty.

उक्थं (*ukthaṃ*)—उक्थैः शस्त्रैः शंसनीयं (*ukthaiḥ śastraiḥ śaṃsanīyaṃ*). Uktha means hymn. The sense is: Indra, who is praised both by hymns and by śastra mantras.

पुरुहूतं (*puruhūtaṃ*)—स्तोतृभिर्बहुवारमाहूतं (*stotṛbhirbahuvāramāhūtaṃ*). The one called many times by the people who sing hymns; or by many people, that is, the one invited by the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice, the priests, other singers and the like.

सुवृक्तिभिः (*suvṛktibhiḥ*)—स्तुतिकरणभूता ऋचो व्यक्तिशब्देनोच्यंते (*stutikaraṇabhūtā ṛco vyaktiśabdenocyaṃte*). Ṛks that are devoted to praise are named vyakti (vṛkti). For this word Yāska has given the explanation सुप्रवृत्ताभिः शोभनाभिः स्तुतिभिः (*supravṛttābhiḥ śobhanābhiḥ stutibhiḥ*) (Ni. 2-24): with excellent words of praise.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मे मदीया गिरः स्तुतिलक्षणा वाचः शतक्रतुं । शतं क्रतवो यज्ञा यस्य
> तं । अर्णवं पर्जन्यात्मनोदकवंतं शाकिनं । शक्नोत्येभिरिंद्र इति शाकाः सहायभूता मरुतः । तद्वंतं। नरं सर्वस्य जगतो नेतारं वाजसनिं वाजस्यान्नस्य दातारं
> पूर्भिदं शत्रुपुरां भेत्तारं तूर्णिं युद्धं प्रति शीघ्रं गंतारमप्पुरं मेघभेदनद्वारापां प्रेरकं धामसाचं तेजो भजमानं । यद्वा धनं धाम । तदर्थिभिः
> सह योजयितारं । अभिषाचं शत्रूणामभिभवितारं स्वर्विदं स्वर्गस्य लंभकं तमिमनिंद्रं विश्वतः सर्वत उप यंति । उपगच्छंतु ॥ अर्णवं । अर्णोऽस्यास्तीति
> मत्त्वर्थेऽर्णसः सलॊपश्चति वप्रत्ययः सकारलोपश्च । प्रत्ययस्वरः । नरं । नयतेर्डिच्चेत्कृप्रत्ययः । अमः सुप्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे प्रत्ययस्वरः । यंति । इण् गतावित्यस्य लटीणो यणिति यण् । निघातः । वाजसनिं । षणु दाने । खनिकष्यंज्यसिवसीत्यादिना इप्रत्ययः ; परादिष्पंदसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । तूर्णिं ।
> इत्वरा संभ्रमे । वहिश्रीत्यादिना निप्रत्ययः । ज्वरत्वरेत्यादिना ऊट् । निदित्यतिदेशादाद्युदात्तः । अप्पुरं । तुर त्वर्णे । क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । अभिषाचं । षच समवाये । ण्यंतस्य क्विप् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

मे मदीया गिरः (*me madīyā giraḥ*): my words in the form of praise should approach on every side (विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*), from all directions) this Indra (उप यंति (*upa yaṃti*): let them approach), who is: शतक्रतुं (*śatakratuṃ*), he of whom there are a hundred sacrifices (kratu); अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*), the possessor of water in the form of Parjanya; शाकिनं (*śākinaṃ*), he by whom Indra is able — the शाकाः (*śākāḥ*) are the Maruts, who are his helpers — the possessor of them; नरं (*naraṃ*), the leader of the whole world; वाजसनिं (*vājasaniṃ*), the giver of food (वाज (*vāja*)); पूर्भिदं (*pūrbhidaṃ*), the breaker of the cities of enemies; तूर्णिं (*tūrṇiṃ*), one who goes swiftly to battle; अप्पुरं (*appuraṃ*), the impeller of the waters by splitting the cloud; धामसाचं (*dhāmasācaṃ*), one who partakes of splendour; or else धाम (*dhāma*) is wealth, and he is the one who unites with those who desire it; अभिषाचं (*abhiṣācaṃ*), the overcomer of enemies; स्वर्विदं (*svarvidaṃ*), the obtainer of heaven.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मे (*me*)—my
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—words in the form of praise
- शतक्रतुं (*śatakratuṃ*)—the performer of many sacrifices
- अर्णवं (*arṇavaṃ*)—the one filled with water as Parjanya
- शाकिनं (*śākinaṃ*)—the one accompanied by the Maruts
- नरं (*naraṃ*)—the one who is the leader
- वाजसनिं (*vājasaniṃ*)—the giver of food
- पूर्विदं (*pūrvidaṃ*)—the destroyer of enemy cities
- तूर्णिं (*tūrṇiṃ*)—the one who runs toward battle
- अफ्पुरं (*aphpuraṃ*)—the one who pours down rain
- धामसाचं (*dhāmasācaṃ*)—the one endowed with splendour
- अभिषाचं (*abhiṣācaṃ*)—the conqueror of enemies
- स्वर्विदं (*svarvidaṃ*)—the one who brings heaven within reach; who is such
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—from all sides
- उप यंति (*upa yaṃti*)—let them approach and join.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May my words in the form of praise approach and join, from all sides, Indra, who is the performer of many sacrifices, filled with water as Parjanya, accompanied by the Maruts, the leader, the giver of food, the destroyer of enemy cities, who runs toward battle, pours down rain, is endowed with splendour, conquers enemies and brings heaven within reach.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
My praises constantly propitiate Indra, the object of many rites, the sender of rain attended by the Maruts, the leader (of all), the giver of food,

### Printed p. 138

the destroyer of cities, the swift (in combat), the prompt (dispenser) of waters, the distributors of riches, the subduer of foes, the conferrer of heaven.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

शतक्रतुं (*śatakratuṃ*)—शतं क्रतवो यज्ञा यस्य तं (*śataṃ kratavo yajñā yasya taṃ*). The commentator explains Indra as Śatakratu because he performed a hundred sacrifices. But this explanation follows a Purāṇic statement. Nowhere in the Vedas is it said that Indra performed a hundred sacrifices and so obtained the rank of Indra. If the word is explained in accordance with the Vedic sense, śata means "hundreds" or "many", and kratu means "deed" or "feat of daring"; Śatakratu then means one who has performed hundreds (many) of heroic deeds such as the slaying of Vṛtra. To explain it so is the proper course.

शाकिनं (*śākinaṃ*)—शक्नोत्येभिरिंद्र इति शाकाः सहायभूता मरुतः तद्वंतं (*śaknotyebhiriṃdra iti śākāḥ sahāyabhūtā marutaḥ tadvaṃtaṃ*). Because they help, the Maruts are called Śākāḥ. Indra, who has obtained the help of those Marut deities, is called Śākī.

पूर्भिदं (*pūrbhidaṃ*)—शुत्रपुरां भेत्तारं (*śutrapurāṃ bhettāraṃ*). The destroyer of enemy cities. Epithets such as पुरां भिंदुः (*purāṃ bhiṃduḥ*) describe Indra as the destroyer of enemy cities in many Ṛks.

धामसाचं (*dhāmasācaṃ*)—तेजो भजमानं । यद्वा धनं धाम । तदर्थिभिः सह योजयितारं (*tejo bhajamānaṃ | yadvā dhanaṃ dhāma | tadarthibhiḥ saha yojayitāraṃ*). The commentator gives two explanations: one who shines with splendour; or, if dhāma is taken to mean wealth, one who provides wealth to the people who praise him.

स्वर्विदं (*svarvidaṃ*)—स्वर्गस्य लंभकं (*svargasya laṃbhakaṃ*). One who obtains heaven, that is, one who goes to heaven, or dwells in heaven, or secures heaven for people.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जरिता शत्रूणां जरयितेंद्र आकरे । आकीर्यते यद्वार्थं धनमत्रेत्याकरो युद्धं । तस्मिन्वसोर्धनस्य स्थानभूते युद्धे पनस्यते । सर्वैः स्तूयते ।
> यद्वा वसोः । वसत्याभिमुख्येन तिष्ठतीति वसुः शत्रुस्तस्य जरयितेति योजनीयं ।
> स इंद्रोऽनेहसोऽपापाः स्तुभः स्तुतीर्दुवस्यति । परिचरति । तासां फलं प्रयच्छन् पूजयतीत्यर्थः । किंच स इंद्रो विवस्वतो विशेषेणाग्निहोत्रार्थं वसतो
> हविष्मतो ना यजमानस्य सदने गृह आ पिप्रिये हि । सोमपानादिनात्यंतं प्रीतो
> भवति खलु । सत्रासाहं शत्रूणामेव हंतारं यद्वा मरुद्भिः सह शत्रूणामभिभवितारं अत एवाभिमातिहनं शत्रूणां हंतारमिंद्रं स्तुहि । हे विश्वामित्रेति ॥ आकरे
> कृ विक्षेपे । अधिकरण यूदोरबित्यप् । थाथादिस्वरेणांतोदात्तः । जरिता । जृष्
> वयोहानानित्य स्यांतर्भावितण्यर्थस्य तृचि रूपं । चित्वादंतोदात्तः । पनस्यते ।
> पनस्यतिः स्तुतिकर्मा । तस्य कर्मणि लटि रूपं । निघातः । अनेहसः । हंतेर्नइ्युपपदे नञ हन एह चेत्यसिप्रत्यय एह इत्ययं चादेशो धातोः । नञ सुभ्यामिति
> स्वरेणांतोदात्तः । स्तुभः । स्तोभतिरर्चतिकर्मा । क्विप् । दुवस्यति । दुवः परिचरणमात्मन इच्छतीत्यर्थॆ क्यच् । निघातः । पिप्रिये । प्रीज् तर्पणी । लिट रूपं ।
> हियोगादनिघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Jaritā is Indra, who makes his enemies decay. आकरे (*ākare*): that in which wealth is scattered about (or for the sake of which it is gathered) is ākara, battle. In that battle, the place of wealth (vasu), he is praised (panasyate) by all. Or else vasoḥ: vasu is the enemy who stands facing him, and the sense is "the one who makes him decay". That Indra serves (duvasyati) the sinless praises (stubhaḥ): he honours them by granting their fruit. Further, Indra is greatly pleased at the house of the sacrificer (विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)), who dwells especially for the Agnihotra and has oblations, through Soma-drinking and the like. "Conqueror, slayer of enemies; or one who with the Maruts overcomes enemies; therefore the slayer of the foe: praise that Indra, O Viśvāmitra." The remainder is grammar on ākare, jaritā, panasyate, anehasaḥ, stubhaḥ, duvasyati and pipriye.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- जरिता (*jaritā*)—destroyer of enemies
- इंद्रः (*iṃdraḥ*)—Indra
- आकरे (*ākare*)—in battle
- वसोः (*vasoḥ*)—for the gaining of wealth
- पनस्यते (*panasyate*)—is praised (by all)
- अनेहसः (*anehasaḥ*)—sinless
- स्तुमः (*stumaḥ*)—praises **NOTE**
- दुवस्यति (*duvasyati*)—serves
- विवस्वतः (*vivasvataḥ*)—of the sacrificer
- सदने (*sadane*)—in the sacrificial house
- आ पिप्रिये (*ā pipriye*)—is satisfied with Soma and other drinks
- (O Viśvāmitra) सत्रासाहं (*satrāsāhaṃ*)—the conqueror of enemies
- अभिमातिहनं (*abhimātihanaṃ*)—the slayer of arrogant enemies, Indra
- स्तुहि (*stuhi*)—praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Indra, the destroyer of enemies, is praised by all in battle for the gaining of wealth. He serves the sinless praises. In the sacrificial houses of the sacrificer he is satisfied with Soma and other drinks. O Viśvāmitra, praise Indra, the conqueror of enemies and slayer of arrogant foes.

### Printed p. 140

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, the enfeebler (of adversaries), is praised as a mine of wealth; he is propitiated by righteous commendations; he is gratified in the dwelling of the offerer of oblations: glorify Indra, the conquerer, the destroyer of his enemies.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

आकरे एसोः (*ākare esoḥ*)—कृ विक्षेपे । आकीर्यते धनमत्रेत्याकरो युद्धं तस्मिन् (*kṛ vikṣepe | ākīryate dhanamatretyākaro yuddhaṃ tasmin*). The word ākara is derived from the root kṛ, meaning to scatter, to collect. Because in battle the victors collect the wealth of the defeated enemies, battle is called ākara, the commentator explains.

अनेहसः स्तुभ इंद्रो दुवस्यति (*anehasaḥ stubha iṃdro duvasyati*)—अपापाः स्तुतीः परिचरति । शासां फलं प्रयच्छन् पूजयतीत्यर्थः (*apāpāḥ stutīḥ paricarati | śāsāṃ phalaṃ prayacchan pūjayatītyarthaḥ*). People praise Indra with sinless praises; the sense is that Indra gives such people the fruit and honours them.

विवस्वतः सदने आ हि पिप्रिये (*vivasvataḥ sadane ā hi pipriye*) विशेषेणाग्निहोत्रार्थं वसतो हविष्मतो वा यजमानस्य गृहे सोमपानादिनात्यंतं प्रीतो भवति खलु (*viśeṣeṇāgnihotrārthaṃ vasato haviṣmato vā yajamānasya gṛhe somapānādinātyaṃtaṃ prīto bhavati khalu*). It is described here that in the house of sacrificers who dwell performing good rites such as the Agnihotra and stand ready to offer oblations, Indra is happy, drinking Soma.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the priests (sabādhaḥ: those who, by reciting the Rakṣoghna mantras, live with the harassment of the demons concerned) honour you, the foremost leader of men in his own work, the hero endowed with strength, with praises, the words that serve as means of praise, and with ukthas (śastras), facing you. Indra, of many exploits such as slaying Vṛtra, sets out for strength. Further, he, ancient and alone without helper, is lord of this nama, the food in the form of oblation; or else he is lord of this whole world, so homage to that Indra. The rest is grammar.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Indra) सबाधः (*sabādhaḥ*)—priests
- नृणां (*nṛṇāṃ*)—of all men
- नृतमं (*nṛtamaṃ*)—the pre-eminent leader
- वीरं (*vīraṃ*)—and endowed with strength
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with words in the form of praise
- उक्षैः (*ukṣaiḥ*)—with mantras in the form of śastras
- अभि (*abhi*)—sitting before you
- प्र अर्चत (*pra arcata*)—worship exceedingly
- पुरुमायः (*purumāyaḥ*)—Indra, the doer of many valorous deeds
- सहसे (*sahase*)—for the gaining of strength
- सं जिहीते (*saṃ jihīte*)—wishes to move about
- प्रदिवः (*pradivaḥ*)—the ancient
- एकः (*ekaḥ*)—the unaided Indra
- नमः अस्य (*namaḥ asya*)—for this food in the form of oblation
- ईशे (*īśe*)—desires

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the priests, sitting before you, worship exceedingly you, the pre-eminent leader of all men, endowed with strength, with words in the form of praise and mantras in the form of śastras. Indra, the doer of many valorous deeds, wishes to move about to gain strength. Indra, the ancient and unaided, desires this food in the form of oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
The priests glorify you, heroic leader of men, with praises and with prayers : Indra, the author of many delusions, exerts himself for (the acquirement of) strength : he from of old is the lord of this (oblation).

### Printed p. 142

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सबाधः (*sabādhaḥ*)—रक्षोघ्नमंत्रोच्चारणेन तद्विषयबाधया सह वर्तंत इति सबाध ऋत्विजः (*rakṣoghnamaṃtroccāraṇena tadviṣayabādhayā saha vartaṃta iti sabādha ṛtvijaḥ*). In sacrifices and the like, Rākṣasas and others cause obstacles. To remove them the priests recite Rakṣoghna mantras. Therefore priests accompanied by harassment from Rākṣasas are called sabādhaḥ; thus the component meaning of the word is explained. Yāska reads the word sabādhaḥ among the names of priests (Ni. 3-19).

पुरुमायः (*purumāyaḥ*)—वृत्रहननादिबहुकर्मा (*vṛtrahananādibahukarmā*). Because in the work of destroying enemies Indra displays many kinds of māyā (devices, stratagems) and daring, he is described as Purumāyaḥ, one who has done many daring deeds.

नमः अस्य प्रदिवः एकः ईशे (*namaḥ asya pradivaḥ ekaḥ īśe*)—पुरातनः असहायः स इंद्रो हविर्लक्षणस्यान्नस्य ईष्टे । यद्वा अस्य सर्वस्य जगत ईष्टे । तस्मा इंद्राय नमः (*purātanaḥ asahāyaḥ sa iṃdro havirlakṣaṇasyānnasya īṣṭe | yadvā asya sarvasya jagata īṣṭe | tasmā iṃdrāya namaḥ*). The commentator's explanation is that this sentence admits two meanings. If nama is taken to mean food (Ni. 3-9), then Indra, ancient and heroic without helper, is lord of the food in the form of oblation, that is, the oblation must be offered to Indra. If nama is taken to mean homage, then Indra is lord of this whole world, and homage is due to such an Indra.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मर्त्येषु मनुष्यस्येंद्रस्य निष्पिधोऽनुशासनानि पूर्विर्हितोपदेशादिभिः
> प्रभूतानि नानाप्रकाराणि भवंति । इंद्रस्य शासितृवे मंत्रः । उक्धमिंद्राय शंस्यं
> वर्धनं पुरुनिष्ठिधे । ऋग्वे. १-१०-५ । इति । तथा शासकाय तस्मा इंद्राय पृथिवी
> पुरु पुरूणि बहूनि वसूनि धनानि बिभर्ति । अंतर्धारयति । किंच द्यावो द्युलोका
> ओषधीरोषधय उत अपि चापो जलानि जीरयः । जीय्यंत इति जीरयो
> मनुष्याः । वनानि वृक्षाश्च एते सर्व इंद्रस्याज्ञया तदुपभोगयोग्यं रयिं धनं
> रक्षंति ॥ निष्पिधः । षिधु गत्यां । क्विप् । संहितायां निसः सकारेणेणो व्यवधानं
> छांदसत्वादनादृत्योपसर्गात्सुनोतीत्यादिना षत्वं । निसः सकारस्य ष्टुना ष्टुरिति
> षत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Among mortals, the injunctions (niṣpidhaḥ) of Indra are many and of various kinds, through beneficial teachings and the like. A mantra on Indra as ruler: उक्धमिंद्राय शंस्यं वर्धनं पुरुनिष्ठिधे (*ukdhamiṃdrāya śaṃsyaṃ vardhanaṃ puruniṣṭhidhe*) (Ṛg. 1-10-5). Likewise the earth holds many treasures within for that ruling Indra. Further, the heavens, the plants, the waters, the jīrayaḥ (men, who are worn out) and the forests (trees): all these, by Indra's command, guard the wealth fit for his enjoyment. The rest is grammar on niṣpidhaḥ.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मर्त्येषु (*martyeṣu*)—among men
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Indra
- निषिधः (*niṣidhaḥ*)—teachings in the form of grace
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—are many
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for this Indra, the teacher
- पृथिवी (*pṛthivī*)—the earth
- पुरु (*puru*)—many
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—treasures
- भिभर्ति (*bhibharti*)—holds
- द्यावः (*dyāvaḥ*)—the heavens
- ओषधीः (*oṣadhīḥ*)—the plants
- उत (*uta*)—and
- आपः (*āpaḥ*)—the waters
- जीरयः (*jīrayaḥ*)—men
- वनानि (*vanāni*)—trees
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- रक्षंति (*rakṣaṃti*)—guard

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The teachings of this Indra, in the form of grace, are many among men. For this Indra, the teacher, the earth holds many treasures. The heavens, the plants, the waters, men and the trees also keep wealth guarded for him.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Many are his prohibitions (against evil enjoined) to men : many are the treasures that the earth enshrines : for Indra the heavens, the plants, the waters, men and priests, preserve their riches.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पूर्वीः अस्य निष्पिधः मर्त्येषु (*pūrvīḥ asya niṣpidhaḥ martyeṣu*)- अनुशासनानि हितोपदेशादिभिः नानाप्रकाराणि भवंति (*anuśāsanāni hitopadeśādibhiḥ nānāprakārāṇi bhavaṃti*). Indra's injunctions or rules are many with regard to men, in the form of beneficial teaching. Here the commentator explains the word niṣpidhaḥ as injunctions, rules; that is, to punish and restrain the wicked is called anuśāsana. With this meaning—

### Printed p. 144

[The sentence continues from the previous page:] The commentator cites as an example the Ṛk

उक्कमिंद्राय शंस्यं वर्धनं पुरुनिष्पिधे । (*ukkamiṃdrāya śaṃsyaṃ vardhanaṃ puruniṣpidhe |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-10-5).

For the word पुरुनिष्पिधे (*puruniṣpidhe*) in this Ṛk he explains बहूनां शत्रूणां निषेधकारिणे (*bahūnāṃ śatrūṇāṃ niṣedhakāriṇe*), that is, "to him who defeats many enemies and keeps them under restraint". It is therefore indicated that the ordinances called niṣpidha, namely the punishing of the wicked and the protecting of the good, are carried out by Indra.

पुरु वसूनि (*puru vasūni*) …… वनानि (*vanāni*)—In accordance with the command of such a supremely glorious Indra, the earth bears wealth of many kinds in the form of plants and the like; the heaven, the herbs, the waters and the trees all guard, by Indra's command, the wealth in each of them, that is, the essential, excellent things, for Indra's enjoyment. This is the main purport of the Ṛk.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे हरिवोऽश्ववन्निंद्र तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राणि तथा तुभ्यं गिरः
> शास्त्राणि च सत्ता सत्यमेव दधिरे । ऋत्विजो धारयंति । तानि जुषस्व । सेवस्व । हे
> वसो सर्वस्य वासयितः सखे सखिभूत हे इंद्र आपिर्वाप्तस्त्वं नूतनस्य नवतरमवसोऽन्नलक्षणं हविर्भोधि । त्वदर्थं दीयमानं जानीहि । आतस्त्वं जरितृभ्यः
> स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यं वयोऽन्नं धाः । देहि ॥ तुभ्यं । जयि चेत्याद्युदात्तत्वं। जुषस्व।
> जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोरित्यस्य लोटि रूपं । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः । बोधि । बुध अवगमन इत्यस्य लोटि वा छंदसीति हेर्विकल्पेन जित्वादत्र पित्त्वाद्गुणः । हुझल्फो
> हेर्धिरिति ध्यादेशः । जित्वादंतोदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, हरिवः (*harivaḥ*), possessor of horses: for you the Brahmans (stotras, hymns of praise) and for you the "gir" (śāstras, recitations) the priests truly hold up; enjoy them, accept them. O वसो (*vaso*), he who causes all to dwell, O friend, O Indra, who are all-pervading: know that the newest food, the oblation in the form of अवसः (*avasaḥ*) (food), is being given for you. Therefore give food to us, the singers who praise you. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरिवे (*harive*)—O one yoked with horses
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you alone
- ब्रह्माणि (*brahmāṇi*)—the hymns of praise
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you alone
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—the śastra-mantras
- सत्रा (*satrā*)—truly
- दधिरे (*dadhire*)—(the priests) have held
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—(them) enjoy
- वसो (*vaso*)—O maker of dwelling-places
- सखी (*sakhī*)—O Indra, who are a friend
- आपि (*āpi*)—you, who are all-pervading
- नूतनस्य (*nūtanasya*)—(though) new
- अवसः (*avasaḥ*)—the food, which is in the form of oblation
- बोधि (*bodhi*)—know
- जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*)—to us, the praisers
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—food
- धाः (*dhāḥ*)—give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, yoked with horses, the priests have held up hymns of praise and śastra-mantras for you alone. Enjoy them. O Indra, maker of dwelling-places and friend, you who are all-pervading, know the food, new and in the form of oblation, accept it, and give us, who praise you, the food that we desire.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
To you, Indra, (the pious) address prayers, and praises, and sacrifi-
ces : accept them, lord of horses : giver of dwellings, friend (of man), you
are the pervader (of all things), partake of this present oblations, and grant
food to the worshippers.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हरिव: (*hariva:*)—अश्ववन्निंद्र । (*aśvavanniṃdra |*) Indra's horses are named "Hari" (Ni. 2-28). Indra is addressed by the word हरिवः (*harivaḥ*) as "O Indra, possessor of such horses".

तुभ्यं ब्रह्माणि तुभ्यं गिरः सत्रा दधिरे जुषस्व (*tubhyaṃ brahmāṇi tubhyaṃ giraḥ satrā dadhire juṣasva*)—O Indra, the priests are reciting hymns of praise and words of praise for you. "Enjoy it" means "hear it and be pleased"; this is the main purport. Here the word तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*) is recited twice in order to indicate the great affection of the worshipper for Indra.

सखे वसो आपि नूतनस्य अवसः बोधि (*sakhe vaso āpi nūtanasya avasaḥ bodhi*)—सर्वस्य वासयितः सखिभूत हे इंद्र व्याप्तस्तं नूतनस्य अन्नलक्षणं हविः त्वदर्थं दीयमानं जानीहि । (*sarvasya vāsayitaḥ sakhibhūta he iṃdra vyāptastaṃ nūtanasya annalakṣaṇaṃ haviḥ tvadarthaṃ dīyamānaṃ jānīhi |*) O Indra, who provide a dwelling-place for all and are beneficent like a friend, you who are all-pervading, know that the oblation in the form of food, newly prepared by us just now to be offered to you, is made ready for you alone.

### Printed p. 146

जरितृभ्यः वयः धाः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ vayaḥ dhāḥ*)—स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यमन्नं वेहि । (*stotṛbhyo 'smabhyamannaṃ vehi |*) Favour us, who sing praise, by giving अत्मनन्नु (*atmanannu*). **NOTE** The words अवः (*avaḥ*) and वयः (*vayaḥ*) are read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9).

> आ स्मा रथं वृषपाणेषु तिष्ठसि शार्यातस्य प्रकृता येषु मंदसे । ऋग्वे. १-५१-१२
> । इति । हे शूरेंद्र तव संबंधिनि शर्मन् शर्मणि निर्बाधस्थाने स्थिताः सुयज्ञाः
> सुष्टु कृतयज्ञाः कवयो मेधाविनो यजमानाः प्रणीती तव हविषां प्रणयनेन
> प्रापणेन आ समंताद्विवासंति । त्वामेव परिचरंति । विवासतिः परिचरणकर्मा ॥
> शार्यते । शर्यातेरयमित्यर्थे तस्येदमित्यण् प्रत्ययः । अपिबः । यथायोगादनिघातः । अडागमस्वरः । प्रणीती । नयतेभार्वॆ क्तिन् । तादौ च निति कृतीति गतेः
> प्रकृतिश्वरत्वं । सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयायाः सवर्णदीर्घः । उपसर्गादसमासेऽपि
> णत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O मरुत्वः (*marutvaḥ*), Indra accompanied by the Maruts, come to this our sacrifice and drink the soma; as you formerly drank the pressed soma when Śāryāta, the son of Śaryāti, was performing a sacrifice, so drink here also. That Indra drank the soma-juices at Śāryāta's sacrifice is stated clearly in the Kauṣītaki; and there is a mantra text to the same effect: आ स्मा रथं वृषपाणेषु तिष्ठसि शार्यातस्य प्रकृता येषु मंदसे । (*ā smā rathaṃ vṛṣapāṇeṣu tiṣṭhasi śāryātasya prakṛtā yeṣu maṃdase |*) (Ṛgve. 1-51-12) **NOTE**. O hero Indra, the wise sacrificers who have performed their sacrifice well, abiding in your own shelter, a place free of obstruction, serve you all around by bringing you the oblations; they attend on you alone. विवासति (*vivāsati*) is a word of the sense of attendance.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदुत्वः (*madutvaḥ*)—accompanied by the Maruts
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यथा (*yathā*)—in the way in which
- शार्यते (*śāryate*)—at the sacrifice of the son of Śaryāta **NOTE**
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—the pressed soma
- अपिबः (*apibaḥ*)—you drank, even so
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrificial rite
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the soma-juice
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

### Printed p. 147

- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- तव (*tava*)—pertaining to your worship
- शर्मन् (*śarman*)—those engaged in the rites
- सुयज्ञाः (*suyajñāḥ*)—excellent sacrificers
- कवयः (*kavayaḥ*)—wise sacrificers
- तव (*tava*)—to you
- प्रणीती (*praṇītī*)—by offering the oblation
- आ विवासंति (*ā vivāsaṃti*)—they worship (you) all around

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, as you formerly drank the pressed soma-juice at the sacrifice of Śaryāta's son, so drink at this sacrificial rite also the soma that is offered. O valiant Indra, the sacrificers, who are engaged in the rites that are the object of your worship, who are excellent performers of sacrifice and wise, serve you all around by offering the oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the soma at this ceremony as you have drunk of the libation of the son of Sharyati : your far-seeing and devout worshippers, being in security, adore you through their offerings

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मरुत्वः (*marutvaḥ*)—मरुद्भिस्तद्वन् । (*marudbhistadvan |*) The meaning is "O Indra, together with the Marut deities". Here Indra is prayed to come with the Marut deities to our sacrificial ground and drink the soma.

यथा शार्याते अपिबः सुतस्य (*yathā śāryāte apibaḥ sutasya*)—O Indra, as you formerly came to the sacrifice performed by the son of one named Śaryāti and drank soma, so come to our sacrificial ground also and drink the soma; thus the seer prays. The commentator says that the matter of Indra's drinking soma at the sacrifice of Śaryāti's son is stated clearly in the Kauṣītakī Brāhmaṇa, and as an example he gives the Ṛk that mentions this matter in the Ṛgveda also:

आ स्मा रथं वृषपाणेषु तिष्ठसि शार्यातस्य प्रभृता येषु मंदसे । (*ā smā rathaṃ vṛṣapāṇeṣu tiṣṭhasi śāryātasya prabhṛtā yeṣu maṃdase |*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-12).

Śaryāti was a royal seer. His son is customarily called Śāryāta. Formerly, when this Śāryāta performed a sacrifice, the great sage Cyavana, born in the Bhṛgu lineage, gave the share of the oblation first to the Aśvin deities. Indra then became greatly angry. Śāryāta, knowing this, praised Indra in various ways and pleased him, prepared the soma-juice by the rites of pressing and the like, and offered that purified soma to Indra.

### Printed p. 148

Indra, satisfied, drank the soma-juice to his heart's content at Śāryāta's sacrifice; so runs the legend. The seer describes that very thing here. The name of this Śāryāta is indicated in the present Ṛk, in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-51-12, in Ai. Brā. 4-32-7, Śa. Brā. 4-1-5-1, the Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa 3-121 and other places.

#### Ṛk 8

> स वा॑वशा॒न इ॒ह पा॑हि॒ सोमं॑ म॒रुद्भि॑रिंद्र॒ सखि॑भिः सु॒तं नः॑ ।  
> जा॒तं यत्त्वा॒ परि॑ दे॒वा अभू॑षन्म॒हे भरा॑य पुरुहूत॒  ॑
> विश्वे ॥ ८ ॥

> *sa vāvaśāna iha pāhi somaṃ marudbhiriṃdra sakhibhiḥ sutaṃ naḥ |*  
> *jātaṃ yattvā pari devā abhūṣanmahe bharāya puruhūta*  
> *viśve ‖ 8 ‖*

> जातं । यत् । त्वा । परि । देवाः । अभूषन् । महे । भराय । पुरुहूत । विश्वे ॥

> *saḥ | vāvaśānaḥ | iha | pāhi | somaṃ | marutbhiḥ | iṃdra | sakhibhiḥ | sutaṃ | naḥ |*  
> *jātaṃ | yat | tvā | pari | devāḥ | abhūṣan | mahe | bharāya | puruhūta | viśve ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वावशानः सोमं कामयमानः स तादृशस्त्वं सखिभिः समानख्यानैर्मरुद्भिः सह नोऽस्मत्संबंधिनीहास्मिन्यज्ञे सुतमभिषुतं सोमं पाहि । पिब ।
> हे पुरुहूत पुरुभिराहूतेंद्र जातं पानेन प्रबलं संपन्नं यत् यं त्वां विश्वे
> सर्वॆ देवा महे महते भराय । ह्रियंते योधानामायुंष्यत्रेति भरः
> संग्रामः । तस्मै संग्रामाय पर्यभूषन् । सर्वतोऽलमकुर्वन् ॥ वावशानः ।
> वशेर्यज् लुकि चानशि रूपं । चित्तादंतोदात्तः । अभूषन् । भूष अलंकारे ।
> भूवादिः । लजि रूपं । यद्योगादनिघातः । भराय । हृञ् हरणे। अधिकरणे घः ।
> हृग्रहोर्भश्चंदसीति हकारस्य भकारः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*), desirous of soma: such as you are, with the Maruts, who are your friends, of the same name, drink the soma pressed for us here, at this our sacrifice. O पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*), invoked by many, Indra, born, made strong and complete by drinking: you whom all the gods equipped for the great भराय (*bharāya*). भरः (*bharaḥ*) is battle, because the lives of warriors are carried off in it (ह्रियंते योधानामायुंष्यत्रेति (*hriyaṃte yodhānāmāyuṃṣyatreti*)); for that battle they adorned you on all sides.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—O one invoked by many
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- जातं (*jātaṃ*)—you who, drinking soma as soon as you were born, became full of strength
- यत् त्वा (*yat tvā*)—whom you
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods

### Printed p. 149

- महे (*mahe*)—great
- भराय (*bharāya*)—for the work of battle
- परि अभूषन् (*pari abhūṣan*)—made ready
- स (*sa*)—such as you are
- वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*)—desirous of drinking soma
- सखिभिः (*sakhibhiḥ*)—your friends
- मरुद्भिः (*marudbhiḥ*)—with the Maruts
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrifice
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—soma
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, invoked by many, whom all the gods made ready for the great work of battle, you who became full of strength by drinking soma as soon as you were born: such as you are, desirous of drinking soma, drink together with the Maruts, your friends, the soma pressed at this our sacrifice.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, yoo are gratified by the beverage, drink the Soma that has been effused by us, together with your friends, the Maruts, at this ceremony: you who are invoked of many, and whom all the gods equipped as soon as born for the great battle (with the Asuras).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the seer describes that Indra is requested to come to the sacrificial ground with his friends, the Marut deities, and drink soma, and that all the gods served Indra, made strong by that soma-drinking, in order to win victory in battle.

The eternal companionship and friendship of Indra and the Maruts, the relation of king and subjects between them, the offering of oblations in the principal sacrificial acts to Indra accompanied by the Maruts, and the help the Maruts gave Indra when he fought with the demon Vṛtra are praised in many places in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. A legend telling how Indra, joining the Maruts, stood apart from the other gods is told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa **NOTE**. Besides, it is said in many places that Indra is the king and the Maruts the subjects. It is also indicated that Indra's valour increased through the help of the Maruts. Because of such a close relation and companionship, the custom of offering oblations addressed to Indra and the Maruts together is seen in the Śrutis.

स नो मरुद्भिर्वृषभ श्रवो धा उग्र उग्रेभिः स्थविरः सहोदाः । (*sa no marudbhirvṛṣabha śravo dhā ugra ugrebhiḥ sthaviraḥ sahodāḥ |*)
(Ya Saṃ. 1-171-5) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 150

…in ṛks such as this there is, for Indra and the Maruts together, a joint invocation and an offering of the oblation.

And in the Bṛhaddevatā as well: मरुद्भिः सह यत्रेंद्रो मरुत्वांस्तत्र सोऽभवत् । (*marudbhiḥ saha yatreṃdro marutvāṃstatra so 'bhavat |*) (Bṛ. De. 4-56). This gives an account of the companionship of Indra and the Maruts.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तेभिः॑ सा॒कं पि॑बतु वृत्रखा॒दः सु॒तं सोमं॑ दा॒शुषः॒ स्वे  ॒॑
> सधस्थे ॥ ९ ॥

> *apūrye maruta āpireṣo 'maṃdanniṃdramanu dātivārāḥ |*  
> *tebhiḥ sākaṃ pibatu vṛtrakhādaḥ sutaṃ somaṃ dāśuṣaḥ sve*  
> *sadhasthe ‖ 9 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्त्तूर्ये । मरुतः । अपिः । एषः । अमंदन् । इंद्रं । अनु । दाशिवाराः ।  
> तेभिः साकं । पिबतु । वृत्रखादः । सुतं । सोमं । दाशुषः । स्वे । सधस्थे ॥ ९ ॥

> *asttūrye | marutaḥ | apiḥ | eṣaḥ | amaṃdan | iṃdraṃ | anu | dāśivārāḥ |*  
> *tebhiḥ sākaṃ | pibatu | vṛtrakhādaḥ | sutaṃ | somaṃ | dāśuṣaḥ | sve | sadhasthe ‖ 9 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मरुतो य एष इंद्रोऽपूर्येऽपां प्रेरण आपिर्युष्माकं सखा
> सन् वर्तते दाशिवाराः । वारो वरणेयं बलं धनं वा । दत्तबला दत्तधना वा ते
> मरुतस्तमिंद्रमन्वमंदन् । अहृष्यन् । वृत्रखादो वृत्रस्य हिंसकः स इंद्रस्तेभिस्मैर्मरुद्धिः साकं दाशुषो हविर्दत्तवतो यजमानस्य स्वे स्वकीये सधस्थे । सह
> तिष्ठंत्यस्मिन्निति सधस्थं गृहं । तस्मिन् सुतमभिषुतं सोमं पिबतु ॥ अपूर्ये ।
> तूरी त्वराहिंसयोरित्यस्मादघ्न्यादयश्चेति यत्पत्ययः । यतोऽनाव इत्याद्युदात्तः । समासे कृदुत्तरपदस्वरः । अमंदन् । मदि स्तुत्यादिषु । परस्मैपदी ।
> पादादित्वादनिघातः । वृत्रखादः । खादृ भक्षणे । कर्मण्यण् । दाशुषः । दाश्व दान
> इत्यस्य क्वसौ दाश्वान्साह्वान्निढ्वांश्चेति द्विर्वचनाद्यभावः । वसोः संप्रसारणं ।
> प्रत्ययस्वरः । सधस्थे । सध मादस्थयोशृंदसीति सहस्य सधादेशः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Maruts, this Indra who is your friend (āpi) in the apūrya, the sending forth of the waters, was gladdened after by those Maruts who are दाशिवाराः (*dāśivārāḥ*)." Vāra means choice, strength or wealth; so the dāśivārāḥ are those who have given strength or given wealth. The Maruts gladdened that Indra. Vṛtrakhāda is the slayer of Vṛtra. Let that Indra, together with those Maruts, drink the soma pressed in the own abode (sadhastha) of the sacrificer who has given the oblation. A sadhastha is a house, since people stand together (saha tiṣṭhanti) in it. The remainder of the block is grammar.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—O Maruts
- एषः (*eṣaḥ*)—this Indra
- अप्त्यो (*aptyo*)—at the time of pouring rain
- आपि (*āpi*)—is your friend
- दातिवाराः (*dātivārāḥ*)—(to him) those Maruts, the providers of strength

### Printed p. 151

- इंद्रं अनु (*iṃdraṃ anu*)—to Indra
- अमंदन् (*amaṃdan*)—became givers of delight
- वृत्रखादः (*vṛtrakhādaḥ*)—Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra
- तेभिः साकं (*tebhiḥ sākaṃ*)—together with those Maruts
- दाशुषः (*dāśuṣaḥ*)—of the sacrificer who offers the oblation
- स्वे सधस्थे (*sve sadhasthe*)—in his own sacrificial house
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the soma
- पिबतु (*pibatu*)—let him drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, this Indra is your friend at the time of pouring rain. Those Maruts, the providers of strength to him, became givers of delight to Indra. Let Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, together with those Maruts, drink the soma pressed in the own sacrificial house of the sacrificer who offers the oblation.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Maruts, this is your friend for sending of the waters: they (the Maruts), the givers of strength, have yielded Indra gratification: may the devourer of Vritra drink with them the libation offered by the worshipper in his own abode.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The friendly feeling and companionship of Indra and the Maruts were already subtly set out in the preceding ṛk. This ṛk tells that Indra helps the Marut deities even in the pouring of rain. The help rendered to the Maruts is this: Indra strikes with the thunderbolt the demon Vṛtra, who has held back the rain from falling, and so assists the pouring of the rain. The seer prays that Indra come with such Marut deities and drink soma in the sacrificial house of the sacrificer.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे राधानां पते धनानां स्वामिन् गिर्वणो गीर्भिः स्तुतिभिर्वननीय हे
> इंद्र इदमनु अनेनानुक्रमेण । उद्देशानुक्रमेणेत्यर्थः । ओजसा बलेन ग्रावभिः
> सुतमभिषुतं सोमं तु क्षिप्रं पिब हि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O lord of riches (rādhas), O Indra, who art to be won (vananīya) by songs (gīrbhiḥ), i.e. by praises: इदमनु (*idamanu*) means 'in this sequence', that is, in the sequence of the purpose. With strength (ojas), i.e. with the pressing-stones, drink quickly this soma that has been pressed."

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- राधानां (*rādhānāṃ*)—of riches
- पते (*pate*)—O lord
- गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—O Indra, who art praised with songs
- इदं अनु (*idaṃ anu*)—in sequence of the purpose
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—with the powerful stones
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—crushed and pressed
- अस्य (*asya*)—this soma
- तु (*tu*)—quickly
- पिब हि (*piba hi*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, lord of riches, praised with songs: in the sequence of the purpose, drink quickly this soma pressed with the powerful stones.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Lord of riches, entitled to praise, this libation has been effused agreeably to (our) strength : drink of it quickly.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

गिर्वणः (*girvaṇaḥ*)—गीर्भिर्वननीयः (*gīrbhirvananīyaḥ*). He who is approached with words of praise; that is, when he is invoked with hymns and the like, Indra comes to the sacrificial ground to favour them and drinks the soma. This is the meaning.

ओजसा सुतं (*ojasā sutaṃ*)—बलेन ग्रावभिः अभिषुतं सोमं (*balena grāvabhiḥ abhiṣutaṃ somaṃ*). Since, when the soma plants are crushed with stones to take out the juice, they have to be crushed with the application of force, the expression ओजसा सुतं (*ojasā sutaṃ*) is appropriate.

> यस्ते॒ अनु॑ स्व॒धामस॑त्सु॒ते नि य॑च्छ त॒न्वं॑ ।  
> स त्वा॑ ममत्तु सो॒म्यं ॥ ११ ॥

> *yaste anu svadhāmasatsute ni yaccha tanvaṃ |*  
> *sa tvā mamattu somyaṃ ‖ 11 ‖*

> सः । त्वा । ममत्तु । सोम्यं ॥ ११ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र त्वदर्थं यः सोमः स्वधामन्नमनु अनुसृत्य ग्रावभिरभिषुतोऽसत् सुते तस्मिन् सोमे तन्नं स्वकीयं शरीरं नि यच्छ । प्रेरय । स सोमः
> सोम्यं सोमार्हं त्वा त्वां ममत्तु । मादयातु ॥ असत् । अस्तेर्लेट्यडागमे
> रूपं । यद्वत्तयोगादनिघातः । आगमस्यानुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, the soma that, for thee, has been pressed with the stones in accordance with svadhā (food) — in that pressed soma नि यच्छ (*ni yaccha*) thy own body, that is, direct it. Let that soma gladden thee, who art worthy of soma." The rest of the block is grammar.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- ते (*te*)—for thee
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the soma which
- स्वधां अनु (*svadhāṃ anu*)—pressed in accordance with the contest
- असत् (*asat*)—is ready
- सुते (*sute*)—in this pressed soma
- तन्नं (*tannaṃ*)—thy body
- नि यच्छ (*ni yaccha*)—rouse up
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same soma
- सोम्यं (*somyaṃ*)—worthy of the soma-drink
- त्वा (*tvā*)—thee
- ममत्तु (*mamattu*)—let it gladden

**NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, the soma that has been pressed for thee in accordance with the contest and made ready: in this pressed, ready soma rouse up thy body. Let that same soma gladden thee, who art worthy of the soma-drink.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Invigorate your body with the soma that has been poured out as food for you: may it exhilarate you, delighting in the Soma draught.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

स्वधां अनु (*svadhāṃ anu*)—The word svadhā is read among the names of food. The meaning is: O Indra, the soma juice that is fit to be consumed, standing in the place of food, as food for thee. Or else it may be understood that after the eating of food and the like, this soma juice has been prepared for drinking.

सुते नि यच्छ तन्वं (*sute ni yaccha tanvaṃ*)—When the soma juice is ready, direct thy body; that is, make thyself ready for drinking soma, or resolve to do so.

### Printed p. 154

The seer prays that this soma juice that we have prepared may gladden thee, who art worthy of the soma-drink.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रते॑ अश्नोतु कु॒क्ष्योः प्रेंद्र॒ ब्रह्म॑णा॒ शिरः॑ ।  
> प्र बा॒हू शू॑र॒ राध॑से ॥ १२ ॥

> *prate aśnotu kukṣyoḥ preṃdra brahmaṇā śiraḥ |*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । ते । अश्नोतु । कुक्ष्योः । प्र । इंद्र । ब्रह्मणा । शिरः ।  
> प्र । बार इति । शूर । राधसे ॥ १२ ॥

> *pra | te | aśnotu | kukṣyoḥ | pra | iṃdra | brahmaṇā | śiraḥ |*  
> *pra | bāra iti | śūra | rādhase ‖ 12 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र स सोमस्ते तव कुक्षोः कुक्षेरुभयोः पार्श्वयोरुभौ पार्श्वा
> प्राश्नोतु । प्रकर्षण व्याप्नोति । तथा ब्रह्मणा स्तोत्रेण सहितः स सोमः शिरः
> शरीरं अवयवादिनावयवी लक्ष्यते । त्वच्छरीरं प्राश्नोतु । हे शूर इंद्र राधसे
> धनाय तव बाहू अपि प्राश्नोतु ॥ अश्नोतु । अशू व्याप्तावित्यस्य लोटि व्यत्ययेन
> परस्मैपदं । निघातः । कुक्षोः । उदात्तयणो हल्पूर्वादिति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Indra, let that soma pervade thy two sides of the belly (kukṣi), i.e. both flanks. Likewise let that soma, together with the brahman, i.e. the praise-song, pervade thy head (śiras); by the part the whole is indicated, so: let it pervade thy body. O hero Indra, for wealth (rādhas) let it pervade also thy arms." The rest of the block is grammar.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same soma
- ते (*te*)—thy
- कुक्षोः (*kukṣoḥ*)—in both sides of the belly
- प्र अश्नोतु (*pra aśnotu*)—let it pervade fully
- ब्रह्मणा (*brahmaṇā*)—that soma accompanied by praise
- शिरः (*śiraḥ*)—thy body
- प्र (*pra*)—let it pervade fully
- शूर (*śūra*)—O valiant Indra
- राधसे (*rādhase*)—for the gain of wealth
- बाहू (*bāhū*)—in thy arms
- प्र (अश्नोतु) (*pra (aśnotu)*)—let it pervade fully

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, let the soma offered to thee pervade fully both sides of thy belly, thy head, thy arms, and also thy whole body, for the gain of wealth for us.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May this libation, Indra, penetrate to your flanks ; may it, (aided) by prayer, reach your head; may it spread, hero, through your arms, (that they may distribute) wealth.

### Printed p. 155

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this ṛk the seer expresses the wish: let the soma juice that we have prepared pervade well both parts of Indra's belly and the other parts of his body, especially the head and the arms, and cause him delight; and let Indra, delighted by that soma-drinking, bring us gain of wealth.

## Sūkta 52 (Maṇḍala 3)
**NOTE**

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धानावंतमित्यष्टर्चं चतुर्दशं सूक्तं वैश्वामित्रम्यंद्रं । अत्रेयमनुक्रमणिका । धानावंतमष्टौ पूर्वार्धं गायत्रं षष्ठी जगतीति । आदितश्चतुस्रो
> गायत्र स्तृतीये धाना इति षष्ठी जगती शिष्टास्त्रिष्टुभः ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लिंगादवगंतव्यः । प्रातःसवनीयपुरोडाशस्यानुवाक्या धानावंतमित्याद्या । सूत्रितं
> च । धानावंतं करंभिणमिति प्रातःसवनेऽनुवाक्या । आ. ५-४ । इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*) has eight ṛks and is the fourteenth sūkta; its seer is Viśvāmitra and its deity Indra. The Anukramaṇikā here: धानावंतमष्टौ पूर्वार्धं गायत्रं षष्ठी जगती (*dhānāvaṃtamaṣṭau pūrvārdhaṃ gāyatraṃ ṣaṣṭhī jagatī*). Explained: the first four ṛks are gāyatrī; the sixth, तृतीये धानाः (*tṛtīye dhānāḥ*), is jagatī; the remaining ones are triṣṭubh. The use (viniyoga) of the sūkta is to be learnt from the indication (liṅga) of the ṛks. The first ṛk, धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*), is the anuvākyā of the puroḍāśa of the morning pressing. It is also stated in the sūtra: धानावंतं करंभिणमिति प्रातःसवनेऽनुवाक्या (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ karaṃbhiṇamiti prātaḥsavane 'nuvākyā*) (Ā. 5-4).

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*) is the fourteenth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. Viśvāmitra is the seer of this sūkta; Indra is the deity. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: धानावंतमष्टौ पूर्वार्धं गायत्रं षष्ठी जगती (*dhānāvaṃtamaṣṭau pūrvārdhaṃ gāyatraṃ ṣaṣṭhī jagatī*). The first four ṛks of this sūkta are in the gāyatrī metre; the sixth ṛk, तृतीये धानाः (*tṛtīye dhānāḥ*), is in the jagatī metre; the remaining three ṛks are in triṣṭubh metre. The use of the sūkta follows the meaning of the several ṛks. The first ṛk of this sūkta, धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*), is to be used as the anuvākyā mantra in the puroḍāśa oblation connected with the morning pressing; this is set forth by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra धानावंतं करंभिणमिति प्रातस्सवनेऽनुवाक्या (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ karaṃbhiṇamiti prātassavane 'nuvākyā*) (Ā. 5-4).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> धा॒ना॑नंतं करं॒भिण॑मपू॒पवं॑तमु॒क्थिन॑म् ।  
> इंद्र॑ प्रा॒तर्जु॑षस्व नः ॥ १ ॥

> *dhānānaṃtaṃ karaṃbhiṇamapūpavaṃtamukthinam |*  
> *iṃdra prātarjuṣasva naḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> धानावंतं । करंभिणं । अपूपवंतं । उक्किनं ।  
> इंद्र । प्रातः । जुषस्व । नः ॥ १ ॥

> *dhānāvaṃtaṃ | karaṃbhiṇaṃ | apūpavaṃtaṃ | ukkinaṃ |*  
> *iṃdra | prātaḥ | juṣasva | naḥ ‖ 1 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र धानावंतं । धाना भृष्टयवाः । तद्वंतं करंभिणं । करंभो दधिमिश्राः सक्तवः । तद्वंतमपूपवंतं सवनीयपुराडाशोपेतमुक्थिनं शस्त्रिणं नोऽस्मदीयमिमं सोमं प्रातः प्रातःसवने जुषस्व । सेवस्व ॥ प्रातः । स्वरादिष्टंतोदात्तत्वेन पठितश्वादंतोदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, the verse addresses you as धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*). धाना (*dhānā*) are parched barley grains, and the word means "having these". करंभिणं (*karaṃbhiṇaṃ*) means having करंभ (*karaṃbha*), which is barley meal mixed with curds. अपूपवंतं (*apūpavaṃtaṃ*) means accompanied by the purodāśa cakes of the pressing. ukthin means accompanied by the recited śastra. Sāyaṇa takes all four words as qualifying "this Soma of ours" (नः (*naḥ*)). The prayer is: accept (जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)), that is, enjoy, this Soma in the morning pressing (प्रातः (*prātaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*)—that which is mixed with barley grain
- करंभिणं (*karaṃbhiṇaṃ*)—that which is mixed with curds
- अपूपवंतं (*apūpavaṃtaṃ*)—that which is accompanied by purodāśa and the like
- उक्किनं (*ukkinaṃ*)—that which is sanctified by the śastra-mantra
- नः (*naḥ*)—this Soma of ours
- प्रातः (*prātaḥ*)—at the time of the morning pressing
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept

### Printed p. 157

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, accept, at the time of the morning pressing, this Soma of ours, which is mixed with barley grain, mixed with curds, accompanied by purodāśa and the like, and sanctified by the śastra-mantra.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Accept, Indra, at our morning sacrifice, this libation, combined with fresh barley, with parched grain and curds, and with cakes, and sanctified by holy prayer.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

धानापंतं (*dhānāpaṃtaṃ*): the Soma juice prepared by mixing in barley flour from which husk and chaff have been removed and which has been made clean. The Soma juice is not merely filtered and drunk as it is. To make it tasty, the āśira substances (milk, curds and barley flour) are mixed into it. Soma juice mixed with milk is called gavāśira, Soma juice mixed with curds is called dadhyāśira, and Soma juice mixed with barley flour is called yavāśira. We have explained this matter at length earlier. Here the word धानावंतं (*dhānāvaṃtaṃ*) denotes the Soma juice mixed with the flour called yavāśira.
करंभिणं (*karaṃbhiṇaṃ*): करंभो दधिमिश्राः सक्तवः । तद्वंतं । (*karaṃbho dadhimiśrāḥ saktavaḥ | tadvaṃtaṃ |*) It is Soma juice mixed with curds and flour. It is also called dadhyāśira.
अपूपवंतं (*apūpavaṃtaṃ*): पुरोडाशोपेतं । (*puroḍāśopetaṃ |*) Barley flour is kneaded, baked on an earthen griddle as one makes a flat bread, and then offered in the fire. This is called purodāśa. Here the word अपूपवंतं (*apūpavaṃtaṃ*) denotes the oblation called purodāśa.
उक्किनं (*ukkinaṃ*): the meaning is "sanctified by recitation of the śastra-mantra and the like". It is the custom to purify the substances of the offering, before offering them, by reciting mantras and by sprinkling water and so on. Here the offering sanctified by mantras is described by the qualifying word उक्किनं (*ukkinaṃ*).
इंद्र प्रातः जुषस्व नः (*iṃdra prātaḥ juṣasva naḥ*): O Indra, the yavāśira, dadhyāśira, purodāśa and so on that we offer are ready, sanctified by mantras. Indra is prayed to accept them at this time of the morning pressing.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पु॒रो॒ळाशं॑ पच॒त्यं॑ जु॒षस्वें॒द्रा गु॑रस्व च ।  
> तुभ्यं॑ ह॒व्यानि॑ सिस्रते ॥ २ ॥

> *puroḷāśaṃ pacatyaṃ juṣasveṃdrā gurasva ca |*  
> *tubhyaṃ havyāni sisrate ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुरोळाशं । पचत्यं । जुषस्व । इंद्र । आ । गुरस्व । च ।  
> तुभ्यं । हव्यानि । सिस्रते ॥ २ ॥

> *puroḷāśaṃ | pacatyaṃ | juṣasva | iṃdra | ā | gurasva | ca |*  
> *tubhyaṃ | havyāni | sisrate ‖ 2 ‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र पचत्यं पचने साधुं पुरोडाशं । पुरो दाशंत एनमिति
> पुरोडाशो हविः । जुषस्व । किंच आ गुरस्व । पुरोडाशभक्षणार्थमुद्यमं कुरु ।
> हव्यानि हवनयोग्यानि पुरोडाशादीनि हवींषि तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं सिस्त्रते । अहवनीयं
> गच्छंति । तानि सेवस्वेति भावः ॥ पचत्यं । पचतशब्दात्तत्र साधुरिति यत्पत्ययांतस्य
> पदस्य द्वच्त्वाभावादत्र यतोऽनाव इत्यस्य प्राप्तिर्नास्ति । तित्सरितः । गुरस्व ! गुरी
> उद्यमने । शविकरणी । निघातः । सिस्त्रते । सृ गतौ । छंदसि जुहोत्यादिः । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, accept the purodāśa that is पचत्यं (*pacatyaṃ*), good (fit) for cooking. Purodāśa is an oblation, explained as "they offer it first" (पुरो (*puro*) …). Further, आ गुरस्व (*ā gurasva*): make an effort to eat the purodāśa. The oblations (हव्यानि (*havyāni*)), the purodāśa and other offerings fit for offering, flow (सिस्त्रते (*sistrate*)) for you, that is, go to the āhavanīya fire for your sake. The sense is: enjoy them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- पचत्यं (*pacatyaṃ*)—that which is cooked
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—the oblation in the form of purodāśa
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept
- आ गुरस्व (*ā gurasva*)—strive for it
- हव्यानि (*havyāni*)—all the oblations
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—intended for you alone
- stream and flow (accept them)

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, accept the oblation in the form of cooked purodāśa. Strive for it. All the oblations flow to you alone. Accept them.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Accept, Indra, the prepared cakes and butter; eat them eagerly :
the oblations flow for you.

### Printed p. 159

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पुरोळाशं पचत्यं (*puroḷāśaṃ pacatyaṃ*): पचने साधुं पुरोडाशं । पुरो दाशंत एनमिति पुरोडाशो हविः । (*pacane sādhuṃ puroḍāśaṃ | puro dāśaṃta enamiti puroḍāśo haviḥ |*) The etymological meaning of the word purodāśa is explained as follows: when oblations are offered to the gods, the oblation that is given before everything else is called purodāśa. The idea is that this purodāśa is well cooked and fit to be eaten.
तुभ्यं हव्यानि सिस्रते (*tubhyaṃ havyāni sisrate*): हवनयोग्यानि पुरोडाशादीनि हवींष त्वदर्थं आहवनीयं गच्छंति । (*havanayogyāni puroḍāśādīni havīṃṣa tvadarthaṃ āhavanīyaṃ gacchaṃti |*) Oblations such as purodāśa, which are fit to be offered, have been prepared and placed for you, Indra, near the āhavanīya fire. Indra is prayed to accept them.
Why must the purodāśa and other oblations be placed near the āhavanīya fire? Could they not be offered to Indra directly? The answer given: Indra is not a deity present before the eyes. Moreover, the established method of offering oblations to the gods is solely by offering them with mantras in the consecrated fire. Therefore the oblations are prepared and placed near the āhavanīya fire so as to be offered in that fire in that manner.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, eat (घसः (*ghasaḥ*)) our purodāśa, and accept (जोषयासे (*joṣayāse*)) our words of praise. The example is वधूयुरिव योषणां (*vadhūyuriva yoṣaṇāṃ*): as one desirous of a woman (वधूयुः (*vadhūyuḥ*)) enjoys a young woman (योषणां (*yoṣaṇāṃ*)) worthy of being enjoyed, so you accept. The rest of the block, which begins at घसः (*ghasaḥ*) and breaks off at the page end, is grammatical.

This block continues the grammatical derivations of the preceding block (the forms जोषयासे (*joṣayāse*), वधूयुरिव (*vadhūyuriva*), योषणां (*yoṣaṇāṃ*)). It adds nothing to the sense.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नः (*naḥ*)—our (O Indra)
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—the purodāśa

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, eat our purodāśa. As a man desirous of a woman enjoys a beautiful woman, accept our speech in the form of praise.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Eat, Indra, our (offered) cakes and butter : derive enjoyment from
our praises, as a lover from his mistress.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this verse, in praying to Indra, the prayer is that he should eat the oblation called purodāśa with relish and listen to our praises. The seer has given an example for this. A young man attached to a woman, that is, to a newly married young bride, is eager to join her. In the same way, let Indra listen to our praise with the greatest relish and eat the oblations that we offer. This is the comparison stated here.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सनश्रुत पुराणतया प्रसिद्ध हे इंद्र नोऽस्मत्संबंधिनमिमं पुरोडाशं
> प्रातःसावे । सूयतेऽत्र सोम इति सावः । तस्मिन् प्रातःसवने जषस्व । यतस्ते प
> तव क्रतुः कर्म बृहन् महद्धि ॥ प्रातःसावे । षुञ् अभिषवे । कर्मणि घञ् ।
> प्रादिसमासः । थाथादिस्वरेणांतोदात्तः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Sanaśruta, O Indra, famed as ancient, accept this purodāśa of ours in the प्रातःसावे (*prātaḥsāve*), that is, in the morning pressing. सावः (*sāvaḥ*) is explained as "that in which Soma is pressed". The reason given is that your क्रतुः (*kratuḥ*), your work, is great (बृहन् महद्धि (*bṛhan mahaddhi*)). The remainder of the block is grammatical.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सनश्रुत (*sanaśruta*)—famed as ancient
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- नः (*naḥ*)—given by us
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—the purodāśa
- प्रातःसावे (*prātaḥsāve*)—in the morning pressing
- जुषस्व (*juṣasva*)—accept
- ते (*te*)—your
- क्रतुः (*kratuḥ*)—work
- बृहन् हि (*bṛhan hi*)—is it not of great nature?

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, famed as ancient, accept at the time of the morning pressing the purodāśa given by us. Your work is renowned as being of great nature.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Indra, renowned of old, accept our cakes and butter, offered at dawn;
for great are your deeds.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

प्रातःसावे (*prātaḥsāve*): सूयतेऽत्र सोम इति सावः । तस्मिन् प्रातस्सवने । (*sūyate 'tra soma iti sāvaḥ | tasmin prātassavane |*) Because in this rite the Soma juice is pressed out and prepared, it is called सावः (*sāvaḥ*) or pressing. This rite performed in the morning is called the morning pressing, that performed at midday the midday pressing, and that performed in the evening the third pressing. According to the Śruti sentence त्रीणि वाव सवनानि (*trīṇi vāva savanāni*), there are only these three pressings. Here only the morning pressing is indicated. In Ṛks 1–4 of this sūkta the morning pressing is the subject, in Ṛk 5 the midday pressing, and in Ṛk 6 the third pressing.
इंद्र क्रतुः हि ते बृहत् (*iṃdra kratuḥ hi te bṛhat*): Since Indra has performed many deeds of valour, such as the slaying of Vṛtra, he is praised here thus: O Indra, your deed of valour is very great, that is, extraordinary.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viniyoga: the anuvākyā verse माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य धानाः (*mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya dhānāḥ*) is for the savanīya cake (puroḍāśa) at the midday pressing. It is prescribed in the sūtra माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य धाना इति माध्यंदिने (*mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya dhānā iti mādhyaṃdine*) (Ā. 5-4).

"O Indra, come to this rite and make fit by eating the roasted barley belonging to the midday pressing, that is, the pressing that takes place at midday, and the lovely, desirable cake. When the worshipper (jaritā), who serves you, hurries here and there to praise you, and therefore acts like a bull (vṛṣāyamāṇa), approaches you with hymns of praise and praises you intensely, then eat the cakes and other oblations." This is the sense.

The rest of the block is grammatical and is not summarised here (the derivations of māddhyandina, cāru, tūrṇārthaḥ, vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ and īṭṭe). He explains तूर्णर्थः (*tūrṇarthaḥ*) with तूर्तिः (*tūrtiḥ*) and इत्वरा संभ्रम (*itvarā saṃbhrama*), and says that ईट्टे (*īṭṭe*) is the present of the root ईड (*īḍa*), "to praise".

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- जरिता (*jaritā*)—the praiser
- तूर्णर्थ (*tūrṇartha*)—one who hurries about in eagerness to praise you
- वृषायमाणः (*vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ*)—one who is swift like a bull
### Printed p. 163
(and intent on his duty)
- स्तोता (*stotā*)—the praiser
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—with words in the form of praise
- उप (*upa*)—(you) approaching
- प्र ईट्टे (*pra īṭṭe*)—praises intensely (then)
- माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य (*mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya*)—offered at the time of the midday pressing
- धानाः (*dhānāḥ*)—the barley grains
- चारुं (*cāruṃ*)—satisfying
- पुरोडाशं (*puroḍāśaṃ*)—the cake
- इह (*iha*)—in this sacrificial rite
- कृष्ण (*kṛṣṇa*)—(by your eating) make fit

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, when the praiser, who hurries about like a bull in eager haste to praise you, approaches you with words in the form of praise and praises you intensely, then eat the barley grains offered at that midday pressing and the satisfying cake in this sacrificial rite, and make them fit.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Partake, Indra, of the barley and the delicious cakes and butter of
the mid-day sacrifice, when by your zealous worshipper, hastening to adore
you, and eager as a bull, is present, and celebrates (you) with hymns.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra explains, in the sūtra माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य धाना इति माध्यंदिने (*mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya dhānā iti mādhyaṃdine*), that this Ṛk, माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य धाना (*mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya dhānā*), is to be recited as the puronuvākyā mantra in the cake-offering belonging to the midday pressing. (Ā. 5-4)

स्तोता जरिता (*stotā jaritā*)—Although these two words both indicate one meaning, "one who praises", the commentator explains a difference in meaning: for the word stotā he takes "one who praises with words in the form of praise", and for the word jaritā, भवत्परिचरणं कुर्वाणः (*bhavatparicaraṇaṃ kurvāṇaḥ*), "one who does service (śuśrūṣā) to you".

तूर्णर्थः (*tūrṇarthaḥ*)—त्वां स्तोतुमितस्ततस्वरितॆगमनः (*tvāṃ stotumitastatasvaritègamanaḥ*). The word tūrṇi, formed from the word इत्वरा संभ्रमे (*itvarā saṃbhrame*), means "running about in eagerness". Here it means the ṛtvij, or the praiser, who runs about eagerly here and there in order to praise Indra.

वृषायमाणः (*vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ*)—This word is an adjective of the word stotā. It describes the praiser who hurries about like a bull: as a bull moves swiftly of its own will, so the ṛtvij runs about eagerly; this is the comparison with the bull. While a sacrifice is performed, the praisers and the ṛtvij priests help one another and run about eagerly, heedless of any toil, in order to work with devotion
### Printed p. 164
at their own duties. To indicate this, the seer has used the words tūrṇarthaḥ and vṛṣāyamāṇaḥ and has made his intention plain.

> ऋ॒भु॒मंतं॒ वाज॑वंतं त्वा कवे॒ प्रय॑स्वंत॒ उप॑ शिक्षेम  ॒॑

> *tṛtīye dhānāḥ savane puruṣṭuta puroḷāśamāhutaṃ māmahasva naḥ |*
