#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मि॒त्रो जना॑न्यातयति ब्रुवा॒णो मि॒त्रो दा॑धार पृथि॒वीमु॒त द्यां ।  
> मि॒त्रः कृ॒ष्टीरनि॑मिषा॒बि च॑ष्टे मि॒त्राय॑ ह॒व्यं घृ॒तव॑ज्जुहोत॥

> *mitro janānyātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthivīmuta dyāṃ |*  
> *mitraḥ kṛṣṭīranimiṣābi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ ghṛtavajjuhota‖*

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मित्रः । जनान् । यातयति । ब्रुवाणः । मित्रः । दाधार । पृथिवीं । उत । द्यां ।  
> मित्रः । कृष्टीः । अनिमिषा । अभि । चष्टे । मित्राय । हव्यं । धृतवत् । जुहोत ॥१॥

> *mitraḥ | janān | yātayati | bruvāṇaḥ | mitraḥ | dādhāra | pṛthivīṃ | uta | dyāṃ |*  
> *mitraḥ | kṛṣṭīḥ | animiṣā | abhi | caṣṭe | mitrāya | havyaṃ | dhṛtavat | juhota ‖1‖*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ब्रुवाणः स्तूयमानः शब्दं कुर्वाणो वा मित्रः । प्रकर्षेण सर्वैर्मायते ज्ञायते तथा सर्वान्वृष्टिप्रदानेन त्रायत इति वा मित्रः सूरः । जनान्
> कर्षकादिजनान्यातयति । कृष्यादिकर्मसु प्रयत्नं कारयति । तथा मित्र एव पृथिवीमुतापि च द्यामेतावुभौ लोकौ वृष्टिद्वारान्नं यागांश्च जनयन् दाधार । धारयति । तथा सति मित्रोऽनिमिषानिमिषेणानुग्रहदृष्ट्वा कृष्टीः कर्मवतो मनुष्यानभि चष्टे । सर्वतः पश्यति । एतत्सर्वं ज्ञात्वा हे ऋत्विजो धृतवदुपस्तरणाभिघारणयुक्तं हव्यं हवनयोग्यं पुरोडाशादिकं तस्मै मित्राय देवाय जुहोत ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

ब्रुवाणः (*bruvāṇaḥ*) means being praised, or making sound; this is Mitra. Mitra is so called because he is widely known (मायते (*māyate*), from प्रकर्षेण (*prakarṣeṇa*)) by all, or because he protects all by granting rain; Mitra is the sun. He यातयति (*yātayati*) the people, the farmers and others: he makes them strive in tilling and other works. Likewise Mitra alone sustains (दाधार (*dādhāra*)) both earth and heaven, these two worlds, by producing food and sacrifices through rain. That being so, Mitra with an unwinking, gracious gaze (अनिमिषा (*animiṣā*)) looks all around (अभि चष्टे (*abhi caṣṭe*)) on the कृष्टीः (*kṛṣṭīḥ*), men engaged in work. Knowing all this, O priests, offer (जुहोत (*juhota*)) to that god Mitra the oblation fit for offering, such as the puroḍāśa, accompanied by ghee (धृतवत् (*dhṛtavat*)), with the spreading of ghee beneath and the pouring of it over.

### Printed p. 442

> जुहुत । प्रयच्छतेत्यर्थः । उक्तार्थं यास्को ब्रवीति । मित्रो जनान्यातयति
> ब्रुवाणः शब्दं कुर्वन् । मित्र एव धारयति प्रथिवीं च दिवं च । मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषन्नभिपश्यतीति । कृष्टय इति मनुष्यनाम कर्मवंतो भवंति विकृष्टदेहा वा ।
> मित्राय हव्यं धृतवज्जुहोतेति व्याख्यातं । जुहोतिर्दानकर्मा । नि. १०-२२ ।
> इति ॥ यातयति । यती प्रयत्न इत्यस्य ण्यंतस्य लटि रूपं । दाधार । तुजादीनामित्यभ्यासस्य दीर्घः । जुहोत । जुहोतेर्लोटि प्रत्ययस्य तबादेशः । गुणः ।
> निघातः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa completes the gloss of the word जुहोत (*juhota*): it means "give". He then cites Yāska for the sense already stated. "Mitra urges men on, speaking, that is, making a sound. Mitra alone sustains the earth and the heaven. Mitra looks upon the कृष्टीः (*kṛṣṭīḥ*) without closing his eyes." Yāska adds that कृष्टयः (*kṛṣṭayaḥ*) is a name for men, who are active, or whose bodies are extended. "मित्राय हव्यं धृतवज्जुहोत (*mitrāya havyaṃ dhṛtavajjuhota*)" is already explained; जुहोति (*juhoti*) is a verb of giving (Ni. 10-22).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ब्रुवाणः (*bruvāṇaḥ*)—the one who is praised
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—the Sun, in the form of Mitra
- जनान् (*janān*)—the people
- यातयति (*yātayati*)—impels them each to their own works
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—that same Mitra
- पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*)—the earth
- उत (*uta*)—and
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heaven too
- दाधार (*dādhāra*)—has upheld
- मित्रः (*mitraḥ*)—that same Mitra
- अनिमिषा (*animiṣā*)—with a favouring gaze
- कृष्टीः (*kṛṣṭīḥ*)—all people
- अभि चष्टे (*abhi caṣṭe*)—looks around upon (O priests)
- धृतवत् (*dhṛtavat*)—endowed with ghee
- हव्यं (*havyaṃ*)—the oblation
- मित्राय (*mitrāya*)—addressed to that Mitra
- जुहोत (*juhota*)—offer in the form of an oblation

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Mitra, who is praised by the singers, impels the people to their own works. That same Mitra has upheld the earth and the heaven. That same Mitra looks around upon all people with a favouring gaze. O priests, offer the oblation, endowed with ghee, as an oblation addressed to that Mitra.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Mitra, when praised, animates men to exertion : Indra sustains both
the earth and heaven : Mitra looks upon men with unclosing eyes : offer to
Mitra the oblations of clarified butter.**NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The author of the Nirukta too has explained the purport of this mantra: मित्रः जनान् आयातयति प्रब्रुवाणः । शब्दं कुर्वन् । मित्र एव धारयति पृथिवीं च दिवं च । मित्रः कृष्टी अनिमिषन् अभिविपश्यति इति । कृष्टयः इति मनुष्यनाम । कर्मवंतः भवंति । विकृष्टदेहा वा .... .... ॥ (*mitraḥ janān āyātayati prabruvāṇaḥ | śabdaṃ kurvan | mitra eva dhārayati pṛthivīṃ ca divaṃ ca | mitraḥ kṛṣṭī animiṣan abhivipaśyati iti | kṛṣṭayaḥ iti manuṣyanāma | karmavaṃtaḥ bhavaṃti | vikṛṣṭadehā vā .... .... ‖*) (Ni. 10-22)

### Printed p. 443
Mitra, making an exhorting sound, leads the people along the good path. Mitra alone upholds and protects both heaven and earth. Without touching a limit he surveys all the people completely. Here the word कृष्ण (*kṛṣṇa*)**NOTE** is a synonym for human beings. Because the body is always engaged in action and is extended, this is a word used as an epithet.

Sāyaṇa's view is that the word Mitra is a synonym of the Sun. He has shown the meaning of the parts of the word, saying that the word Mitra is formed by the union of the two roots मि (*mi*) and त्रा (*trā*): प्रकर्षेण सर्वैर्मीयते ज्ञायते तथा सर्वान् वृष्टिप्रदानेन त्रायत इति ना मित्रः सूर्यः । (*prakarṣeṇa sarvairmīyate jñāyate tathā sarvān vṛṣṭipradānena trāyata iti nā mitraḥ sūryaḥ |*). He is fully known by all, and he protects all. Because he has these two qualities, the Sun is what the word Mitra denotes.

Since the three actions specified in this mantra also belong to the Sun, the eye of the world, the sense referring to the Sun is proper. They are: impelling men to their respective works; upholding heaven and earth together; and viewing everything completely in the form of his own radiance. These are the three functions.

अवत इत्येष हीदग्ं सर्वमवति (*avata ityeṣa hīdagṃ sarvamavati*) (Śa. Brā. 8-7-3-13). "This Sun alone makes the whole world animate" and so on: the power of the Sun thus described is indicated here by the word यातयति (*yātayati*). Moreover, praises such as सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता (*savitā sarvasya prasavitā*) are well known. And:

आदित्यास्ता पृष्ठे सादयामीति । इयं ना अदितिरस्यामेवैनमेतत्पतिष्ठायां प्रतिष्ठापयत्यंतरिक्षस्य धर्त्रिं विष्टंभनीं दिशामधिपत्नीं भुवनानामित्यंतरिक्षस्य ह्येष धर्ता विष्टंभनो दिशामधिपतिर्भुवनानामूर्मिर्दप्रोऽपामसीतिरसः .... .... ॥ (*ādityāstā pṛṣṭhe sādayāmīti | iyaṃ nā aditirasyāmevainametatpatiṣṭhāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayatyaṃtarikṣasya dhartriṃ viṣṭaṃbhanīṃ diśāmadhipatnīṃ bhuvanānāmityaṃtarikṣasya hyeṣa dhartā viṣṭaṃbhano diśāmadhipatirbhuvanānāmūrmirdapro 'pāmasītirasaḥ .... .... ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 8-2-1-10)

In sentences of this kind all the qualities of the Sun mentioned above are stated together. This Āditya, the son of Aditi who supports all, is the light of the universe. He is the upholder of all the worlds beginning with the atmosphere, the lord of the universe, Prajāpati, the eye of the world; thus all the qualities are described.

कृष्टीः (*kṛṣṭīḥ*)—for the word कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*) he has given the meaning कर्मवतः मनुष्यान् (*karmavataḥ manuṣyān*), "men engaged in action". Since it is described that Mitra, in the form of the Sun, has upheld both heaven and earth, one would not be wrong in saying that the word कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*) means all beings, including the gods.

### Printed p. 444
यस्येक्ष्वाकुरुप व्रते रेवान्मराय्येधते दिवीव पंच कृष्टयः । (*yasyekṣvākurupa vrate revānmarāyyedhate divīva paṃca kṛṣṭayaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-60-9)

In passages of this kind a likeness is stated between the five कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*) of the earth and the five कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*) of the heavenly world. Moreover, when it is told who the five कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*) are, it is said: मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गंधर्वोरगराक्षसाः (*manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ*) (Bṛ. De. Ni. 68); the five groups, gods, men and the rest, together are the five कृष्टि (*kṛṣṭi*). Therefore there can be no fault in stating the above meaning here.

अभिचष्टे (*abhicaṣṭe*)—when the root चक्ष (*cakṣa*) is joined with the prefix अभि (*abhi*), it has the sense "look around", and also the sense "shine so as to be seen all around by all". The author of the Nirukta has given for the word चक्षसे (*cakṣase*) the purport दर्शनाय (*darśanāya*) (Ni. 9-27), "for seeing", and for the word अभिचष्टे (*abhicaṣṭe*) the purport अभिपश्यति (*abhipaśyati*) (Ni. 10-22), सर्वतः पश्यति (*sarvataḥ paśyati*), "sees well all around". The above sense is found in examples such as महे रणाय चक्षसे (*mahe raṇāya cakṣase*) (10-9-1). And:

महत्ते विष्णो अभिचक्ष्यं कृतं पश्येम तुर्वशं यदुं । (*mahatte viṣṇo abhicakṣyaṃ kṛtaṃ paśyema turvaśaṃ yaduṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-4-7)

Here the word अभिचक्ष्य (*abhicakṣya*) means प्रकाश्य (*prakāśya*), that is, to make oneself manifest and visible so that others can see fully. In the present Ṛk it may be said that Āditya, who has upheld heaven and earth together, possesses two kinds of power: the power of illuminating the whole world and the power of being the eye of the world are found in him alone.

चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अंतरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थुषश्च ॥ (*citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī aṃtarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-1)

In mantras of this kind all the qualities mentioned in the present Ṛk are described together. This same mantra is recited in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā with a slight variation. The text there is:

मित्रो जनान्यातयति प्रजानन्मित्रो दाधार वृद्धिवीमुत द्यां । मित्रः कृष्टीरनिमिषाभिचष्टे सत्याय हव्यं धृतवद्विधेम ॥ (*mitro janānyātayati prajānanmitro dādhāra vṛddhivīmuta dyāṃ | mitraḥ kṛṣṭīranimiṣābhicaṣṭe satyāya havyaṃ dhṛtavadvidhema ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 3-4-11-5)

In place of ब्रुवाणः (*bruvāṇaḥ*) of the present Ṛk, the Taittirīya Saṃhitā has प्रजानन् (*prajānan*), and in the second half, in place of मित्राय (*mitrāya*) it has सत्याय (*satyāya*). Since the cited mantra has प्रजानन् (*prajānan*) in the first half, for the word अभिचष्टे (*abhicaṣṭe*) the meaning प्रकाशयति (*prakāśayati*),

### Printed p. 445
"makes everything shine", fits. And it is natural that, in सत्याय हव्यं (*satyāya havyaṃ*), the word सत्य (*satya*) is a synonym of the word मित्र (*mitra*). In the sacrifice called Devasū, the injunction that the offering be made to Mitra, whose nature is truth, shows this non-difference: देवसुवां हविष्णु मित्रस्य सत्यस्य (*devasuvāṃ haviṣṇu mitrasya satyasya*) and so on. This subject will be explained in the Special Topics of the next Ṛk.

> न ह॑न्यते॒ न जी॑यते॒ त्वोतो॒ नैन॒मंहो॑ अश्नो॒त्यंति॑तो॒ न  ॒

> *dūrāt ‖ 2 ‖*

> न । हन्यते । न । जीयते । त्वाऊतः । न । एनं । अ०हः । अश्नोति । अंतितः । न ।

> *pra | saḥ | mitra | martaḥ | astu | prayasvān | yaḥ | te | āditya | śikṣati | vratena |*

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवसुवां हविषु मित्रस्य सत्यस्य प्र स मित्रॆति याज्या । एष्यव प्रातर्होमस्य कालात्ययनिमित्ते मृत्रे चरौ याज्या । सूत्रितं च । प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु
> प्रयस्वांस्तां नष्टवान्महिमाय पृच्छते । आ. ४-११ । इति ॥ तत इष्टिर्मित्रः
> सूर्योऽभि यो महिना दिवं प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वानिति संस्थितायां ।
> आ. ३-१२ । इति च ॥
> हे आदित्य व्रतेन यज्ञेन युक्तो यो मनुष्यस्ते तुभ्यं शिक्षति हनिर्लक्षणमन्नं ददाति हे मित्र स मर्तो मनुष्यः प्रयस्वानन्नवान् प्रास्तु । प्रभवतु ।
> तोतस्त्वया रक्षितः स मनुष्यः केनापि न हन्यते न बाध्यते । न जीयते ! नाभिभूयते च। एनं तुभ्यं हविर्दत्तवंतं पुरुषमंहः पापमंतितः समीपान्नाश्नोति।
> न प्राप्नोति । दूरादपि न प्राप्नोति ॥ शिक्षतिर्दानकर्मा । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं
> यद्वृत्तयोगादनिघातः । जीयते । जयतेः कर्मणि यक्यकृत्सार्वधातुकयोरिति
> दीर्घः । त्वोतः । तृतीया कर्मणीति पूर्वपदस्वरः । अश्नोति । अशू व्याप्तौ ।
> स्वादिः । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Viniyoga: in the offerings of the देवसुवां हविषु (*devasuvāṃ haviṣu*) to Mitra, the true, "प्र स मित्र (*pra sa mitra*)" is the yājyā. It is likewise the yājyā in the caru offered to Mitra when the time of the morning homa has been exceeded. This is laid down in the sūtra (Ā. 4-11), "प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वांस्तां नष्टवान्महिमाय पृच्छते (*pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvāṃstāṃ naṣṭavānmahimāya pṛcchate*)", and in the sūtra (Ā. 3-12), "then the iṣṭi to Mitra: सूर्योऽभि यो महिना दिवं (*sūryo 'bhi yo mahinā divaṃ*), प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान् (*pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvān*), when the rite is completed".

Meaning: O Āditya, the man who, bound to the rite, gives you the food that is the oblation, O Mitra, let that mortal be rich in food and prosper. Protected by you, that man is neither slain nor hindered by anyone, and he is not overcome. Sin does not reach this man who has given you the oblation, whether from near or from afar. शिक्षति (*śikṣati*) is a verb of giving; the parasmaipada is by interchange.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आदित्य (*āditya*)—O Āditya
- व्रतेन (*vratena*)—joined to the sacrifice
- यः (*yaḥ*)—the man who
- ते (*te*)—to you
- शिक्षति (*śikṣati*)—offers the food in the form of the oblation
- मित्र (*mitra*)—O Mitra
- स मर्तः (*sa martaḥ*)—that man
- प्रयस्वान् (*prayasvān*)—possessed of food
- प्र अस्तु (*pra astu*)—let him be
- त्वोतः (*tvotaḥ*)—the man protected by you
- न हन्यते (*na hanyate*)—is not injured by anyone
- न जीयते (*na jīyate*)—is not conquered by anyone
- एनं (*enaṃ*)—such a sacrificer
- अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—sin
- अंतितः (*aṃtitaḥ*)—even near
- न अश्नोति (*na aśnoti*)—does not reach
- दूरात् न (*dūrāt na*)—nor is it far off

### Printed p. 446

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Āditya, the man bound to the sacrifice who offers you food in the form of the oblation, O Mitra, let that man become rich in food. The man protected by you is not injured by anyone and is not conquered by anyone. Sins do not come near such a sacrificer, nor are they far off.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May that mortal enjoy abundance, Mitra, who presents you, Aditya, (with offerings) at the sacred rite ; protected by you he is not harmed ; he is not overcome by any one ; sin reaches him not, either from afar or nigh.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

At the offering of the oblations called देवसुव (*devasuva*), and at the morning offering when its time has been exceeded, and also when a caru is offered to Mitra, this Ṛk प्र स मित्र (*pra sa mitra*) is to be used as the yājyā mantra. This is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वांस्तां नष्टवान्महिमाय पृच्छते (*pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvāṃstāṃ naṣṭavānmahimāya pṛcchate*) (Ā. 4-11) and by the sūtra तत इष्टिर्मित्रः सूर्योऽभि यो महिना दिवं प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वानिति संस्थितायां (*tata iṣṭirmitraḥ sūryo 'bhi yo mahinā divaṃ pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvāniti saṃsthitāyāṃ*) (Ā. 3-12).

The chief purport of the mantra is that one who worships Āditya, whose nature is Mitra, becomes wholly free of sin and becomes victorious. There is an injunction that this mantra be recited and the offering made at the time of offering oblations to the Devasūs, when the offering is addressed to Mitra, whose nature is truth. One may first learn what the Devasū sacrifice is, and then learn the explanation of the mantra.

### Printed p. 447
देवसुवः (*devasuvaḥ*): this is the name by which the group of gods who give vitality to the whole world is called. The number of these gods is eight. At the time of the abhiṣecanīya rite, a part of the Rājasūya, the prescribed oblation is to be offered to these eight gods. Its order is as follows.

1. सवित्रे सत्यप्रसवाय । द्वादशकपालं वाष्टाकपालं वा पुरोडाशं निर्वपति प्लाशुकानां व्रीहीणां सविता वै देवानां प्रसविता सवितृप्रसूतः सूया इत्यथ यत्‌ प्लाशुकानां व्रीहीणां क्षिप्रे मा प्रसुवानिति ॥ (*savitre satyaprasavāya | dvādaśakapālaṃ vāṣṭākapālaṃ vā puroḍāśaṃ nirvapati plāśukānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ savitā vai devānāṃ prasavitā savitṛprasūtaḥ sūyā ityatha yat plāśukānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ kṣipre mā prasuvāniti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 5-3-3-2)

The grain called प्लाशुक (*plāśuka*) gives vitality; it is to give rain quickly. With it an oblation consisting of eight potsherds or of twelve potsherds is to be prepared and offered to Savitṛ, the impeller of the gods and impeller of truth. By thus offering, the king who is ready for the consecration gains confidence of acquiring vigour in his duty.

2. अधाग्नये गृहपतये । अष्टाकपालं पुरोडाशं निर्वपत्याशूनां श्रीर्वै गार्हपत्यं यावतो-यावत ईष्टे तदेनमग्निरेव गृहपतिर्गार्हपत्यमभिपरिणयत्यथ यदाशूनां क्षिप्रे मा परिणयानिति ॥ (*adhāgnaye gṛhapataye | aṣṭākapālaṃ puroḍāśaṃ nirvapatyāśūnāṃ śrīrvai gārhapatyaṃ yāvato-yāvata īṣṭe tadenamagnireva gṛhapatirgārhapatyamabhipariṇayatyatha yadāśūnāṃ kṣipre mā pariṇayāniti ‖*)

The grain called आशु (*āśu*) is quick to bear fruit. From this grain a puroḍāśa of eight potsherds is to be prepared and offered to Agni, the lord of the house. The position of lord of the house is endowed with wealth. The king who obtains lordship of the house through the grace of such an Agni becomes endowed with wealth. And by offering a puroḍāśa made of आशु (*āśu*) grain, he too, like it, gains quick prosperity.

3. अथ सोमाय वनस्पतॆये । श्यामाकं चरुं निर्वपति तदेनग्ं सोम एव वनस्पतिरोषदिभ्यः सुवत्यथ यच्छ्यामाको भवत्येते वै सोमसौषधीनां प्रत्यक्षतमां यच्छ्यामाकास्तस्नाच्छ्यामाको भवति ॥ (*atha somāya vanaspatèye | śyāmākaṃ caruṃ nirvapati tadenagṃ soma eva vanaspatiroṣadibhyaḥ suvatyatha yacchyāmāko bhavatyete vai somasauṣadhīnāṃ pratyakṣatamāṃ yacchyāmākāstasnācchyāmāko bhavati ‖*)

King Soma is lord of the plants. Among plants, this श्यामाक (*śyāmāka*) is the dearest to Soma. If a puroḍāśa is prepared from श्यामाक (*śyāmāka*) and offered to Soma, the cause of peace and nourishment, the king who is being consecrated obtains peace and nourishment.

4. अथ बृहस्पतये वाचे । नैवारं चरुं निर्वपति तदेनं बृहस्पतिरेव वाचे सुवत्यथ यन्नॆवारो भवति ब्रह्म वै बृहस्पतिरेते वै ब्रह्मणा सच्यंते यन्नीवारास्तस्नान्नीवारो भवति ॥ (*atha bṛhaspataye vāce | naivāraṃ caruṃ nirvapati tadenaṃ bṛhaspatireva vāce suvatyatha yannèvāro bhavati brahma vai bṛhaspatirete vai brahmaṇā sacyaṃte yannīvārāstasnānnīvāro bhavati ‖*)

### Printed p. 448
Bṛhaspati is lord of speech, which is dear to brahman. The नीवार (*nīvāra*) grain is nourished by brahman. Therefore, by preparing a puroḍāśa from this नीवार (*nīvāra*) grain and offering it to Bṛhaspati, the king obtains the grace of Bṛhaspati, lord of speech, and increases his own power of speech.

1. अथेंद्राय ज्येष्ठाय । हायनानां चरुं निर्वपति तदेनमिंद्र एव ज्येष्ठो ज्येष्ठमभिपरिणयत्यथ यद्धायनानां भवत्यतिष्ठा वा एता ओषधयो यद्वायना अतिष्टो वा इंद्रस्तस्माद्दायनानां भवति ॥ (*atheṃdrāya jyeṣṭhāya | hāyanānāṃ caruṃ nirvapati tadenamiṃdra eva jyeṣṭho jyeṣṭhamabhipariṇayatyatha yaddhāyanānāṃ bhavatyatiṣṭhā vā etā oṣadhayo yadvāyanā atiṣṭo vā iṃdrastasmāddāyanānāṃ bhavati ‖*)**NOTE**

Among the gods Indra alone is the eldest and the lord. Among plants हायन (*hāyana*) is the eldest. Therefore a caru is to be prepared from हायन (*hāyana*) grain and offered to Indra. Through the grace of this Indra the king, surpassing the foremost position, becomes fit to be lord of all.

6) अथ रुद्राय पशुपतये । रौद्रं गावीधुकं चरुं निर्वपति तदेनग्ं रुद, एव पशुपतिः पशुभ्यः सुवत्यथ यद्दावीधुको भवति वास्तवो वा विष देवो वास्तव्या गावीधुकास्त्स्माद्गावीधुको भवति ॥ (*atha rudrāya paśupataye | raudraṃ gāvīdhukaṃ caruṃ nirvapati tadenagṃ ruda, eva paśupatiḥ paśubhyaḥ suvatyatha yaddāvīdhuko bhavati vāstavo vā viṣa devo vāstavyā gāvīdhukāstsmādgāvīdhuko bhavati ‖*)

Rudra is lord of animals. गावीधुक (*gāvīdhuka*) grain belongs to Rudra. In the sacrifice the वास्तव्य (*vāstavya*) portion is due to Rudra. गवेधुक (*gavedhuka*)**NOTE** too must belong to this वास्तव्य (*vāstavya*) group. Therefore, by offering a caru of गवेधुक (*gavedhuka*) grain to Rudra, lord of animals, there is no doubt that the king obtains wealth of cattle.

7) अथ मित्राय सत्याय ! नांबानां चरुं निर्वपति तदेनं मित्र एव सत्यो ब्रह्मणे सुवत्यथ यन्नांबानां भवति (*atha mitrāya satyāya ! nāṃbānāṃ caruṃ nirvapati tadenaṃ mitra eva satyo brahmaṇe suvatyatha yannāṃbānāṃ bhavati*)

Although the नांब (*nāṃba*) seed belongs to Varuṇa, the नांब (*nāṃba*) plant belongs to Mitra. Therefore, if a caru is prepared from नांब (*nāṃba*) seed and offered to Mitra, whose nature is truth and who is the impeller of truth, the king gains Mitra's favour and obtains brahmanical splendour.

8) अथ वरुणाय धर्मपतॆये । वारुणं यवमयं चरुं निर्वपति तदेनं वरुण एव धर्मपतिर्धर्मस्य पतिं करोति परमता वै सा यो धर्मस्य पतिरसद्यो हि परमतां गच्छति तग्ंहि धर्म उपयंति तस्माद्वरुणाय धर्मपतये (*atha varuṇāya dharmapatèye | vāruṇaṃ yavamayaṃ caruṃ nirvapati tadenaṃ varuṇa eva dharmapatirdharmasya patiṃ karoti paramatā vai sā yo dharmasya patirasadyo hi paramatāṃ gacchati tagṃhi dharma upayaṃti tasmādvaruṇāya dharmapataye*) (Śa. Brā. 5-3-3-9)**NOTE**

To be lord of dharma and president of dharma is the highest office of a king. For him to obtain this office the favour of Varuṇa, the protector of all dharma in the universe, is absolutely necessary. Therefore a caru is to be prepared from barley, which is dear to him, and offered to him. Through Varuṇa's favour the king obtains the most praiseworthy office of president of dharma.

### Printed p. 449
Thus all eight gods are worshipped, each according to his position, in the rite called Devasū, a part of the Rājasūya. Among them Mitra, whose nature is truth, is one. For his satisfaction the present mantra is recited. The same Devasū sacrifice is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā also, with slight variation. Differences appear only in a few small points; there is no difference in the explanation of the principal points.

अग्नये गृहपतये पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालं निर्वपति कृष्णानां व्रीहीणाग्० सोमाय वनस्पतये श्यामाकं चरुग्० सवित्रे सत्यप्रसवाय पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालमाशूनां व्रीहीणाग्० रुद्राय पशुपतये गावीधुकं चरुं बृहस्पतये वाचस्पतये नैवारं चरुमिंद्राय ज्येष्ठाय पुरोडाशमेकादशकपालं महाव्रीहीणां मित्राय सत्यायाम्यानां चरुं वरुणाय धर्मपतये यवमयं चरुग्० सविता त्वा प्रसवानाग्० सुवतां ॥ (*agnaye gṛhapataye puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālaṃ nirvapati kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇāg0 somāya vanaspataye śyāmākaṃ carug0 savitre satyaprasavāya puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālamāśūnāṃ vrīhīṇāg0 rudrāya paśupataye gāvīdhukaṃ caruṃ bṛhaspataye vācaspataye naivāraṃ carumiṃdrāya jyeṣṭhāya puroḍāśamekādaśakapālaṃ mahāvrīhīṇāṃ mitrāya satyāyāmyānāṃ caruṃ varuṇāya dharmapataye yavamayaṃ carug0 savitā tvā prasavānāg0 suvatāṃ ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 18-10)

In these mantras the order of the oblations to be offered to the Devasuvas is explained. The number and names of the gods are just as stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. But there is a slightly different account of the grains used for the oblations. For Savitṛ, the impeller of truth, the Śatapatha prescribes the grain called प्लाशुक (*plāśuka*); for Agni, lord of the house, the आशु (*āśu*) grain; for Indra, the eldest, the हायन (*hāyana*) grain. The Taittirīya Saṃhitā specifies the आशु (*āśu*) grain for Savitṛ, black rice for Agni, and large rice for Indra. Although the number of gods is the same, the Śatapatha describes these eight gods in one order. In place of the Śatapatha's बृहस्पतये वाचे (*bṛhaspataye vāce*), the Taittirīya Saṃhitā has बृहस्पतये वाचस्पतये (*bṛhaspataye vācaspataye*).

Thus Mitra, described in the Devasū sacrifice as truth in nature, is praised in this mantra. The man who worships and adores this god is declared to become victorious, possessed of food and free from sin. The same Āditya-principle that was praised as Mitra in the previous mantra is praised in the present one also. This same mantra is recited in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa also (Tai. Brā. 1-7-4-1). There Sāyaṇa and Bhaṭṭabhāskara have given the explanation of the present Ṛk.

यः ते शिक्षति सः प्रयस्वान् अस्तु (*yaḥ te śikṣati saḥ prayasvān astu*)—Sāyaṇa explains in the Ṛksaṃhitā-bhāṣya that the prayer is: "may he who offers you oblations and the like be rich in food." He has shown that the word शिक्षति (*śikṣati*) has the meaning ददाति (*dadāti*), "gives". Bhaṭṭabhāskara, on the Taittirīya Saṃhitā

### Printed p. 450
[The first lines of this page complete the sentence from the previous page.] In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, Bhaṭṭabhāskara shows two kinds of construction for the word शिक्षति (*śikṣati*) and states two kinds of purport. First: हे आदित्य आदितेः पुत्र यस्तव प्रीतेन कर्मणा यागादिना शिक्षति शक्तो भवितुमिच्छति....सः न हन्यते....॥ (*he āditya āditeḥ putra yastava prītena karmaṇā yāgādinā śikṣati śakto bhavitumicchati....saḥ na hanyate....‖*) "O Āditya, son of Aditi, whoever gains the power to please you with an action dear to you and to win your favour, he becomes possessed of food": this is one way. Second: शिक्ष-विद्यो पादाने । (*śikṣa-vidyo pādāne |*) वृतेनेति व्यत्ययेन द्वितीयं बहुवचनस्य स्थाने तृतीयैकवचनं । (*vṛteneti vyatyayena dvitīyaṃ bahuvacanasya sthāne tṛtīyaikavacanaṃ |*) The root शिक्ष (*śikṣa*) is used in the sense "acquire learning". Instead of the accusative व्रतानि (*vratāni*) ("vows") the instrumental व्रतेन (*vratena*) is used. The purport, he gives as another way of taking the meaning, is that those who practise the vows again and again and worship Āditya become possessed of food.

But there are many places in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā where the root शिक्ष (*śikṣa*) is used in the sense of giving. For example—

द्युमा असि क्रतुमा इंद्र धीरः शिक्षा शचीवस्तव नः शचेभिः । (*dyumā asi kratumā iṃdra dhīraḥ śikṣā śacīvastava naḥ śacebhiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-12)

Here the sense of giving is stated for शिक्ष (*śikṣa*): "O Indra, possessed of action, give us wealth." Therefore, in the present mantra, the meaning of शिक्षति (*śikṣati*) as "offers the oblation" is not unsound.

अंहः (*aṃhaḥ*)—अंहतिश्चांहश्चांहुश्च हंतेः । (*aṃhatiścāṃhaścāṃhuśca haṃteḥ |*) (Ni. 4-25). Although the word अंहस् (*aṃhas*) is derived from the root हन् (*han*), meaning "to injure", the sense in commonest use for this word is "sin", the source of injury; in the present Ṛk too the meaning is sin.

तोतः (*totaḥ*)—त्वया ऊतः । (*tvayā ūtaḥ |*) "One protected by you": it refers to Āditya. The purport is that for one protected by Āditya, wealth of food, protection from enemies in the form of poverty and the like, and release from sin are all assured.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This is the anuvākyā for Mitra (Satya) in the Devasū oblations; the Āśvalāyana sūtra अनमीवास इळया मदंतः प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान् (*anamīvāsa iḷayā madaṃtaḥ pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvān*) (Ā. 4-11) prescribes it. "O Mitra, free from disease, rejoicing with इळया (*iḷayā*), food, moving about at will everywhere in the wide expanse of the earth, 'with measured knees' (मितज्ञवः (*mitajñavaḥ*), i.e. मितजानुका (*mitajānukā*)), dwelling near the rite of Āditya, that is, performing his rite, may we be in the good, gracious mind of Mitra, Āditya." The rest is grammar.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अनमीवासः (*anamīvāsaḥ*)—free from disease (O Mitra)
- इळॆया (*iḷèyā*)—with food
- मदंतः (*madaṃtaḥ*)—being satisfied
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- वरिमन् (*variman*)—in the wide region
- मितज्ञवः (*mitajñavaḥ*)—with measured walking
- आ (*ā*) (गच्छंत (*gacchaṃta*))—moving about freely
- आदित्यस्य (*ādityasya*)—directed to Āditya
- व्रतं (*vrataṃ*)—the rite
- उपक्षियंतः (*upakṣiyaṃtaḥ*)—performing
- वयं (*vayaṃ*)—we
- मित्रस्य (*mitrasya*)—of Āditya
- सुमत् (*sumat*)—in the gracious mind
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Mitra, may the gracious mind of Āditya rest upon us, who are free from disease, satisfied with food, moving about freely in the wide regions of the earth, and performing the rite directed to Āditya.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
May we, exempt from disease, rejoicing in (abundant) food, roaming free over the wide (expanse) of the earth, diligent in the worship of Aditya, ever be in the good favour of Mitra.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the oblations called Devasū are offered, this Ṛk अनमीवास इळया (*anamīvāsa iḷayā*) is to be recited as the puronuvākyā mantra addressed to Mitra; this is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra अनमीवास इळया मदंतः प्र स मित्र मर्तो अस्तु प्रयस्वान् (*anamīvāsa iḷayā madaṃtaḥ pra sa mitra marto astu prayasvān*) (Ā. 4-11).

In this mantra the favour of Āditya, in the form of Mitra, is prayed for. Neither wealth of food nor wealth of cattle is sought. Even where life is prosperous and contented, the prayer is for good understanding, that one may be a doer of good acts and follow the good path. The epithets अनमीवासः (*anamīvāsaḥ*) and इळॆया मदंतः (*iḷèyā madaṃtaḥ*) also show the good state of the worshipper.

On the nature of Iḷā. The word इळया (*iḷayā*) is here explained as "food". The particular deity denoted by the word इळा (*iḷā*) was described earlier, when the deities of the Āprī hymns were treated [Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 11, p. 264]. But the other meanings suggested by this word were not explained there. The uses of this word, which in many contexts give room for doubt, must be examined for what meanings they indicate in which contexts.

The Nirukta author lists the word इळा (*iḷā*) among the names of the earth (Ni. 1-1), among the names of speech (1-11), and among the names of food (2-7). Here it is explained as food. Food may be either earthly wealth of food, or else a particular divine power that is the original cause of this food.

In places such as येषामिळा धृतहस्ता दुरोण आ अपि प्राता निषीदति । (*yeṣāmiḷā dhṛtahastā duroṇa ā api prātā niṣīdati |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-16-8), the goddess in the form of food, characterised as the oblation, अन्नरूपा हविर्लक्षणा देवी निषीदति । (*annarūpā havirlakṣaṇā devī niṣīdati |*): since the goddess in the form of food is described as sitting with butter in her hands, a particular power is indicated. There is room for the doubt whether the goddess Iḷā praised in the Āprī hymns is different from this Iḷā in the form of food; but if all the Śruti passages are examined closely, identity is what appears.

यज्ञे चेद्वै मावकल्पयिष्यसि बहुः प्रजया पशुभिर्भविष्यसि । (*yajñe cedvai māvakalpayiṣyasi bahuḥ prajayā paśubhirbhaviṣyasi |*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-19)**NOTE**

### Printed p. 453
This assurance — "if you perform the sacrifice with my help, the sacrificer will be endowed with wealth of food, of cattle and of offspring" — was spoken by the goddess Iḷā. Who is this Iḷā? What is her connection with the sacrifice? These matters are explained in detail in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. Although, in reality, the Iḷā described in many passages of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā and the Iḷā described in the Śatapatha are the same, particular usages give room for doubt. In some contexts the word इळॆ (*iḷè*) is used in the masculine; and in places such as इति त्वा देवा इम आहुरैळॆ .... .... (*iti tvā devā ima āhuraiḷè .... ....*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-95-18), Aila (Purūravas) raises the doubt whether he is a son of Iḷā (fem. इळॆ (*iḷè*)) or of Iḷa; so there is room for such doubt as well. If the Śruti passages are closely examined, there is no room for such doubts. To know in what context the above-quoted sentence यज्ञे चेद्वै मावकल्पयिष्यसि (*yajñe cedvai māvakalpayiṣyasi*) was spoken and what its real meaning is, the story of the Śatapatha must be known. In this narrative the origin, power and nature of Iḷā are fully understood. Thereafter one can understand that the Iḷā praised in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā has this same nature. Moreover, one can examine the appropriateness of the use of इळा (*iḷā*) in the present mantra concerning Mitra.

The origin of Iḷā and her earthly nature.
मनवे ह वै प्रातः .... .... .... .... तदप्येतदुत्तरस्य गिरेर्मनोरवसर्पणमित्यौघो ह ताः सर्वाः प्रजा निरुवाहाधेह मनुरेवैकः परिशिशिषे । (*manave ha vai prātaḥ .... .... .... .... tadapyetaduttarasya girermanoravasarpaṇamityaugho ha tāḥ sarvāḥ prajā niruvāhādheha manurevaikaḥ pariśiśiṣe |*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-1 to 6)

Manu reared a fish in the water brought for washing, and with the help of that fish crossed the great flood, and sat practising austerity at the place famed as Manu's mountain. When the flood had swept away all other creatures and he alone sat there in that tranquil setting practising austerity, the wish for offspring arose in him.

सोऽर्चञ्चाम्यंश्चकार प्रजाकामः । तत्रापि पाकयज्ञेनेजे स धृतं दधि मस्त्वामिक्षामित्यप्सु जुहवांचकार ततः संवत्सरे योषित्संबभूव सा ह पिब्बमानेवोदेयाय तस्यै ह स्म धृतं पदे संतिष्ठते तया मित्रावरुणौ संजग्माते ॥ (*so 'rcañcāmyaṃścakāra prajākāmaḥ | tatrāpi pākayajñeneje sa dhṛtaṃ dadhi mastvāmikṣāmityapsu juhavāṃcakāra tataḥ saṃvatsare yoṣitsaṃbabhūva sā ha pibbamānevodeyāya tasyai ha sma dhṛtaṃ pade saṃtiṣṭhate tayā mitrāvaruṇau saṃjagmāte ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-7)

Desiring offspring, Manu stayed silent, practising austerity and engaged in worship of the gods. At this time he performed a pāka-yajña and, in the rite belonging to it, offered butter, curds, whey ("Whey" printed) and āmikṣā ("Curds" printed) into the water. Within a year a woman came into being. When she arose, firm of limb (पिब्बमान (*pibbamāna*) = "firm", with limbs), she appeared with butter on her feet.
### Printed p. 454
(The epithet धृतहस्ता (*dhṛtahastā*), 7-16-8, in the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā was mentioned above.) At that time Mitra and Varuṇa met her.

ताग्ंहोचतुः कासीति । मनोर्दुहितेत्यावयोर्ब्रूष्टेति नेति होवाच य एव मामजीजनत तस्यॆवाहमस्मीति तस्यामपित्वमीषाते तद्वा जज्ञा तद्वा न जज्ञावतित्त्वेवेयाय सा मनुमाजगाम ॥ (*tāgṃhocatuḥ kāsīti | manorduhitetyāvayorbrūṣṭeti neti hovāca ya eva māmajījanata tasyèvāhamasmīti tasyāmapitvamīṣāte tadvā jajñā tadvā na jajñāvatittveveyāya sā manumājagāma ‖*)

When they asked who she was, she said, "I am Manu's daughter." When they pressed, "Say that you are ours," she said, "Certainly not; I belong to him who begot me; I am his daughter." They wished to have a share in her. Then she signified neither consent nor refusal, but went to her father Manu and joined him.

ताग्ं ह मनुरुवाच कासीति । तव दुहितेति कथं भगवति मम दुहितेति या अमूरस्त्वाहुतीरहौषीर्घृतं दधि मस्तामिक्षां ततो मामजीजनथाः साशीरस्मि तां मा यज्ञेवकल्पय यज्ञे चेद्वै मावकल्पयिष्यसि बहुः प्रजया पशुभिर्भविष्यसि याममुया कां चाशिषमाशासिष्यसे सा ते सर्वा समर्थिष्यत इति तामेशन्मध्ये यज्ञस्यावाकल्पयनमध्यग्ग् हैतद्यक्षस्य यदंतरा प्रयाजानुयाजान् ॥ (*tāgṃ ha manuruvāca kāsīti | tava duhiteti kathaṃ bhagavati mama duhiteti yā amūrastvāhutīrahauṣīrghṛtaṃ dadhi mastāmikṣāṃ tato māmajījanathāḥ sāśīrasmi tāṃ mā yajñevakalpaya yajñe cedvai māvakalpayiṣyasi bahuḥ prajayā paśubhirbhaviṣyasi yāmamuyā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāsiṣyase sā te sarvā samarthiṣyata iti tāmeśanmadhye yajñasyāvākalpayanamadhyagg haitadyakṣasya yadaṃtarā prayājānuyājān ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-9)

Then Manu too asked who she was. "Your daughter," she said. "O revered one, how are you my daughter?" he said. She replied: "By the oblations of butter, curds, whey and āmikṣā that you offered in the water, in the rite belonging to the pāka-yajña, I was produced; I am a blessing (āśīḥ) for all your undertakings. In sacrificial acts, if you seek my help and perform your rites together with me, you will be possessed of cattle, sons and all wealth. Whatever desires you have, you will obtain them all." On this assurance Manu obtained her help during the sacrificial acts performed in the middle, between the Prayājas and the Anuyājas.

तयर्चञ्चाम्यंश्चचार प्रजाकामः । तयेमां प्रजातिं प्रजज्ञे येयं मनोः प्रजातियाम्वेनया कां चाशिषमाशास्त्र सास्मै सर्वा समार्थ्यत॥ (*tayarcañcāmyaṃścacāra prajākāmaḥ | tayemāṃ prajātiṃ prajajñe yeyaṃ manoḥ prajātiyāmvenayā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāstra sāsmai sarvā samārthyata‖*)

With her help, worshipping and practising austerity, desiring a son, he remained absorbed in meditation. Through her he created this human progeny. Whatever gracious blessings of hers were to be obtained, he obtained them all and fulfilled his desires.
### Printed p. 455
सैषा निदानेन यदिडा । स यो ह्येवं विद्वानिडया चरत्येताग्ं हैव प्रजातिं प्रजायते यां मनुः प्राजायत याम्वेनया कां चाशिषमाशास्त्रे सास्मै सर्वा समृध्यते ॥ (*saiṣā nidānena yadiḍā | sa yo hyevaṃ vidvāniḍayā caratyetāgṃ haiva prajātiṃ prajāyate yāṃ manuḥ prājāyata yāmvenayā kāṃ cāśiṣamāśāstre sāsmai sarvā samṛdhyate ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-11)

This excellent woman is Iḍā in every respect. Whoever, knowing this truth, performs the rite together with Iḍā, increases this human progeny; through her he obtains all blessings and fulfils all his desires. (In इडया चरति (*iḍayā carati*) there are two meanings: one, "with the woman in the form of Iḍā"; the other, "with the pāka-yajña having the nature of Iḍā".)

The sacrificial nature of Iḷā.
Up to here the origin and nature of Iḍā as history have been explained; now the nature of Iḍā in the form of the sacrifice is explained. Iḍā is praised as the animal, Iḍā as food, Iḍā as everything.

सा वै पंचावत्ता भवति । पशवो वा इडा पांक्ता वै पशवः तस्मात्पंचावत्ता भवति । स समवदायेडां । पूर्वार्धं पुरोडाशस्य प्रशीर्य पुरस्ताद्भुवायै निदधाति ताग्ं होत्रे प्रदाय दक्षिणात्येति ॥ (*sā vai paṃcāvattā bhavati | paśavo vā iḍā pāṃktā vai paśavaḥ tasmātpaṃcāvattā bhavati | sa samavadāyeḍāṃ | pūrvārdhaṃ puroḍāśasya praśīrya purastādbhuvāyai nidadhāti tāgṃ hotre pradāya dakṣiṇātyeti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-12, 13)

Iḍā is of the nature of the animal. The animal has five chief parts; therefore Iḍā too is to be divided into five parts. (By sentences such as यो वै यज्ञं हविष्पंक्तिं वेद हविष्पंकिना यज्ञेन राध्नोति (*yo vai yajñaṃ haviṣpaṃktiṃ veda haviṣpaṃkinā yajñena rādhnoti*) etc., the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa explains these five kinds also, in four or five ways: Ai. Brā. 8-24.) The Adhvaryu divides Iḍā into five portions and places the forward part of the puroḍāśa on the barhis. Then he hands Iḍā to the Hotṛ. The division into five is made by these three acts: upastaraṇa, abhighāraṇa and sviṣṭakṛt.

Having thus stated the procedure belonging to the sacrificial process, the other-worldly power-nature of Iḍā is told next.

The worldly power-nature of Iḷā.
अथोपाग्ंशूपह्वयेते । एतद्ध वै मनुर्विभयां चकारेदं वै मे कनिष्ठं यज्ञस्य यदियमिडा पाकयज्जिया यद्वै म इह रक्षाग्‌सि याज्ञं न (*athopāgṃśūpahvayete | etaddha vai manurvibhayāṃ cakāredaṃ vai me kaniṣṭhaṃ yajñasya yadiyamiḍā pākayajjiyā yadvai ma iha rakṣāgsi yājñaṃ na*)

### Printed p. 456

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

हन्युरिति तामेतत्पुरा रक्षोभ्यः पुरा रक्षोभ्य इत्येवोपागंशूपाह्वयत तथो एवैनमेष एतत्पुरा .... .... पह्वयते ॥ (*hanyuriti tāmetatpurā rakṣobhyaḥ purā rakṣobhya ityevopāgaṃśūpāhvayata tatho evainameṣa etatpurā .... .... pahvayate ‖*)

On this occasion the Hotṛ calls Iḍā in a soft voice. Even so, Manu [thought]: "This act, which is a limb of the sacrifice, is not so firm. Therefore, before the fear of the demons draws near, Iḍā must be protected." Declaring just this wish, he calls her.

स उपह्वयते । उपहूतग्ं रथंतरग्ं सह पृथिव्योपमां वामदेव्यग्ं सहांतरिक्षेण ह्वयतामुपहूतं वामदेव्यग्ं सहांतरिक्षेण ह्वयतामुपहूतं बृहत्सह दिवोप मां बृहत्सह दिवा ह्वयतामिति तदेतामेनै तदुपह्वयमान इमांश्च लोकानुपह्वयत एतानि च सामानि ॥ (*sa upahvayate | upahūtagṃ rathaṃtaragṃ saha pṛthivyopamāṃ vāmadevyagṃ sahāṃtarikṣeṇa hvayatāmupahūtaṃ vāmadevyagṃ sahāṃtarikṣeṇa hvayatāmupahūtaṃ bṛhatsaha divopa māṃ bṛhatsaha divā hvayatāmiti tadetāmenai tadupahvayamāna imāṃśca lokānupahvayata etāni ca sāmāni ‖*)

Next he recites the mantras that praise Iḍā. If Iḍā is praised with these mantras, the three worlds beginning with the earth are praised and called for protection. How? By calling the earth together with the Rathantara sāman, the atmosphere together with the Vāmadevya, and the heaven-world together with the Bṛhat, he has called for protection Iḍā herself, who pervades the three worlds. In this way the invocation of the goddess Iḍā, in the form of praise, indicates her special powers.

उपहूता गावः सहर्षभा इति । पशवो वा इडा .... .... उपहूतेडा ततुरिरिति तदेनां प्रत्यक्षमुपह्वयते ततुरिरिति सर्वग् हैषा पाप्मानं तरति तस्मा दाह ततुरिरिति ॥ (*upahūtā gāvaḥ saharṣabhā iti | paśavo vā iḍā .... .... upahūteḍā tatuririti tadenāṃ pratyakṣamupahvayate tatuririti sarvag haiṣā pāpmānaṃ tarati tasmā dāha tatuririti ‖*)

The goddess Iḍā herself is of the nature of cattle. She is therefore called with the prayer that she appear together with the bull, and, since Iḍā herself brings about the quieting of all sin, that she come to the sacrifice in a form that gives victory.

उपहूतः सखा भक्ष इति । प्राणा वै सखा भक्षस्तप्राणमुपह्वयतउपहूतग्ं हेगिति तच्छरीरमुपह्वयते । (*upahūtaḥ sakhā bhakṣa iti | prāṇā vai sakhā bhakṣastaprāṇamupahvayataupahūtagṃ hegiti taccharīramupahvayate |*) (Śa. Brā. 1.8-1-2)

Iḍā is the dearest friend. Iḍā is the food that is the vital breath. Friend and food are forms of the vital breath and nothing else. The invocation, in the form of a prayer, is made to Iḍā, who is of the nature of the vital breath.

मानवी धृतपदीति । मनुर्ह्येतामग्रेऽजनयत तस्मादाह मानवीति धृतपदीति यदेवास्यै धृतं पदे समतिष्ठत तस्मादाह धृतपदीति ॥ (*mānavī dhṛtapadīti | manurhyetāmagre 'janayata tasmādāha mānavīti dhṛtapadīti yadevāsyai dhṛtaṃ pade samatiṣṭhata tasmādāha dhṛtapadīti ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-26)

### Printed p. 457
Thus the goddess Iḍā, described above as of the nature of a cow, bestower of victory, of the nature of food and of the vital breath, is famed as the daughter of Manu. Because ghee clung to her foot, the name Dhṛtapadī also became famous for her.

The spiritual nature of Iḍā.

उत मैत्रावरुणीति । यदेव मित्रावरुणाभ्याग्ं समगच्छत स एव मैत्रावरुणो न्यंगो ब्रह्मा देवकृतोपहूतेति ब्रह्मा ह्येषां देवकृतोपहूता दैव्या अध्वरव उपहूता मनुष्या इति तद्दैवांश्चैवाध्वरूनुपह्वयते ये च मानुषा वत्सा वै दैव्याअध्वरवोऽथ य इतरे ते मानुषाः॥ (*uta maitrāvaruṇīti | yadeva mitrāvaruṇābhyāgṃ samagacchata sa eva maitrāvaruṇo nyaṃgo brahmā devakṛtopahūteti brahmā hyeṣāṃ devakṛtopahūtā daivyā adhvarava upahūtā manuṣyā iti taddaivāṃścaivādhvarūnupahvayate ye ca mānuṣā vatsā vai daivyāadhvaravo 'tha ya itare te mānuṣāḥ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-27)

Iḍā, so described, has shown her relation also to Mitra and Varuṇa. Since, as soon as she was born of Manu, she appeared to Mitra and Varuṇa, she may also be called of the nature of Maitrāvaruṇa. Because she is made by the gods, she is also called Brahma. She is also the Adhvaru connected with the gods. The Adhvarus connected with the gods are like calves to Iḍā, who is of the nature of a cow. All, gods and men alike, obtain food only through Iḍā's favour. That Iḍā is the giver of food and herself of the nature of food. This Iḍā, famed as Maitrāvaruṇī and of the nature of food, is the one indicated in the Ṛk at hand. The meaning is that this food is itself of the nature of Brahma.

The milk of the cow that is Iḍā.

स होवाच । इडैव मे मानव्यग्निहोत्री वायुव्यो वत्सः सजूरुपसृष्टा विराट् संयोजनमाश्विनं दुह्यमानं वैश्वदेवं दुग्धं वायव्यमाह्रियमाणमाग्नेयमधिश्रितमैंद्राग्नमवज्योत्यमानं वारुणमद्भिः प्रत्यानीतं वायव्यमुद्वास्यमानं द्यावापृथिव्यमुद्वासितमाश्विनमुन्नीयमानं वैश्वदेवमुन्नीतं महादेवायोद्यतं वायव्यग्ं ह्रियमाणं वैष्णवं निगृहीतः ॥ (*sa hovāca | iḍaiva me mānavyagnihotrī vāyuvyo vatsaḥ sajūrupasṛṣṭā virāṭ saṃyojanamāśvinaṃ duhyamānaṃ vaiśvadevaṃ dugdhaṃ vāyavyamāhriyamāṇamāgneyamadhiśritamaiṃdrāgnamavajyotyamānaṃ vāruṇamadbhiḥ pratyānītaṃ vāyavyamudvāsyamānaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyamudvāsitamāśvinamunnīyamānaṃ vaiśvadevamunnītaṃ mahādevāyodyataṃ vāyavyagṃ hriyamāṇaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ nigṛhītaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 11-5-3-5)

"Iḍā, daughter of Manu, is my cow of the Agnihotra. The principle of Vāyu is the calf. The relation of the two is Virāj." [Here Sāyaṇa explains: वायुना संश्रितः द्यौः (*vāyunā saṃśritaḥ dyauḥ*), the connection of Vāyu with the atmosphere.] "When the calf joins this cow, after the drinking of the milk, at the time of milking it belongs to the Aśvins; after the milk has been drawn, to the Viśvedevas; when it is brought from the cow-pen, to Vāyu; when it is placed on the fire, to Agni; when it shines, to Indra and Agni; when it is brought out,

### Printed p. 458
to Heaven and Earth; at the time of removal, to the Aśvins; when it is raised up, to Mahādeva; when it is made ready for the Āhavanīya, to Viṣṇu." So Uddālaka explained. In such a context one should understand Iḍā to be a special power that propounds a very hidden principle.

The nature of this cow that is Iḍā, the greatness of this milk that is to be offered at the times of the Pāka-yajña and the like, and the wealth of food, in the form of Iḍā, that comes to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice with her help, are described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā as follows.

पाकयज्ञं वा अन्वाहिताग्नेः पशव उप तिष्ठंत इडा खलु वै पाकयज्ञस्यॆषांतरा प्रयाजानूयाजान् यजमानस्य लोकेवहिता तामाह्रियमाणामभि मंत्रयेत सुरूपवर्षवर्ण एहीति पशवो वा इडा पशूनेवोपश्वयते यज्ञं वै देवा अदुह्रन् यज्योऽसुराग्ं अदुहत्तेऽसुरा यज्ञदुग्धाः पराभवन् (*pākayajñaṃ vā anvāhitāgneḥ paśava upa tiṣṭhaṃta iḍā khalu vai pākayajñasyèṣāṃtarā prayājānūyājān yajamānasya lokevahitā tāmāhriyamāṇāmabhi maṃtrayeta surūpavarṣavarṇa ehīti paśavo vā iḍā paśūnevopaśvayate yajñaṃ vai devā aduhran yajyo 'surāgṃ aduhatte 'surā yajñadugdhāḥ parābhavan*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-1-1) **NOTE**

Wealth of cattle comes to one who has established the fire for the Pāka-yajña. Iḍā herself is this Pāka-yajña. She is placed between the Prayājas and the Anuyājas. Then one should pray, "O goddess of fair form and of the colour of the rain, be gracious." Since Iḍā is cattle, by this invocation cattle themselves are called. The gods called the sacrifice; the sacrifice called the Asuras. Therefore the Asuras suffered defeat.

यो वै यज्ञस्य दोहं विद्वान् यजतेऽप्यन्यं यजमानं दुहे सा मे सत्याशीरस्य यज्ञस्य भूयादित्याहैष वै यज्ञस्य दोहस्तेनैवैनं दुहे प्रत्ता वै गौर्दुहे प्रत्तेडा यजमानाय दुह एते वा इडाय्कॆ स्तना इडोपहूतेति वायुर्वत्सो यर्हि होतेडामुपह्वयेत तर्हि यजमानो होतारमीक्षमाणो वायुं मनसा ध्यायेत् । (*yo vai yajñasya dohaṃ vidvān yajate 'pyanyaṃ yajamānaṃ duhe sā me satyāśīrasya yajñasya bhūyādityāhaiṣa vai yajñasya dohastenaivainaṃ duhe prattā vai gaurduhe pratteḍā yajamānāya duha ete vā iḍāykè stanā iḍopahūteti vāyurvatso yarhi hoteḍāmupahvayeta tarhi yajamāno hotāramīkṣamāṇo vāyuṃ manasā dhyāyet |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-1-2)

Whoever knows this principle and the way of calling the sacrifice, the sacrifice in the form of Iḍā calls another sacrificer to help him. The sacrificer's reciting, "May the blessing of this sacrifice be fulfilled for me," is itself the milking of the sacrifice. The cow gives her consent to this milking. Since this same prayer is addressed to Iḍā, it is the cow in the form of Iḍā that has been called. [The response इडोपहूता (*iḍopahūtā*) shows the order followed by the gods, and उपहूतेडा (*upahūteḍā*) that of the Asuras. This is a point to be noted in the sacrificial procedure.] Before the worship that calls this cow,

### Printed p. 459
the calf must be joined to the cow. When the sacrificer prays addressing Iḍā, he should look at the Hotṛ's face and meditate on Vāyu.

मात्रे वत्समुपाव सृजति सर्वेण वै यज्ञेन देवास्सुवर्गं लोकमायन्हाकयज्ञेन मनुरश्रामृत्सेडा मनुमुपावर्तत तां देवासुरा व्यह्वयंत प्रतीचीं देवाः पराचीमसुरास्सा देवानुपावर्तत पशवो वै तद्देवानवृणत पशवोऽसुरानजहुर्यं कामयेतापशुस्स्यादिति पराचीं तस्यॆडामुप द्वयेतापशुरेव भवति ॥ (*mātre vatsamupāva sṛjati sarveṇa vai yajñena devāssuvargaṃ lokamāyanhākayajñena manuraśrāmṛtseḍā manumupāvartata tāṃ devāsurā vyahvayaṃta pratīcīṃ devāḥ parācīmasurāssā devānupāvartata paśavo vai taddevānavṛṇata paśavo 'surānajahuryaṃ kāmayetāpaśussyāditi parācīṃ tasyèḍāmupa dvayetāpaśureva bhavati ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-1-3)

While meditating on Vāyu he lets the calf go to the cow. It was by the help of this complete sacrifice that the gods obtained heaven. Manu too toiled for this sacrifice. Iḍā went to Manu. When gods and Asuras came to resort to this same Iḍā, the gods called her face to face and the Asuras with face turned away. Iḍā went to the gods and joined them. Therefore the gods obtained wealth of cattle; the Asuras did not obtain it. If a sacrificer wishes that someone remain without cattle, and one calls Iḍā on that man's behalf standing with face turned away, then that sacrificer becomes without cattle.

यं कामयेत पशुमान्त्स्यादिति प्रतीचीं तस्येडामुपह्वयेत पशुमानेव भवति ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति स त्वा इडामुप ह्वयेत य इडामुपहूयात्मानमिडायामुपह्वयेतॆति सा नः प्रिया सुप्रतूर्तिर्मघोनीत्याहेडामेवोपहूयात्मानमिडायमुपह्वयते व्यस्तमिव वा एतद्यज्ञस्य यदिडा सामि प्राश्नंति ॥ (*yaṃ kāmayeta paśumāntsyāditi pratīcīṃ tasyeḍāmupahvayeta paśumāneva bhavati brahmavādino vadaṃti sa tvā iḍāmupa hvayeta ya iḍāmupahūyātmānamiḍāyāmupahvayetèti sā naḥ priyā supratūrtirmaghonītyāheḍāmevopahūyātmānamiḍāyamupahvayate vyastamiva vā etadyajñasya yadiḍā sāmi prāśnaṃti ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-1-4) **NOTE**

If the sacrificer is to obtain wealth of cattle, one must stand face to face and call Iḍā with prayer on his behalf. At once that sacrificer obtains wealth of cattle. When calling Iḍā with prayer, the praiser sees unity between himself and Iḍā; the knowers of the principle say that he has made his own nature one with Iḍā. He prays: "May Iḍā be for my share the doer of what is dear, the giver of victory, and the giver of abundant wealth." Iḍā is, as it were, somewhat broken in the middle of the sacrifice. By saying that in it the meaning is enjoyed, and so on, her protective nature and her power to break the Asuras and others are described. And Iḍā's capacity to protect the world is explained still more fully.

सग्ग श्रवा ह सौवर्चनसस्तु मिंजमौपोदितिमुवाच यत्सत्रिणाग्ंहोता भूः कामिडामुपाह्वथा इति तामुपाह्व इति होवाचॆ या प्राणेन देवान्हा- धार व्यानेन मनुष्यानपानेन पितृनिति छिनत्ती सा न छिनत्ती ३ इति छिनत्तीति होवाच शरीरं वा अस्यै तदुपाह्वथा इति होवाच गौर्वै अस्यै शरीरं। (*sagga śravā ha sauvarcanasastu miṃjamaupoditimuvāca yatsatriṇāgṃhotā bhūḥ kāmiḍāmupāhvathā iti tāmupāhva iti hovācè yā prāṇena devānhā- dhāra vyānena manuṣyānapānena pitṛniti chinattī sā na chinattī 3 iti chinattīti hovāca śarīraṃ vā asyai tadupāhvathā iti hovāca gaurvai asyai śarīraṃ|*) (Śai. Saṃ. 1-7-2-1) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 460
Saṃśravas, son of Suvarcanas, asked Tumiñja Aupoditi: "When were you Hotṛ to those who perform a sattra sacrifice? In which form of Iḍā did you pray, praising her?" Aupoditi answered: "I prayed to that Iḍā who sustains the gods with the prāṇa breath, men with the vyāna breath, and the fathers with the apāna breath." To the question whether she is one who divides or one who does not divide, he answered that she is one who divides. "Then did you praise her body?" he asked. The body of that Iḍā is the cow.

गां वाव तौ तत्परवदतां या यज्ञे दीयते सा प्राणेन देवान्दाधार यया मनुष्या जीवंति सा व्यानेन मनुष्यान् यां पितृभ्यो घ्निंति सापानेन पित्र्यन् य एवं वेद पशुमान्भवत्यथ वै तामुपाह्व इति होवाच या प्रजाः प्रभवंतीः प्रत्याभवतीति ॥ (*gāṃ vāva tau tatparavadatāṃ yā yajñe dīyate sā prāṇena devāndādhāra yayā manuṣyā jīvaṃti sā vyānena manuṣyān yāṃ pitṛbhyo ghniṃti sāpānena pitryan ya evaṃ veda paśumānbhavatyatha vai tāmupāhva iti hovāca yā prajāḥ prabhavaṃtīḥ pratyābhavatīti ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-7-2-2) **NOTE**

The two of them, eager to know the meaning of the principle, were discussing that cow in the form of Iḍā. This Iḍā, offered for the sake of the sacrifice, sustains the gods in the form of prāṇa. She by whose support men live, those men she sustains with vyāna and is the cause of their growth; the fathers, for whose sake they slay her, she sustains with apāna. He who knows all these principles is possessed of wealth of cattle. Aupoditi answered: "I have prayed to that Iḍā who is the cause of the increase of creatures."

अन्नं वा अस्यैतदुपाह्वथा इति होवाचौषधयो वा अन्या अन्नमौपधयो वै प्रजाः प्रभवंतीः प्रत्या भवंति य एवं वेदान्नादो भवत्यथ वै तामुपाह्व इति होवाच या प्रजाः पराभवंतीरनुगृह्णांति प्रता,भवंतीर्गृह्णांतीति प्रतिष्ठां वा अस्यै तदुपाह्वथा इति होवाच ॥ (*annaṃ vā asyaitadupāhvathā iti hovācauṣadhayo vā anyā annamaupadhayo vai prajāḥ prabhavaṃtīḥ pratyā bhavaṃti ya evaṃ vedānnādo bhavatyatha vai tāmupāhva iti hovāca yā prajāḥ parābhavaṃtīranugṛhṇāṃti pratā,bhavaṃtīrgṛhṇāṃtīti pratiṣṭhāṃ vā asyai tadupāhvathā iti hovāca ‖*) (Kṛ. Saṃ. 1-7 2 3) **NOTE**

Then it amounts to praying for Iḍā's food. This food is itself in the form of herbs. If creatures prosper, they obtain these herbs that are of the nature of food. When Saṃśravas said that one who knows this principle eats food, Aupoditi said again: "I have prayed to Iḍā, who lifts up those fallen into misfortune and shows favour to them when they prosper." He replied that then he has obtained her complete support.

### Printed p. 461
इयं ना अस्यॆ प्रतिष्ठेयं वै प्रजाः पराभवंतीरनु गृह्णाति प्रत्याभवंतीर्गृह्णातिय एवं वेद प्रत्येक तिष्ठत्यथ वै तामुपाह्व इति होवाच यस्यॆ निक्रमणे धृतं प्रजास्संजीवंतीः पिबंति त्रि छिनत्ति सा न छिनत्ती ३ इति न छिनत्तीति होवाच प्र तु जनयतीत्येष वा इडामुपाह्वथा इति होवाच वृष्टिर्वा इडा वृष्टैः वै निक्रमणे धृतं प्रजास्संजीवंतीः पिबंति य एवं वेद प्रैव जायतेऽन्नादो भवति॥ (*iyaṃ nā asyè pratiṣṭheyaṃ vai prajāḥ parābhavaṃtīranu gṛhṇāti pratyābhavaṃtīrgṛhṇātiya evaṃ veda pratyeka tiṣṭhatyatha vai tāmupāhva iti hovāca yasyè nikramaṇe dhṛtaṃ prajāssaṃjīvaṃtīḥ pibaṃti tri chinatti sā na chinattī 3 iti na chinattīti hovāca pra tu janayatītyeṣa vā iḍāmupāhvathā iti hovāca vṛṣṭirvā iḍā vṛṣṭaiḥ vai nikramaṇe dhṛtaṃ prajāssaṃjīvaṃtīḥ pibaṃti ya evaṃ veda praiva jāyate 'nnādo bhavati‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-7-2-4)

This earth, the support of all and of the nature of Iḍā, is the one who lifts up those fallen into misfortune and favours those who are to grow. He who knows this principle obtains a complete and firm support for his existence and growth. When again he was asked whether this Iḍā is one who divides or one who does not, whether she is a divider or not, he said: she does not divide, but becomes the cause of increase. This Iḍā of great power is the rain. Relying on this rain, creatures drink ghee, the support of their life. For this satisfaction Iḍā, Dhṛtapadī, is the cause. The praiser who relies on her obtains all wealth and wealth of progeny: so is the greatness of Iḍā described. In the explanations above she is praised as a goddess pervading the universe; as the giver of support to gods, men and all; as the earth, support of all; as the giver of satisfaction to all worlds in the form of food; as the friend in distress; as having power to punish the wicked and protect the good; and as the very form of rain, the support of the life of the world. Ghee, the support of the world's life, is what is to be obtained through her favour. The Iḷā whom the Ṛk Saṃhitā praises as धृतहस्ता (*dhṛtahastā*) is praised in the Śatapatha and other texts as धृतपदी (*dhṛtapadī*). In the Ṛk at hand, which praises Mitra, Iḷā in the form of food is indicated, and the relation between Mitra and Iḷā is told. That she is of the nature of Maitrāvaruṇa has been stated above and its meaning explained. Since in the Ṛk at hand the word इळा (*iḷā*) is taken to mean food, only one aspect of Iḷā's nature is set forth.

अनमीवासः (*anamīvāsaḥ*)—the word अमीव (*amīva*) is formed from the word अम (*ama*), which gives the sense of disease (अम रोगे (*ama roge*)). अनमीवासः (*anamīvāsaḥ*) shows its negation: it means "free from disease". The word अमीव (*amīva*) is also used in the sense of "enemy". अमीवहन् (*amīvahan*) is an epithet of Indra and others, meaning "destroyer of enemies".

उपक्षियंतः (*upakṣiyaṃtaḥ*)—when the preverb उप (*upa*) joins the root क्षि (*kṣi*), the meaning is "dwell nearby". The word is used in this sense on many occasions. For example,

### Printed p. 462
Likewise in यस्य ते अग्ने अन्ये अग्नय उपक्षितो वया इव । (*yasya te agne anye agnaya upakṣito vayā iva |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-19-33), the word उपक्षितः (*upakṣitaḥ*) is used to convey that the other fires also dwell near the chief Agni. In the present Ṛk too that meaning is natural; yet the purport is that one stays near Agni and carries out the sacrificial rite.

> भद्रे कल्याणकारिणि सौमनसे सौमनस्यॆपि यजमाना वयं स्याम । भवेम ॥
> नमस्यः नमसि साधुः । तत्र साधुरिति यत् । तित्स्वरितः । अजनिष्ट । जनी प्रादुर्भाव
> इत्यस्य लुजि सिचि रूपं । सौमनसे । सुमनस इदमित्यर्थे तस्येदमित्यण् । प्रत्ययस्वरः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Mitra, the Sun set forth in the previous mantra, is नमस्यः (*namasyaḥ*), to be bowed to by all; सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*), one of good happiness, that is, easily served; राजा (*rājā*), lord of the whole world through giving light; सुक्षत्रः (*sukṣatraḥ*), for the word क्षत्र (*kṣatra*) denotes strength, so one endowed with good strength; वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*), the ordainer of the whole world. The Sun, endowed with such qualities, has been born, that is, has appeared. May we, the sacrificers, be in the good intention (सुमतौ (*sumatau*)) and the auspicious, welfare-bringing benevolence (सौमनसे (*saumanase*)) of that Sun, who is so endowed and worthy of sacrifice. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं मित्रः (*ayaṃ mitraḥ*)—this Mitra who is praised here
- नमस्यः (*namasyaḥ*)—worthy of worship
- सुशेवः (*suśevaḥ*)—served with ease
- राजा (*rājā*)—lord of the whole world
- सुक्षेत्रः (*sukṣetraḥ*)—possessed of excellent strength

- वेधाः (*vedhāḥ*)—creator of the world
- अजनिष्ट (*ajaniṣṭa*)—has been born
- तस्य (*tasya*)—of such a
- यज्ञियस्य (*yajñiyasya*)—Mitra (the Sun), worthy of worship

- भद्रे (*bhadre*)—and auspicious

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Here the Mitra who is praised has been born worshipful, served with ease, lord of the whole world, possessed of excellent strength and creator of the world. May we sacrificers be in the gracious and auspicious mind of this worshipful Sun.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
This Mitra has been engendered adorable and to be served, the sovereign (over all), endowed with vigour, the creator (of the universe); may we ever be in the good favour, in the auspicious approbation, of this adorable (Aditya).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this mantra addressed to Mitra, the two epithets राजा (*rājā*) and सुक्षेत्रः (*sukṣetraḥ*) show Mitra's qualities. When divine power is described as of two kinds, Brahma and Kṣatra, the Śruti passages praise Mitra as the deity signifying the Brahma-power and Varuṇa as the deity signifying the Kṣatra-power.
क्रतुदक्षौ ह वाअस्य मित्रावरुण् .... .... स दक्षो मित्र एव क्रतुर्वरुणो दक्षो ब्रह्मैव मित्रः क्षत्रं वरुणोऽभिगंतैव ब्रह्म कर्ता क्षत्रियः ॥ (*kratudakṣau ha vāasya mitrāvaruṇ .... .... sa dakṣo mitra eva kraturvaruṇo dakṣo brahmaiva mitraḥ kṣatraṃ varuṇo 'bhigaṃtaiva brahma kartā kṣatriyaḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 4-1-4-1)
Mitra is of the nature of the power of will (resolve); Varuṇa is of the nature of the power of action. Mitra is of the nature of Brahma, Varuṇa of Kṣatra; Brahma holds the will in the form of resolve, and Kṣatra the power that brings that resolve into the form of action: thus the relation and the difference between Brahma and Kṣatra are shown. This being so, the question arises how the epithet सुक्षत्रः (*sukṣatraḥ*) in the present Ṛk fits Mitra. But Sāyaṇa has said that here the word क्षत्र (*kṣatra*) means strength, and that the epithet राजा (*rājā*) means the self-luminous one who illumines the world, of the form of light.

### Printed p. 464
But the word क्षत्र (*kṣatra*) does not mean merely physical power. Since it is joined here with the other epithets, it shows Mitra's extraordinary qualities. Mitra here means Āditya, who is of the nature of Mitra.
दैवं क्षत्रं याचेदित्याहुरादित्यो वै दैवं क्षत्रमादित्य एषां भूतनामधिपतिः ॥ (*daivaṃ kṣatraṃ yācedityāhurādityo vai daivaṃ kṣatramāditya eṣāṃ bhūtanāmadhipatiḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 7-20)
This Āditya, the eye of the world, is the very essence of Kṣatra. By meditating on this greatness the sacrificer, through the protection of the Kṣatra-form power of Āditya, himself attains lordship: thus the nature of Āditya is praised. This power of Kṣatra has also the power to protect Brahma.
क्षत्रं तदपि विजेयं ब्रह्म यत्पाति शाश्वतं (*kṣatraṃ tadapi vijeyaṃ brahma yatpāti śāśvataṃ*) (Bṛ. De. 5-126)
That which has the power to protect the eternal Brahma is renowned as Kṣatra. By this great power all other powers must be protected.
तस्माक्षत्रात्परं नास्ति तस्माद्ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियमधस्तात् उपास्ते । (*tasmākṣatrātparaṃ nāsti tasmādbrāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyamadhastāt upāste |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-11)
That is why, in the Rājasūya and the like, even the Brāhmaṇa sits at a lower place than the Kṣatriya. This is divine power.
तच्छैयोरूपमत्यसृजत धर्मं तदेतत् क्षत्रस्य क्षत्रं यद्धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्मात्परं । (*tacchaiyorūpamatyasṛjata dharmaṃ tadetat kṣatrasya kṣatraṃ yaddharmastasmāddharmātparaṃ |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-24)
This Kṣatra-power is itself the regulation of the universe. Since it is the very law (dharma) of the universe, one who has obtained its protection, though weak, may obtain protection equal to that of the strong. This Kṣatra is of the nature of truth. What is Kṣatra is Dharma; what is Dharma is Kṣatra. Therefore this Kṣatra, the cause of the welfare of the world, is described as Āditya's power of regulating the universe, as productive of welfare, and as the upholder of right conduct. It is because of the great regard for moral conduct that in the present mantra, with भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम (*bhadre saumanase syāma*), the pure mind needed for excellent conduct is desired and prayed for. Therefore, whenever the word क्षत्र (*kṣatra*) stands as an epithet of the word मित्र (*mitra*), this purport is to be stated.
मित्रः क्षत्रं क्षत्रपतिः । क्षत्रमस्मिन्यज्ञे मयि दधातु । (*mitraḥ kṣatraṃ kṣatrapatiḥ | kṣatramasminyajñe mayi dadhātu |*) (Śa. Brā. 11-4-3-10)

### Printed p. 465
In all such sentences too, Mitra is called lord of Kṣatra in this sense. Because he illumines the world, the epithet राजा (*rājā*) also occurs. This epithet shows the world-lordship of Āditya, who is of the form of Mitra.
असावादित्य एकविग्ंशस्तद्दैवं क्षत्रग्ं सा श्रीस्तदाधिपत्यं तद्ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपं तत्स्वाराज्यमश्नुते ॥ (*asāvāditya ekavigṃśastaddaivaṃ kṣatragṃ sā śrīstadādhipatyaṃ tadbradhnasya viṣṭapaṃ tatsvārājyamaśnute ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 13-1-7-3)
This divine lord shining in the atmosphere is the power in the form of Kṣatra. By worshipping this Āditya, of the form of radiance, who illumines the world and brings welfare to it, a radiant sovereignty of one's own is obtained. This nature of Āditya, thus described, is described also in the present Ṛk, and the benevolence and the auspicious good mind to be gained through his grace are prayed for.
