##### Gist of the bhāṣya

(continuing) … of that sun, the visible, universally known, desirable bhargas, the orb of light that burns up sins, we hold in the mind as the object of meditation.

Or else: the word भर्गः (*bhargaḥ*) denotes food. Through the grace of the god Savitṛ who impels thoughts, we take up (धीमहि (*dhīmahi*), we hold) the fruit characterised by food and the like; that is, may we become its support. For भर्गः (*bhargaḥ*) in the sense of food and धी (*dhī*) in the sense of rites, the Atharvaṇa text is cited: वेदांश्चंदांसि सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गॊ देवस्य कवयोऽन्नमाहुः कर्माणि धियस्तदु ते प्रब्रवीमि प्रचोदयंत्सविता याभिरेतीति । (*vedāṃścaṃdāṃsi saviturvareṇyaṃ bhargò devasya kavayo 'nnamāhuḥ karmāṇi dhiyastadu te prabravīmi pracodayaṃtsavitā yābhiretīti |*) (Go. Brā. 1-32)**NOTE**.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—who
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—the intelligence concerned with rites
- प्रचोदयात् (*pracodayāt*)—impels
- तत् (*tat*)—such
- देवस्य (*devasya*)—of the god, of divine nature
- सवितुः (*savituḥ*)—of Savitṛ
- वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*)—to be worshipped by all
- भर्गः (*bhargaḥ*)—the light
- धीमहि (*dhīmahi*)—we meditate on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We meditate on the light, worshipped by the whole world, of such a Savitṛ, the god of divine nature, who impels in us the intelligence concerned with rites.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
We meditate on that desirable light of the divine Savitri, who influences our pious rites.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

On the sixth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra, while the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, this ṛk तत्सवितुः (*tatsavituḥ*) and the next ṛk देवस्य सवितुः (*devasya savituḥ*) are to be recited as the second and third ṛks of the Pratipat tṛca (a tṛca is a group of three ṛks). This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यमिति द्वे दोषो आगात् (*tatsaviturvareṇyamiti dve doṣo āgāt*) (Ā. 8-1).

And on the second day of the sacrifices called Abhiplava, Pṛṣṭhya and Ṣaḍaha, while the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras are recited, these two ṛks are to be recited as the first and second ṛks of the Pratipat tṛca. This is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यमिति द्वे आ विश्वदेवं (*tatsaviturvareṇyamiti dve ā viśvadevaṃ*) (Ā. 7-6).
### Printed p. 557
1) Sāyaṇa's explanation of the purport of the mantra तत्सवितुः (*tatsavituḥ*).

Sāyaṇa has shown that two kinds of meaning are possible for the word सवितृ (*savitṛ*) in this ṛk, and in accordance with it he has also explained the word भर्ग (*bharga*).

First, सवितृ (*savitṛ*) means Parameśvara, the inner controller of all, the impeller of the world, the creator of the world. The meaning of the word भर्ग (*bharga*) is the radiance that is of the nature of the Supreme Brahman. Because it destroys ignorance and the evil deeds that result from it, this radiance is well known by the apt name भर्ग (*bharga*). Because it is to be worshipped and revered by all, it has the adjective वरेण्यं (*vareṇyaṃ*). The word धी (*dhī*) means intellect. The purport is: let us meditate on this radiance, of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, which destroys ignorance, and may Savitṛ impel us to meditate in that way.

Second, सवितृ (*savitṛ*) means the sun, famous in the world. The word धी (*dhī*) means rites in worship of the sun. भर्ग (*bharga*) means the orb of light of Āditya, which destroys sin. The prayer is: may Savitṛ, the sun, impel us, who meditate on such an orb of light, to be devoted to rites.

Further, if on the authority of the Brāhmaṇa sentence वेदाश्चंदांसि तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं भर्गॊ देवस्य कवयोऽन्नमाहुः (*vedāścaṃdāṃsi tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargò devasya kavayo 'nnamāhuḥ*) (Go. Brā. 1-3-2)**NOTE** the word भर्ग (*bharga*) is taken to mean food, the purport becomes: by the grace of that Savitṛ who impels our intellect to be devoted to good rites, let us obtain fruit in the form of food and the like. If the meaning of the word *sava�tṛ* is shown to differ in this way, does the doctrine (tattva) then differ? Is a difference in the nature of the deity worshipped being stated? Do the words सवितृ (*savitṛ*), सूर (*sūra*), आदित्य (*āditya*), परब्रह्म (*parabrahma*) show different forms of one and the same principle, or do they show differences of principle as well? Such an inquiry is quite necessary in the present context.

2) Since the deity Savitṛ conveys the principle, the Gāyatrī is what the word सावित्रि (*sāvitri*) denotes.

तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं (*tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ*) is the great Gāyatrī mantra, famous in the world. It has Savitṛ as its deity; for that very reason it is also well known by the name सावित्रि (*sāvitri*). The Upaniṣad mantra गायत्रि मेव सावित्रीमनुब्रूयात् (*gāyatri meva sāvitrīmanubrūyāt*) teaches this identity (Bṛ. U. 5-14-5). The word सवितृ (*savitṛ*) means the Supreme Brahman; that the Supreme Brahman is the deity worshipped in this mantra is the (sentence continues on the next page)
### Printed p. 558
purport of the Upaniṣads. But since there is also room for objections, such as the pūrvapakṣa छंदोऽभिधानान्न (*chaṃdo 'bhidhānānna*) (Bra. Sū. 1-1-25), which state a meaning contrary to this purport and deny that the Supreme Brahman is the deity worshipped in this mantra, the meaning of this mantra must be examined thoroughly and its profound purport found out. This determination of the purport rests on the meaning of the word सवितृ (*savitṛ*).

3) The nature of Savitṛ as expressing the one principle.

It is the view of some among modern scholars that words such as सूर (*sūra*), सवितृ (*savitṛ*), आदित्य (*āditya*) show, in the Ṛk-saṃhitā, the diversity and the distinct kinds of deities.

"Savitri is comparatively a younger member of the Vedic Pantheon; this fact is simply corroborated by the very name of that God. The genesis of सवितृ (*savitṛ*) indicates cleanly a very last phase in the evolution of Vedic religious thought. The earlier and more important Gods of the Rig-Veda like वरुण (*varuṇa*), मित्र (*mitra*) and इंद्र (*iṃdra*) are mainly the personification of natural phenomena."

In this and similar ways Western scholars such as Oldenberg have expressed their opinion. The meaning is that deities such as Varuṇa, Indra and Mitra are ancient and Savitṛ is a more recent deity. That is, the conception of Savitṛ as a deity came to the ṛṣis who composed the Ṛk-saṃhitā only after a long time; the conception of this deity did not exist at first. The purport is that, having grasped the profundity of the variety of creation, they afterwards developed the conception of a special deity named Savitṛ in order to reflect that principle. Their view is that in this way a difference of name indicates a difference of deity. But careful examination shows that this is not quite the right opinion.

एक एनाग्निर्बहुधा समिद्ध एकः सूरो विश्वमनु प्रभूतः । एकैवोषाः सर्वमिदं वि भात्येकं वा इदं वि बभूव सर्वं ॥ (*eka enāgnirbahudhā samiddha ekaḥ sūro viśvamanu prabhūtaḥ | ekaivoṣāḥ sarvamidaṃ vi bhātyekaṃ vā idaṃ vi babhūva sarvaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-58-2).

As this mantra states clearly, the idea that one principle, which impels and nourishes all the affairs of the universe, pervades the universe is indicated, clearly and subtly, in many places in the Ṛk-saṃhitā.

यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोऽंशसंभवं ॥ (*yadyadvibhūtimatsattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā | tattadevāvagaccha tvaṃ mama tejo 'ṃśasaṃbhavaṃ ‖*) (Bha. Gī. 10-41)**NOTE**
### Printed p. 559
Just as is said in this sentence of the Gītā, the Nirukta authors too have thus stated the nature of the groups of deities described in Vedic literature, and the highest principle that is the source of all deities:

महाभाग्याद्देवताया एक आत्मा बहुधा स्तूयते । .... .... एकस्य आत्मनः अन्ये देवाः प्रत्यंगानि भवंति ॥ (*mahābhāgyāddevatāyā eka ātmā bahudhā stūyate | .... .... ekasya ātmanaḥ anye devāḥ pratyaṃgāni bhavaṃti ‖*) (Ni. 7-4).

The principle that is the source of all deities is one only. But the infinite qualities of that principle are manifested in infinite forms, and all the diversities are only distinctions of the manifold glory of this principle. The Vedic sentence एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदंति (*ekaṃ sadviprā bahudhā vadaṃti*) (1-164-46) also conveys this same point. तत्तत् स्थानविभागेन तत्र तत्रेह दृश्यते (*tattat sthānavibhāgena tatra tatreha dṛśyate*) (Bṛ. De. 1-70): the place and the nature of the action of each indicate the quality of that deity, but the original principle is one.

यो नः पिता जनिता यो विधाता धामानि वेद भुवनानि विश्वा । यो देवानां नामधा एक एव तं संप्रश्नं भुवना यंत्यन्या ॥ (*yo naḥ pitā janitā yo vidhātā dhāmāni veda bhuvanāni viśvā | yo devānāṃ nāmadhā eka eva taṃ saṃpraśnaṃ bhuvanā yaṃtyanyā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-82-3).

Viśvakarman alone, the producer of the whole world, created the many kinds of deities such as Indra and pervaded the whole universe. Because he is the producer of everything, he has also obtained the name Savitṛ. And Prajāpati, the creator, is described as Savitṛ and as Tvaṣṭṛ:

देवस्त्वष्टा सविता विश्वरूपः पुपोष प्रजाः पुरुधा जजान । इमा च विश्वा भुवनान्यस्य महद्देवानामसुरत्वमेकं ॥ (*devastvaṣṭā savitā viśvarūpaḥ pupoṣa prajāḥ purudhā jajāna | imā ca viśvā bhuvanānyasya mahaddevānāmasuratvamekaṃ ‖*) (Mu. Saṃ. 3-55 - C.F)**NOTE**

गर्भे नु नौ जनिता दंपती कर्देवस्त्वष्टा सविता विश्वरूपः । नकिरस्य प्र मिनंति व्रतानि वेद नावस्य पृथिवी उत द्यौः ॥ (*garbhe nu nau janitā daṃpatī kardevastvaṣṭā savitā viśvarūpaḥ | nakirasya pra minaṃti vratāni veda nāvasya pṛthivī uta dyauḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-10-5).

In all such places Prajāpati, the creator and impeller of the world, is described as showing variety through difference of name and difference of action, while being originally the one principle of all. Therefore the opinion that a separate deity named Savitṛ, of a form different from deities such as Sūra, Āditya, Agni and Indra, exists and is described in embodied form is mistaken. Creation of the world, impelling the world's affairs, regulating those affairs, and all such activities are related to Savitṛ. To establish that this Savitṛ is Āditya, the Supreme Person within Āditya, the Vedic sentences that are the basis of this conclusion have to be examined carefully.
### Printed p. 560
सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता (*savitā sarvasya prasavitā*) (Ni. 10-31): because he is the producer of everything, the name is Savitṛ. Having shown this etymology of the word, the Nirukta authors cite

सविता यंत्रृः पृथिवीमरम्णादस्कंभने सविता द्यामद्यंहत् । अश्वमिनाधुक्षद्दुनिमंतरिक्षमतूर्ते बद्धं सविता समुद्रं ॥ (*savitā yaṃtrṛḥ pṛthivīmaramṇādaskaṃbhane savitā dyāmadyaṃhat | aśvaminādhukṣaddunimaṃtarikṣamatūrte baddhaṃ savitā samudraṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-149-1).

Savitṛ has made the earth supported; he has made the unsupported atmosphere stand firm; and he has made the cloud that spreads over the sky pour rain. Having thus described Savitṛ's greatness, they ask कं अन्यं मध्यमात् एवं अवक्षत् (*kaṃ anyaṃ madhyamāt evaṃ avakṣat*): leaving aside the deity of the atmosphere, what other deity would the ṛṣi praise in this way? In answer, they state that आदित्योऽपि सवितोच्यते (*ādityo 'pi savitocyate*), that Savitṛ is also a synonymous name of Āditya. They cite the ṛk

हिरण्यस्तूपः सवितर्यथा त्वांगिरसो जुह्वे वाजे अस्मिन् । एवा त्वार्चन्नवसे वंदमानः सोमस्येवांशुं प्रति जागराहं ॥ (*hiraṇyastūpaḥ savitaryathā tvāṃgiraso juhve vāje asmin | evā tvārcannavase vaṃdamānaḥ somasyevāṃśuṃ prati jāgarāhaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-19-5),

show that Āditya has the epithet Savitṛ, and indicate that the words आदित्य (*āditya*) and सवितृ (*savitṛ*) are synonymous names.

4) Description of the divine nature of Savitṛ, the controller of the universe, with the etymology of the word सवितृ (*savitṛ*).

The root सू (*sū*), from which the word सवितृ (*savitṛ*) comes, has different senses: 1) *ṣū* in the sense of impelling; 2) *ṣūṅ* in the sense of release of the young from the womb. Words formed from this root are used in the senses of "create", "impel" and "pour out" (oblations and the like). Sāyaṇa has explained the word सवितृ (*savitṛ*) in all these senses as suits each context. By explaining these meanings he has shown that Savitṛ alone is the controller of the whole world. That Savitṛ is the lord of creation, maintenance and the regulations is evident from the Ṛk-saṃhitā's own descriptions.

तत्सविता वोऽमृतत्वमासुवदगोह्यं यच्छ्रवयंत ऐतन । त्यं चिच्चमसमसुरस्य भक्षणमेकं संतमकृणुता चतुर्वयं ॥ (*tatsavitā vo 'mṛtatvamāsuvadagohyaṃ yacchravayaṃta aitana | tyaṃ ciccamasamasurasya bhakṣaṇamekaṃ saṃtamakṛṇutā caturvayaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-110-3).

### Printed p. 561

In the Ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-110-3) quoted above, the deed of the Ṛbhus, who by Savitṛ's favour made the single cup (camasa) into four, must be taken as relating to the first creation of the world. Turning a state that is immortal and endless into a mortal form, and so making it finite, is the work of creation. This work of making things limited (bounded) belongs to the deity Savitṛ (or Sūra), the controller of the order of the seasons.

In all the passages यः पार्थिवानि विममे स एतशो रजांसि देवः सविता महित्वना । (*yaḥ pārthivāni vimame sa etaśo rajāṃsi devaḥ savitā mahitvanā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-3) and मानेनेव तस्थिना अंतरिक्षे वि यो ममे पृथिवीं सूरेयण । (*māneneva tasthinā aṃtarikṣe vi yo mame pṛthivīṃ sūreyaṇa |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-5), the use of the root मा (*mā*) with the prefix वि (*vi*) indicates the controlling work of Savitṛ who is of the form of the sun, and of the sun who is of the form of Savitṛ. It was Savitṛ's work to bring the three worlds, which were formless, into a formed shape. As in the Ṛk 1-110-3 quoted above, so in the Atharva-saṃhitā too there is the description चमस यस्मिन् यशो निहितं विश्वरूपं (*camasa yasmin yaśo nihitaṃ viśvarūpaṃ*) (A. Ve. 10-8-9)**NOTE**. This description is the very one stated in the Īśāvāsyopaniṣad: हिरण्मयेन पात्रेण सत्यस्यापिहितं मुखं (*hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukhaṃ*) (Īśa. 15)**NOTE**. The word पूष (*pūṣa*) addressed in this mantra of the Īśāvāsya means Sūra (the sun). The prayer here is: "Be the one who opens the face of the true Brahman of the solar orb, hidden by the golden vessel." The Ṛk-saṃhitā describes that the Ṛbhus made the truth, which was covered, imperceptible and beyond the senses, and which in its oneness was formless, into a formed thing, and produced variety so that it might become perceptible to the world. [That in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-161-11 the word ऋभु (*ṛbhu*) was explained as the sun's rays and the word अगोह्य (*agohya*) as the sun has been stated earlier, in the special topics of that Ṛk.] The Ṛbhus too, the pupils of Savitṛ who is of the form of the sun (Ai. Brā. 3-30), are the sun's rays. But then everything would be included in the sun alone.

This is like Savitṛ's lordship described in sentences such as वनानि विभ्यो नकिरस्य तानि व्रता देवस्य सवितुर्मिनंति। (*vanāni vibhyo nakirasya tāni vratā devasya saviturminaṃti|*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-7) and यस्येंद्रो वरुणो (*yasyeṃdro varuṇo*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-9). The lordship of Indra and others is also described by sentences such as एको विश्वस्यभुवनस्य राजा (*eko viśvasyabhuvanasya rājā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-46-2). Since such descriptions occur for every deity,

### Printed p. 562

another question arises: what then is Savitṛ's distinction? In answer, some have expressed the opinion that such a description is only figurative and holds no distinction; Savitṛ, like the other deities, is one of the lesser particular deities. To know Savitṛ's distinction, the nivid mantra relating to Savitṛ must be recited. For example:

न प्रमिये सवितुर्दैव्यस्य तद्यथा विश्वं भुवनं धारयिष्यति । यत्पृथिव्या वरिमन्ना स्वंगुरिर्वर्षन्दिवः सुवति सत्यमस्य तत् ॥ (*na pramiye saviturdaivyasya tadyathā viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ dhārayiṣyati | yatpṛthivyā varimannā svaṃgurirvarṣandivaḥ suvati satyamasya tat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-55-4)

In mantras of this kind Savitṛ's chief quality is described. Here activities such as the regulation of the universe and the protection of truth are indicated. In the same way,

(5) Varuṇa too, the overseer of Ṛta, is nothing but a particular manifestation of Savitṛ's glory.

In passages such as त्रिपंचाशः क्रीळति व्रात एषां देव इव सविता सत्यधर्मा (*tripaṃcāśaḥ krīḷati vrāta eṣāṃ deva iva savitā satyadharmā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-34-8), the protection of truth is shown to be Savitṛ's special quality. जगतः स्थातुरुभयस्य यो वशी (*jagataḥ sthāturubhayasya yo vaśī*) (4-53-6): Savitṛ is the master of the whole world, moving and unmoving. विश्वस्य हि श्रुष्टये .... .... .... रमते परिज्मन् (*viśvasya hi śruṣṭaye .... .... .... ramate parijman*) (2-38-2): whether subtle or gross, a thing moves only by his regulation. The Atharvaṇa describes the same in sentences such as देवस्य सवितुः सर्वे कर्म कृण्वंतु मानवाः । (*devasya savituḥ sarve karma kṛṇvaṃtu mānavāḥ |*) (A. Ve. 6-23-3). All this is like the description of the god Varuṇa, overseer of Ṛta. Therefore it must also be examined whether there is a difference between Savitṛ and Varuṇa; whether they are different deities, or two forms of one principle, or one thing described by different qualities.

If certain Saṃhitā sentences are examined, they appear to state the identity of Varuṇa and Savitṛ. For example, प्र त्वा मुंचामि वरुणस्य पाशाद्येन त्वाबध्नात् सविता सुशेवः । (*pra tvā muṃcāmi varuṇasya pāśādyena tvābadhnāt savitā suśevaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-24): here Varuṇa's noose and Savitṛ's noose are alike. In the commentary Sāyaṇa says that Varuṇa, impelled by Savitṛ, binds the born creatures with his noose. But releasing the person so bound is also Savitṛ's work, or must come about through his grace. That the protection of right conduct, the protection of truth and the regulation of the universe are a common property of Savitṛ and Varuṇa

### Printed p. 563

is clear in the passages 2-38-2; 3-33-6; 4-53-4; 10-34-8; 10-139-3 and others where Savitṛ is described, and in the Ṛks 6-70-1; 7-86-1; 8-41-10; 8-42-1 and others where Varuṇa is described. Because he upholds the order of the universe, Savitṛ is also addressed as Mitra: उत रात्रिमुभयतः परीयस उत मित्रो भवसि देव धर्मभिः (*uta rātrimubhayataḥ parīyasa uta mitro bhavasi deva dharmabhiḥ*) (5-81-4). The purport is that, being lord of the work of sustaining the world, Savitṛ is also famed by the name Mitra. As सर्वस्य प्रसविता (*sarvasya prasavitā*) (the impeller of all), the act of generation is not Savitṛ's work alone; he is also the cause of the world's continuance. बृहत्सुम्मः प्रसवीता निवेशनो जगतः (*bṛhatsummaḥ prasavītā niveśano jagataḥ*) and so on (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-53-6): thus Savitṛ's greatness is described.

Secondly, it is a noteworthy point that the very well known word असुर (*asura*), an epithet of Varuṇa, is also an epithet of Savitṛ. In passages such as तद्देवस्य सवितुर्वीर्यं महद्वृणीमहे असुरस्य प्रचेतसः (*taddevasya saviturvīryaṃ mahadvṛṇīmahe asurasya pracetasaḥ*) (4-57-1), Savitṛ's power is indicated in describing this special quality. That Savitṛ is praised in the same manner as Varuṇa, the destroyer of sin, shows the quality they share. For example:

अचित्ती यच्च कृमा दैव्ये जने दीनैर्दक्षैः प्रभूती पूरुषत्वता । देवेषु च सवितर्मानुषेषु च त्वं नो अत्र सुवतादनागसः ॥ (*acittī yacca kṛmā daivye jane dīnairdakṣaiḥ prabhūtī pūruṣatvatā | deveṣu ca savitarmānuṣeṣu ca tvaṃ no atra suvatādanāgasaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-54-3)

"O Savitṛ, if we have sinned through ignorance, through pride, through weakness, or through the weakness common to men, forgive it. If we have reviled a divine person or the gods, forgive it. May no harm come to us." This is a prayer like

यत्किं चेदं वरुण दैव्ये जनेभिद्रोहं मनुष्या ३ श्चरामसि । अचित्ती यत्तव धर्मा युयोपिम मा नस्तस्मादेनसो देव रीरिषः ॥ (*yatkiṃ cedaṃ varuṇa daivye janebhidrohaṃ manuṣyā 3 ścarāmasi | acittī yattava dharmā yuyopima mā nastasmādenaso deva rīriṣaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-89-5)

Here too the uniformity of the manner of prayer, the single style, is a noteworthy point. Looking at such passages one may say that Varuṇa and Savitṛ are one particular deity reflecting one principle. As the epithet सम्राट् (*samrāṭ*) belongs to Varuṇa, so in many places it indicates Savitṛ's lordship also.

### Printed p. 564

(6) Epithets showing the common nature of Savitṛ and Varuṇa

Two epithet words, अमति (*amati*) and माया (*māyā*), serve to show the unity of the two. Both are epithets denoting power and beauty. In the same manner in which the radiance of the golden Puruṣa within the sun is described, the power and beauty of Savitṛ and Varuṇa are described.

उदु ष्य देवः सविता ययाम हिरण्ययामवतिं यामशिश्रेत् । नूनं भगो हव्यो मानुषेभिर्वि यो रत्ना पुरूवसुर्दधाति ॥ (*udu ṣya devaḥ savitā yayāma hiraṇyayāmavatiṃ yāmaśiśret | nūnaṃ bhago havyo mānuṣebhirvi yo ratnā purūvasurdadhāti ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-38-1)

Here is the description of Savitṛ, who is of golden form; and

ऋतस्य बुध्न उषसामिषण्यन्वषा मही रोदसी आ विवेश । मही मित्रस्य वरुणस्य माया चंद्रेव भानुं वि दधे पुरुत्रा ॥ (*ṛtasya budhna uṣasāmiṣaṇyanvaṣā mahī rodasī ā viveśa | mahī mitrasya varuṇasya māyā caṃdreva bhānuṃ vi dadhe purutrā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-7)

here the description of Varuṇa's power of radiance; the two are alike. These two descriptions tell of the unearthly, supernatural radiance and divine power of one divine principle bearing the names Savitṛ and Varuṇa. As in the first example the word अमति (*amati*) is explained as divine radiance, so in the second too the word माया (*māyā*) is explained as divine radiance. As the word अमति (*amati*) has the epithet हिरण्ययीं (*hiraṇyayīṃ*), the word माया (*māyā*) has the simile चंद्रेव (*caṃdreva*). The nature of the two radiances is the same. In passages such as ऋतेन विश्वं भुवनं वि राजथः सूर‍्यामा धत्तो दिवि चित्रं रथं । (*ṛtena viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vi rājathaḥ sūryāmā dhatto divi citraṃ rathaṃ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-7) and विश्वा रूपाणि प्रति मुंचते कविः प्रासावीद्भद्रं द्विपदे चतुष्पदे । (*viśvā rūpāṇi prati muṃcate kaviḥ prāsāvīdbhadraṃ dvipade catuṣpade |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-2), the power is described of spreading their divine radiance over the whole world and making the entire universe attractive. The description of Varuṇa that explains this golden radiance, हिरण्यपक्षं वरुणस्य दूतं (*hiraṇyapakṣaṃ varuṇasya dūtaṃ*) (10-123-6), and the description of Savitṛ in हिरण्ययेन सविता रथेना देवो याति भुवनानि पश्यन् (*hiraṇyayena savitā rathenā devo yāti bhuvanāni paśyan*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-2) and the like, show the non-difference of the two. Moreover, as Savitṛ is established as being of the nature of the sun on the basis of Vedic sentences, there are clear proofs for saying that Varuṇa too is of the nature of the sun. In the Taittirīya-brāhmaṇa and other texts it is said नारुणो वा अश्वः (*nāruṇo vā aśvaḥ*) (Tai. Brā. 3-9-16-1)**NOTE**. As to the hidden meaning of this horse of Varuṇa, the scholar Eggling, when translating the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa, said as follows.

##### English translation (H. H. Wilson)
Varuna's horse is none other than the fiery races who pursue his diurual course across the all-encompassing arch of heaven, the sphere of

### Printed p. 565

Varuna, the all-ruler. It is in the form of the horse that the sun is thus lauded in the hymn in praise of Aswamedha.
[S. B. E. XLIV: p. XIX to 30]**NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

"This horse of Varuṇa, the lord of heaven and earth, is none other than the sun, who undergoes his daily revolution."

By many such proofs it must be said that Varuṇa too is a special manifestation of the sun. This point was set out at length earlier when explaining the mantra sentence ऋतादध्यादधाथे अनृतं (*ṛtādadhyādadhāthe anṛtaṃ*) (1-139-2) and the mantra अनश्वो जातो अनभीशुरर्वा........अचित्तं ब्रह्म जुजुषुर्युवानः (*anaśvo jāto anabhīśurarvā........acittaṃ brahma jujuṣuryuvānaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-152-5). And in the passages cited here a spiritual principle is stated which joins the sacrificial act, whose principle is hidden and not visible to ordinary sight, with the luminous abode of Varuṇa.

(7) The golden Puruṣa within the sun, who is of Savitṛ's nature.

Thus, if Savitṛ and Varuṇa are both special manifestations of the sun, the description of their golden form amounts to a statement of the sun's nature. The nature of the sun described in the Ṛk-saṃhitā by sentences such as हिरण्ययीं अमतिं (*hiraṇyayīṃ amatiṃ*), and the nature of the Supreme Puruṣa within the sun described in the Upaniṣads and other texts, are one and the same.

तस्य हैतस्य पुरुषस्य रूपं । यथा महारजनं वासः । यथा पांड्वाविकं, यथेंद्रगोपः, यथाग्न्यर्चिः, यथा पुंडरीकं । यथा सकृद्विद्युत्तं ॥ (*tasya haitasya puruṣasya rūpaṃ | yathā mahārajanaṃ vāsaḥ | yathā pāṃḍvāvikaṃ, yatheṃdragopaḥ, yathāgnyarciḥ, yathā puṃḍarīkaṃ | yathā sakṛdvidyuttaṃ ‖*) (Bṛ. U. 2-3-6)

The Bṛhadāraṇyaka's description is that the form of this Supreme Puruṣa shines like a cloth filled with saffron colour, like white silk, like the glow of the crimson indragopa insect, like a flame of fire, like a white lotus, like lightning.

य एषोऽंतरादित्ये हिरण्मयः पुरुषो दृश्यते हिरण्यश्मश्रुर्हिरण्यकेश आप्रणखात्सर्व एव सुवर्णः ॥ (*ya eṣo 'ṃtarāditye hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣo dṛśyate hiraṇyaśmaśrurhiraṇyakeśa āpraṇakhātsarva eva suvarṇaḥ ‖*) (Chā. U. 1-6-6)

All the beard of this golden Supreme Puruṣa within the sun is golden. The Chāndogya Upaniṣad's description, that from the nails of the feet to the head the form of this Puruṣa is exceedingly radiant and made attractive by divine light, is likewise equal to the description of Savitṛ's radiance quoted above. And this same sun in the Upaniṣads and other texts

### Printed p. 566

is praised in two ways. That the sun carries on the work of the world by his rising and setting movements is perceptible to ordinary sight. But the sun described in sentences such as न वै तत्र न निम्मोच नोदियाय कदाचन (*na vai tatra na nimmoca nodiyāya kadācana*) (Chā. U. 3-11; 1-3) has no rising or setting. For him it is always eternal day. And सकृद्विभातो हैवैष ब्रह्मलोकः (*sakṛdvibhāto haivaiṣa brahmalokaḥ*) (Chā. U. 8-4-2): here is the praise of the radiance of the eternal, supernatural Supreme Puruṣa within the sun, to the effect that the radiance of this divine world is eternal. It is this solar principle that holds all moving and unmoving things in a regulated state. The praise of the sun to be recited at the daily rites after the utterance of the Gāyatrī mantra तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं (*tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ*) is well known:

चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अंतरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थु षश्च ॥ (*citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī aṃtarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthu ṣaśca ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-1)

In this mantra both the sun's sphere of radiance, perceptible to ordinary sight, and the supernatural divine principle are praised. The radiant sun with his rays rises as the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa and pervades heaven and earth. The Supreme Self within this solar orb is like the self that brings unity to the whole world. He who is praised by sentences such as हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्रे भूतस्य जातः पतिरेक आसीत् ॥ स दाधार पृथिवीं द्यामुतेमां ॥ (*hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre bhūtasya jātaḥ patireka āsīt ‖ sa dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyāmutemāṃ ‖*) (10-121-1) is likewise this same Supreme Self who is of Savitṛ's form. It is therefore proper to state a purport relating to the Supreme Self for the mantra in hand. The commentary written by Bhaṭṭabhāskara on the Taittirīya-saṃhitā for this mantra is as follows.

यो देवस्सविता विश्वस्य प्रसवितास्माकं धर्मादिगोचरा धियः प्रेरयति तस्य स्वभूतं वरेण्यं सर्वैर्भजनीयं भर्गः पापानां तापनं तेजोमंडलात्मकं धीमहि मनसा धारयामः ॥ एवं बोधप्रकाशाभ्यां समस्तस्य प्रपंचस्योपकुर्वाणं श्रेयोऽर्थिभिर्भजनीयं सूर्यात्मना स्थितं पारमेश्वरं तेजः उपास्यत्वेनोपदिश्यते ॥ (*yo devassavitā viśvasya prasavitāsmākaṃ dharmādigocarā dhiyaḥ prerayati tasya svabhūtaṃ vareṇyaṃ sarvairbhajanīyaṃ bhargaḥ pāpānāṃ tāpanaṃ tejomaṃḍalātmakaṃ dhīmahi manasā dhārayāmaḥ ‖ evaṃ bodhaprakāśābhyāṃ samastasya prapaṃcasyopakurvāṇaṃ śreyo 'rthibhirbhajanīyaṃ sūryātmanā sthitaṃ pārameśvaraṃ tejaḥ upāsyatvenopadiśyate ‖*) (Tai. Saṃ. Bhā. 1-5-6-6)

In this commentary, by बोधप्रकाशाभ्यां उपकुर्वाणं (*bodhaprakāśābhyāṃ upakurvāṇaṃ*) two benefits of the sun's radiance are shown: first, the physical light needed for worldly affairs; second, the inner light that helps spiritual knowledge, that is, divine knowledge. Both benefits are possible through Savitṛ's bhargas. The commentary of Mahīdharācārya on this same mantra in the Śukla-yajus-saṃhitā is as follows—

### Printed p. 567

In this bhāṣya the words *bodhaprakāśābhyāṃ upakurvāṇaṃ* show two benefits of Āditya's radiance. The first is the physical light needed for worldly activity. The second is the inner light that helps spiritual knowledge, that is, divine knowledge. Both benefits are possible through the Bharga of Savitṛ. Mahīdhara Ācārya's commentary on this same mantra in the Śukla Yajus Saṃhitā runs as follows:

सवितुः प्रेरकस्यांतर्यामिणो विज्ञानानंदस्वभावस्य हिरण्यगर्भोपाध्यवच्छिन्नस्य वा आदित्यांतरपुरुषस्य वा ब्रह्मणः भर्गः पापानां भर्जनसमर्थं तेजः सत्यज्ञानानन्दादिवेदान प्रतिसाद्यं वयं ध्यायामः ॥ (*savituḥ prerakasyāṃtaryāmiṇo vijñānānaṃdasvabhāvasya hiraṇyagarbhopādhyavacchinnasya vā ādityāṃtarapuruṣasya vā brahmaṇaḥ bhargaḥ pāpānāṃ bharjanasamarthaṃ tejaḥ satyajñānānandādivedāna pratisādyaṃ vayaṃ dhyāyāmaḥ ‖*)

It is a prayer: "We meditate on the divine radiance of the Supreme Brahman. He is the inner controller in all beings and the impeller of the world. He is addressed by names such as Hiraṇyagarbha, and he dwells within Āditya. That radiance destroys sins and is taught by the Vedānta in forms such as truth, knowledge and bliss."

The radiance of Savitṛ of this kind is also well known under the names Sutejas and Sutatejas. The great radiance of which it is said

उद्वयं तमसस्परि ज्योतिष्पश्यंत उत्तरं । देवं देवत्रा सूर्यमगन्म ज्योतिरुत्तमं ॥ (*udvayaṃ tamasaspari jyotiṣpaśyaṃta uttaraṃ | devaṃ devatrā sūryamaganma jyotiruttamaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 150-10) **NOTE**

and so on in the Ṛk Saṃhitā, and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā:

अगन्न ज्योतिरुत्तममित्याहासौ वा आदित्यो ज्योतिरुत्तममादित्यस्यैव सायुज्यं गच्छति ॥ (*aganna jyotiruttamamityāhāsau vā ādityo jyotiruttamamādityasyaiva sāyujyaṃ gacchati ‖*) Tai. Saṃ. 5-1-8-6.

This radiance of Āditya is the Supreme Light. One who has crossed the darkness of ignorance attains union with it. It is noteworthy that, as it is praised in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, the Upaniṣads describe it as Sutejas, Sutatejas and so on. In एष वै सुतेजा आत्मा तस्मात्तव सुतं, प्रसुतमासुतं कुले जन्म (*eṣa vai sutejā ātmā tasmāttava sutaṃ, prasutamāsutaṃ kule janma*) (Chā. 5-12-1) **NOTE**, a relation of cause and effect is stated between the good radiance (sutejas) of Āditya and the constant pressing (suta) of Soma in the family that worships such a radiance. This point will be examined when the relation between Gāyatrī and Soma is explained. Here, the light that is praised in इदं श्रेष्ठं ज्योतिषां ज्योतिः (*idaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ jyotiṣāṃ jyotiḥ*) (1-113-1) and the like is, in the mantra under discussion, designated by the word Bharga. This Bharga is the light of the Supreme Brahman, which destroys ignorance.

**(8) The Supreme Light of the Supreme Person is the Bharga of Savitṛ.**
**(Objection and reply)**

When the Bharga of Savitṛ is thus established as the Supreme Light of the Supreme Person, another objection may be expected. Just as there is an attempt to place Savitṛ in the group of lesser deities, a view may state its opinion in the form of this objection: that this great radiance too is only physical light. For example, the Supreme Light described in the Ṛk Saṃhitā as सूरमगन्म ज्योतिरुत्तमं (*sūramaganma jyotiruttamaṃ*) is praised in the Upaniṣads and elsewhere as अध यदतः परो दिवो ज्योतिः (*adha yadataḥ paro divo jyotiḥ*) (Chā. U. 2-13-7). Is this only the physical light of the sun? Or is it the divine light of the divine Person who dwells within Āditya?

### Printed p. 568

Where this doubt exists, the opponent says: "आदित्यादिकमेव ज्योतिश्येन परिगृह्यत इति (*ādityādikameva jyotiśyena parigṛhyata iti*) — we call this only the light of the sun, which is visible to the physical eye." (Bra. Sū., Śaṅkara-bhāṣya, 1-1-24).

किं तावत्पाप्तं ? आदित्यादिकमेव ज्योतिश्यब्देन परिगृह्यत इति । कुतः प्रसिद्धेः । तमो ज्योतिरिति हीमौ शब्दौ परस्परप्रतिद्वंद्विविषयौ प्रसिद्धौ.... नहि चराचरबीजस्य ब्रह्मणः सर्वात्मकस्य द्यौर्मर्यादा युक्ता ॥ (*kiṃ tāvatpāptaṃ ? ādityādikameva jyotiśyabdena parigṛhyata iti | kutaḥ prasiddheḥ | tamo jyotiriti hīmau śabdau parasparapratidvaṃdviviṣayau prasiddhau.... nahi carācarabījasya brahmaṇaḥ sarvātmakasya dyaurmaryādā yuktā ‖*)

The words "darkness" and "light" are things perceived by the eye. And since the light belongs to the sky, it cannot be of the nature of the Supreme Brahman, which is endless and undivided. The sky is limited and not all-pervading. Therefore the light bounded by such a sky is also limited and, unlike the Supreme Brahman, not all-pervading. Hence, says the opponent, there is a difference between these lights and Brahman. The conclusion that answers this is:

नैष दोषः । सर्वत्रापि गम्यमानस्य ज्योतिषः परो दिवः इत्युपासनार्थः प्रदेशविशेषपरिग्रहो न विरुद्धते ॥ न तु निष्प्रदेशस्यापि ब्रह्मणः प्रदेशविशेषकल्पना भागिनी................ (*naiṣa doṣaḥ | sarvatrāpi gamyamānasya jyotiṣaḥ paro divaḥ ityupāsanārthaḥ pradeśaviśeṣaparigraho na viruddhate ‖ na tu niṣpradeśasyāpi brahmaṇaḥ pradeśaviśeṣakalpanā bhāginī................*)

When the nature of the effect is being explained, it is not right to attribute identity with the principle of the cause and then to limit to a region the all-pervading Lord. As in passages such as तद्देवा ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरायुर्होपासतेऽमृतं (*taddevā jyotiṣāṃ jyotirāyurhopāsate 'mṛtaṃ*) (Bṛ. U. 4-4-16), it is argued from that context that the text points to the Supreme Light of the Supreme Person. From the commentator's explanation of the mantra beginning तत्त्ववितुः (*tattvavituḥ*) it is understood that this same purport applies here also to the Bharga of Savitṛ.

**(9) To know the Bharga, which is the Supreme Light, the chief means is meditation in the form of reciting the Gāyatrī.**

The prayer is: "Impel our intellect to realise directly, through meditation, the Supreme Light of Savitṛ, which lies beyond worldly perception." That is, the nature of the Supreme Light of the Supreme Brahman can be known only by meditation in the form of reciting the great Gāyatrī mantra. Śaṅkarācārya states this very matter in the introduction to the Gāyatrī section of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad:

गायत्रीद्वारेण चोच्यते ब्रह्म सर्वविशेषरहितस्य “ नेति नेति ” इत्यादि विशेषप्रतिषेधगम्यस्य दुर्बोधत्वात् । सत्त्वनेकेषु छंदस्सु गायत्रा एव ब्रह्मज्ञानतयोपादानं प्राधान्यात् । सोमाहरणादितरच्छंदोक्षरा- हरणेनेतरच्छंदोव्याप्त्या च सर्वसवनव्यापकत्वाच्च यज्ञे प्राधान्यं गायत्र्याः । गायत्रीसारत्वाच्च ब्राह्मणस्य मातरमिव । हित्वा गुरुतरां गायत्रीं ततोऽन्यद्गुरुतरं न प्रतिपद्यते यथोक्तं ब्रह्मापीति तस्यामत्यंतगौरवस्य प्रसिद्धत्वात् । अतो गायत्रीमुखेनैव ब्रहोच्यते ॥ (*gāyatrīdvāreṇa cocyate brahma sarvaviśeṣarahitasya “ neti neti ” ityādi viśeṣapratiṣedhagamyasya durbodhatvāt | sattvanekeṣu chaṃdassu gāyatrā eva brahmajñānatayopādānaṃ prādhānyāt | somāharaṇāditaracchaṃdokṣarā- haraṇenetaracchaṃdovyāptyā ca sarvasavanavyāpakatvācca yajñe prādhānyaṃ gāyatryāḥ | gāyatrīsāratvācca brāhmaṇasya mātaramiva | hitvā gurutarāṃ gāyatrīṃ tato 'nyadgurutaraṃ na pratipadyate yathoktaṃ brahmāpīti tasyāmatyaṃtagauravasya prasiddhatvāt | ato gāyatrīmukhenaiva brahocyate ‖*)

### Printed p. 569

Supreme Brahman is beyond perception by the eye and the like. He is not an object visible to the eye, nor can he be seen by the mind's vision, nor is he any object in the world of ordinary dealings. The Supreme Self can be described only in the negative form, in this way. Though there are many other metres, realisation of the Supreme Self is possible only with the help of the Gāyatrī. That the Gāyatrī has this power as a means is shown by the prominent part it plays in the sacrificial act. Because sacrifices and other rites help divine knowledge, and because the Gāyatrī's help is indispensable in carrying out such sacrifices, the Gāyatrī is also the most important means to the knowledge of Brahman. This prominence is understood from three points:

(1) First, because the Gāyatrī brought to the gods the Soma that is central to the sacrifice;
(2) second, because it has drawn into itself the syllables of the other metres and pervades them all;
(3) third, because it pervades all three pressings (savana), the Gāyatrī has primacy in the sacrificial act.

Śaṅkarācārya makes clear that, because it is like a mother to Brāhmaṇas and the rest, and because the knowledge of the nature of Brahman also rests on the Gāyatrī, the Gāyatrī is the chief means for the direct realisation of the nature of the light of Brahman. What is the scriptural basis for each of these three points that Śaṅkarācārya states, and how is this primacy of the Gāyatrī described in the Śruti passages? This now has to be examined.

**(10) Three points showing the primacy of the Gāyatrī.**
**1. The episode of the bringing of Soma. The effort of the Śyena bird.**

First: सोमाहरणात् (*somāharaṇāt*), "because it brought the Soma that is central to the sacrifice". Thus the special power of the Gāyatrī is indicated. This episode of the bringing of Soma is described in all the most important places in the Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas. First of all,

### Printed p. 570

it is told as a story in the Ṛk Saṃhitā itself. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26 and 4-27, when Indra describes his own valour, he tells how that valour grew through drinking Soma, and how the Gāyatrī brought that Soma.

[Whether this description is the speech of the seer Vāmadeva or of Indra, and whether the deity of these sūktas is Indra or the Supreme Self, are also matters to note. That discussion is unnecessary here.

प्र सु ष विभ्यो मरुतो विरस्तु प्र श्येनः श्येनेभ्य अशुपत्वा । अचक्रया यत्स्वधया सुपर्णो हव्यं भरन्मनवे देवजुष्टं ॥ (*pra su ṣa vibhyo maruto virastu pra śyenaḥ śyenebhya aśupatvā | acakrayā yatsvadhayā suparṇo havyaṃ bharanmanave devajuṣṭaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-4)

O Maruts, may this Suparṇa, who brought this Soma desired by the gods to Manu in a chariot without a wheel, swiftly, be greater in vigour than the other Śyena birds, and may he receive greater honour.

भरद्यदि विरतो वेविजानः पथोरुणा मनोजना असर्जि । तॊयं ययौ मधुना सोम्येगोत श्रवो विविदे श्येनो अत्र ॥ (*bharadyadi virato vevijānaḥ pathoruṇā manojanā asarji | tòyaṃ yayau madhunā somyegota śravo vivide śyeno atra ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-5)

This Śyena bird rebuked the guardians of the Soma, carried off the Soma, and glided down through the sky at the speed of thought and helped; therefore honour on earth came to the whole company of Śyena birds.

ऋजीषी श्येनो ददमानो अंशुं परावतः शकुनो मंद्रं मदं । सोमं भरद्दादृहाणो देवानान्दिवो अमुष्मादुत्तरादादाय ॥ (*ṛjīṣī śyeno dadamāno aṃśuṃ parāvataḥ śakuno maṃdraṃ madaṃ | somaṃ bharaddādṛhāṇo devānāndivo amuṣmāduttarādādāya ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-6)

This bird, flying straight through the sky at the speed of thought and followed by the gods, brought the Soma and with it increased resolve and faith. By bringing the Soma it did good to the world.

आदाय श्येनो आभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सना आयुतं च साकं । अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥ (*ādāya śyeno ābharatsomaṃ sahasraṃ sanā āyutaṃ ca sākaṃ | atrā puraṃdhirajahādarātīrmade somasya mūrā amūraḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-7)

The Śyena bird brought the Soma from the heavenly world and helped in carrying out thousands of sacrifices. Indra, satisfied by drinking this Soma, grew in valour and crushed all his enemies.

### Printed p. 571

अव यच्छेनो अस्वनीदथ द्योर्वि यद्यदि वात ऊहुः पुरंधिं । सृजद्यदस्मा अव ह क्षिपज्ज्यां कृशानुरस्ता मनसा भुरण्यन् ॥ (*ava yaccheno asvanīdatha dyorvi yadyadi vāta ūhuḥ puraṃdhiṃ | sṛjadyadasmā ava ha kṣipajjyāṃ kṛśānurastā manasā bhuraṇyan ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-27-3)

यजिष्य ईमिंद्रावतो न भुज्युं श्येनो जभार बृहतो अधि ष्ठोः । अंतः पतत्पतत्र्यस्य पर्णमध यामनि प्रसितस्य तद्वेः ॥ (*yajiṣya īmiṃdrāvato na bhujyuṃ śyeno jabhāra bṛhato adhi ṣṭhoḥ | aṃtaḥ patatpatatryasya parṇamadha yāmani prasitasya tadveḥ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-27-4)

As this Śyena was coming down from the sky that lies under Indra's lordship, it was struck by Kṛśānu's arrow, and in its struggle it lost a feather from its body and was wounded.

While the story is of this kind, finding what principle lies here costs effort. Even so, introducing the seer of this sūkta, Nāmadeva **NOTE**, the Aitareya Āraṇyaka explains this same occasion from the standpoint of principle. There, quoting the Ṛk of the Ṛk Saṃhitā

गर्भे नु सन्नन्वेषामवेदमहं देवानां जनिमानि विश्वा । शतं मा पुर आयसीररक्षन्नध श्येनो जवसा निरदीयं ॥ (*garbhe nu sannanveṣāmavedamahaṃ devānāṃ janimāni viśvā | śataṃ mā pura āyasīrarakṣannadha śyeno javasā niradīyaṃ ‖*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-1)

it says गर्भ एव एतच्छयानो वामदेव एवमुवाच (*garbha eva etacchayāno vāmadeva evamuvāca*) (Ai. Ā. 2-5). It says that Vāmadeva, while still lying in the womb, knew this principle and spoke it. The meaning of the above mantra is that the origins and natures of all the gods were revealed to Vāmadeva while he was in the womb, and that, although there was a bondage made of hundreds of iron bars, he slipped out of it like a Śyena bird and flew towards the earth. The purport of this passage is not easy. Śaṅkarācārya, Ānandatīrtha and Sāyaṇa, when they explain this occasion, take the purport to be that Vāmadeva entered hundreds of bodies as bonds, finally became a knower, was freed from them and attained liberation. But if the context of the Aitareya Āraṇyaka is examined, स एवं विद्वान् आस्माच्छरीरभेदादूर्ध्व उत्क्रम्यामुष्मिन् स्वर्गे लोके सर्वान्नामानाप्तामृतः समभवत्समभवत् । (*sa evaṃ vidvān āsmāccharīrabhedādūrdhva utkramyāmuṣmin svarge loke sarvānnāmānāptāmṛtaḥ samabhavatsamabhavat |*) (Ai. Ā. 2-5): it says that Vāmadeva, who knew this principle while in the womb, gave up the earthly body and attained liberation. It is therefore understood that the words of Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-27-1 apply to Vāmadeva himself **NOTE**. Moreover, on the basis of the statement that in mantras such as 1-32-14 and 10-99-8 Indra is described as like the Śyena bird, some scholars hold that the mantra beginning "Garbhe nu …." (printed with abridgement dots)

### Printed p. 572

refers to Indra himself. But that is wrong. Some others have said that it is the speech of Soma (Ludwig).

**2. The Gāyatrī in the form of a bird is the Śyena.**

Sāyaṇa alone, however, says in

श्येनभावं समास्थाय गर्भाद्योगेन निस्सृतः । ऋषिगर्भे शयानःसन् ब्रूते गर्भे नु सन्निति ॥ (*śyenabhāvaṃ samāsthāya garbhādyogena nissṛtaḥ | ṛṣigarbhe śayānaḥsan brūte garbhe nu sanniti ‖*)
(introduction to the bhāṣya on 4-27-1)

that Vāmadeva himself, freed from the womb by the greatness of his yoga, utters this sentence. None of the English critics such as Ludwig has examined the reason and the basis for the Śyena being described in the form of the Gāyatrī. In describing this same occasion, the Śyena is called by the word Suparṇa and also by the word Gāyatrī. In some places, when explaining the word Śyena, Sāyaṇa explains it as शैनः शंसनीयगतिमान्पक्षि पक्ष्याकारा गायत्री (*śainaḥ śaṃsanīyagatimānpakṣi pakṣyākārā gāyatrī*). Since different words, Śyena, Suparṇa and Gāyatrī, are used in these contexts, a precise meaning cannot be stated here without knowing the narrative. So, after knowing this story as told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, one can examine what the principle is in the matter of the Gāyatrī bringing the Soma.

**3. The incidental story of Kadrū and Suparṇī. The sons of Suparṇī are the metres.**

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā this story is described as follows:

कद्रूश्च वै सुपर्णी चात्मरूपयोरस्पर्देताग्ं सा कद्रूस्सुपर्णीमजयताब्रवीत्तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि सोमस्तमाहर तेनात्मानं निष्क्रीणीष्टेतीयं वै कद्रूरसौ सुपर्णी छंदागांसि सौपर्णेयास्साब्रवीदस्मै वै पितरा पुत्रान् बिभृतस्तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि सोमस्तमाहर तेना - त्मानं निष्क्रीणीष्टेति मा कद्रूरवोचदिति जगत्युदपतच्चतुर्दशाक्षरा सती साप्राप्य न्यवर्तत तस्यै द्वे (*kadrūśca vai suparṇī cātmarūpayoraspardetāgṃ sā kadrūssuparṇīmajayatābravīttṛtīyasyāmito divi somastamāhara tenātmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīṣṭetīyaṃ vai kadrūrasau suparṇī chaṃdāgāṃsi sauparṇeyāssābravīdasmai vai pitarā putrān bibhṛtastṛtīyasyāmito divi somastamāhara tenā - tmānaṃ niṣkrīṇīṣṭeti mā kadrūravocaditi jagatyudapataccaturdaśākṣarā satī sāprāpya nyavartata tasyai dve*)

### Printed p. 573

अक्षरे अमीयेताग्ं सा दक्षिणाभिश्च तपसा चागच्छत्तस्मात्रिष्टुभो लोके माध्यंदिने सवने दक्षिणा नीयंत एतत्खलु वाव तप इत्याहुर्यस्स्वं ददातीति गायत्र्युदपतच्चतुरक्षरा सत्यजया ज्योतिषा तमस्या अजाभ्यरुंध तदजाया अजत्वग्ं सा सोमं चाहरच्चत्कारि चाक्षराणि साष्टाक्षरा समपद्यत ब्रह्मवादिनो वदंति कस्मात्सत्याद्गायत्री कनिष्ठा छंदसाग्ं सती यज्ञमुखं परीयायेति यदेवादसोममाहरत्तस्माद्यज्ञमुखं परैत्तस्मात्तेजस्विनीतमा पद्भां द्वे सवने समग्रह्ञान्मुखेनैकं यन्नुखेन समगृह्णात्तदधयत्तस्माद्वे सवने शुक्रवशी प्रातस्सवनं च माध्यंदिनं च तस्मात्तृतीयसवन ऋजीषमभिषुण्वंति धीतमिव हि मन्यंते । (*akṣare amīyetāgṃ sā dakṣiṇābhiśca tapasā cāgacchattasmātriṣṭubho loke mādhyaṃdine savane dakṣiṇā nīyaṃta etatkhalu vāva tapa ityāhuryassvaṃ dadātīti gāyatryudapataccaturakṣarā satyajayā jyotiṣā tamasyā ajābhyaruṃdha tadajāyā ajatvagṃ sā somaṃ cāharaccatkāri cākṣarāṇi sāṣṭākṣarā samapadyata brahmavādino vadaṃti kasmātsatyādgāyatrī kaniṣṭhā chaṃdasāgṃ satī yajñamukhaṃ parīyāyeti yadevādasomamāharattasmādyajñamukhaṃ paraittasmāttejasvinītamā padbhāṃ dve savane samagrahñānmukhenaikaṃ yannukhena samagṛhṇāttadadhayattasmādve savane śukravaśī prātassavanaṃ ca mādhyaṃdinaṃ ca tasmāttṛtīyasavana ṛjīṣamabhiṣuṇvaṃti dhītamiva hi manyaṃte |*)
(Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-6-1 to 3)

Kadrū and Suparṇī, the two of them, came to compete as to which of them was superior in her form. Kadrū won, defeated Suparṇī and kept her in her power. Then she gave the defeated Suparṇī this assurance: "In the third part of heaven there is Soma. Bring it, and you can obtain your release." Kadrū is this earth; Suparṇī is the sky. The metres are the offspring of Suparṇī. Kadrū told Suparṇī: "With the help of the children who are nourished for the service of their mother, bring me the Soma and obtain your freedom." In the same way Suparṇī too told her children of this occasion. Then the Jagatī, of fourteen syllables, flew up to the sky. But it could not get the Soma and turned back. It lost two syllables of the fourteen, and came back with the sacrificial animals. For this very reason the Jagatī metre is rich in the wealth of animals, and a man rich in animals is fit to be consecrated. Then the Triṣṭubh metre, of thirteen syllables, flew up to the sky. It too lost two syllables and did not obtain the Soma. But when it came back, it returned with the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) useful for the sacrifice and with the materials of austerity. Therefore in worldly practice the dakṣiṇā is offered at the midday pressing. One who gives away his wealth as a gift, that is called the act of austerity. Next the Gāyatrī, of four syllables, set out towards the sky together with an Aja (goat) in the form of light. That Aja made the Soma available to the Gāyatrī. Then, as the Gāyatrī came back taking the Soma, since it brought back with it the four syllables that the Triṣṭubh and the Jagatī had left behind there, these four syllables joined the four that it had before, and in all it became eight-syllabled. Thus, although it is the smallest of all the metres, because it brought the Soma, which is so important for the sacrifice, it holds a very prominent place in the sacrificial work; this is the view of the Brahmavādins. For that very reason it is the most brilliant of all the metres. That (the Gāyatrī in the form of a bird) with both feet

### Printed p. 574

…it brought two savanas, the Prātaḥ and the Mādhyandina, and one from the mouth. The savana brought from the mouth it drank. For this reason the morning savana and the midday savana are accompanied by pure (white) Soma, while the third savana is accompanied by ṛjīṣa (the pressed-out residue). This is the order stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa this account is somewhat different. It is told in two passages. First:

सोमो वै राजा गंधर्वेष्वासीत्तं देवाश्च ऋषयश्चाभ्यध्यायन्कथमयमस्मान्सोमो राजागच्छेदिति सा वागब्रवीत् स्त्रीकामा वै गंधर्वा मयैव स्त्रीया भूतया पणध्वमिति नेति देवा अब्रुवन्नथं वयं त्वदृते स्यामेति साब्रवीत्क्रीणीतैव यर्हि वाव वो मयार्थो भविता तर्ह्येव वोऽहं पुनरागंतास्मीति तथेति तया महानग्न्या भूतया सोमं राजानमक्रीणन्. (*somo vai rājā gaṃdharveṣvāsīttaṃ devāśca ṛṣayaścābhyadhyāyankathamayamasmānsomo rājāgacchediti sā vāgabravīt strīkāmā vai gaṃdharvā mayaiva strīyā bhūtayā paṇadhvamiti neti devā abruvannathaṃ vayaṃ tvadṛte syāmeti sābravītkrīṇītaiva yarhi vāva vo mayārtho bhavitā tarhyeva vo 'haṃ punarāgaṃtāsmīti tatheti tayā mahānagnyā bhūtayā somaṃ rājānamakrīṇan.*) (Ai. Brā. 5-2)

While King Soma was living among the Gandharvas, the gods and the ṛṣis, wishing to obtain him, fell to meditating on him. While they were pondering the way to obtain him, the goddess Vāk came before them and said: "The Gandharvas are fond of women. Send me; I shall bring Soma and hand him over to you." The gods said: "We cannot be without you. That will not do." Then Vāk said: "For the present send me and obtain Soma. Afterwards, as soon as you wish for me, I shall come to you." After she had given this assurance, they obtained Soma with her help. So it is said. The same occasion is told elsewhere in this manner.

**4. The efforts of the metres to fetch Soma, and their defeat.**

सोमो वै राजामुष्मिलोक आसीत्तं देवाश्च ऋषयश्चाभ्यध्यायन्कथमयमस्मान्सोमो राजागच्छेदिति तेऽब्रुवंशद्वासि यूयं न इमं सोमं राजानमाहरतेति तथेति ते सुपर्णा भूत्वोदपतंस्ते यत्सुपर्णा भूत्वोदपतंस्तदेतत् सौपर्णमित्याख्यानविद आचक्षते । छंदांसि नै तत्सोमं राजानमच्छाचरंस्तानि ह तर्हि चतुरक्षराणि चतुरक्षराण्येव छंदांस्यासन् सा जगती चतुरक्षरा प्रथमोदपतत्सा पतित्वार्धमध्वनो गत्वाश्राम्यता परास्य त्रीण्यक्षराण्येकाक्षरा भूत्वा दीक्षां च तपश्च हरंती पुनरभ्यवापतत्तस्मात्तस्य वित्ता दीक्षा वित्तं तपो यस्य पशवः संति जागता हि पशवो जगती हि तानादरदथ त्रिष्टुबुदपतता (*somo vai rājāmuṣmiloka āsīttaṃ devāśca ṛṣayaścābhyadhyāyankathamayamasmānsomo rājāgacchediti te 'bruvaṃśadvāsi yūyaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānamāharateti tatheti te suparṇā bhūtvodapataṃste yatsuparṇā bhūtvodapataṃstadetat sauparṇamityākhyānavida ācakṣate | chaṃdāṃsi nai tatsomaṃ rājānamacchācaraṃstāni ha tarhi caturakṣarāṇi caturakṣarāṇyeva chaṃdāṃsyāsan sā jagatī caturakṣarā prathamodapatatsā patitvārdhamadhvano gatvāśrāmyatā parāsya trīṇyakṣarāṇyekākṣarā bhūtvā dīkṣāṃ ca tapaśca haraṃtī punarabhyavāpatattasmāttasya vittā dīkṣā vittaṃ tapo yasya paśavaḥ saṃti jāgatā hi paśavo jagatī hi tānādaradatha triṣṭubudapatatā*) …

### Printed p. 575

…पतित्वा भूयोऽर्धादध्वनो गत्वाश्राम्यता परास्यैकमक्षरं त्रैक्षरा भूत्वा दक्षिणा हरंती पुनरभ्यवापतत्तस्मान्माध्यंदिने दक्षिणा नीयंते त्रिष्टुभो लोके त्रिष्टुब्बि ता आहरत् । (*patitvā bhūyo 'rdhādadhvano gatvāśrāmyatā parāsyaikamakṣaraṃ traikṣarā bhūtvā dakṣiṇā haraṃtī punarabhyavāpatattasmānmādhyaṃdine dakṣiṇā nīyaṃte triṣṭubho loke triṣṭubbi tā āharat |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-25)

(The same closing line stands printed twice.)

The gods thought for a long time how the Soma that was in the atmosphere could be obtained; then they approached the metres and begged: "Bring us the Soma of the atmosphere." Giving the assurance "So be it," they took the form of birds and flew up into the atmosphere. Because they were transformed into the form of suparṇas (birds) and flew to fetch Soma, this episode became famous as the Suparṇa legend. When those metres in bird form flew toward Soma, each of them consisted of only four syllables. The four-syllabled Jagatī, flying first into the atmosphere, tired out in the middle of the way. Leaving three of her syllables there, she returned with only the remaining one syllable. But on coming back she brought the dīkṣā (consecration) and tapas (austerity). Because Jagatī is closely related to wealth in cattle, one who has wealth in cattle obtains faith and the power of austerity. Then Triṣṭubh also, having passed the middle of the way, grew tired after going only a little further. Leaving only one of her syllables there, she returned with the other three. On coming back she brought the dakṣiṇā, the requisite of the sacrifice. Therefore, at the time of the Mādhyandina savana, the dakṣiṇā has preference.

**5. The victory of Gāyatrī.**

ते देवा अब्रुवन्गायत्रीं त्वं न इमं सोमं राजानमाहरेति सा तथे त्यब्रवीत्तां वै मा सर्वेण स्वस्त्ययनेनानुमंत्रयध्वमिति तथेति सोदपतत्तां देवाः सर्वेण स्वस्त्ययनेनान्वमंत्रयुत प्रेति चेति चेत्येतद्वै सर्वं स्वस्त्ययनं यत्प्रीति चेति चेति तद्योऽस्य प्रियः स्यात्तमेतेनानुमंत्रयेत प्रेति चेति तद्योऽस्य प्रियः स्यात्तमेतेनानुमंत्रयेत प्रेति चेति चेति स्वस्तेव गच्छति स्वस्ति पुनरागच्छति सा पतित्वा सोमपालान् भीषयित्वा पद्भ्यां च मुखेन च सोमं राजानं समगृभ्नाड्यानि चेतरे छंदसी अक्षराण्यजहितां तानि चोपसमगृभ्णात्तस्या अनु विसृज्य कृशानुः सोमपालः सव्यस्य पदो नखमच्चिदत्तच्छल्यकोऽभवत्तस्मात्सनखमिव यद्वशमस्रवत्सा वशाभवत्तस्मात्सा हविरिवाध यः शल्यो यदनीकमासीत्स सर्पो निर्दंश्यभवत्सहसस्सजो यानि पर्णानि ते मंथावला यानि स्नावानि ते गंडूपदा यत्तेजनं सोऽंधाहिः सो सा तथेषुरभवत् । (*te devā abruvangāyatrīṃ tvaṃ na imaṃ somaṃ rājānamāhareti sā tathe tyabravīttāṃ vai mā sarveṇa svastyayanenānumaṃtrayadhvamiti tatheti sodapatattāṃ devāḥ sarveṇa svastyayanenānvamaṃtrayuta preti ceti cetyetadvai sarvaṃ svastyayanaṃ yatprīti ceti ceti tadyo 'sya priyaḥ syāttametenānumaṃtrayeta preti ceti tadyo 'sya priyaḥ syāttametenānumaṃtrayeta preti ceti ceti svasteva gacchati svasti punarāgacchati sā patitvā somapālān bhīṣayitvā padbhyāṃ ca mukhena ca somaṃ rājānaṃ samagṛbhnāḍyāni cetare chaṃdasī akṣarāṇyajahitāṃ tāni copasamagṛbhṇāttasyā anu visṛjya kṛśānuḥ somapālaḥ savyasya pado nakhamaccidattacchalyako 'bhavattasmātsanakhamiva yadvaśamasravatsā vaśābhavattasmātsā havirivādha yaḥ śalyo yadanīkamāsītsa sarpo nirdaṃśyabhavatsahasassajo yāni parṇāni te maṃthāvalā yāni snāvāni te gaṃḍūpadā yattejanaṃ so 'ṃdhāhiḥ so sā tatheṣurabhavat |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-26)

### Printed p. 576

Then the gods approached Gāyatrī and prayed: "Bring us King Soma." Gāyatrī agreed, saying "So be it," and said that the gods should follow her reciting a svastyayana (auspicious) mantra. The gods gladly accepted this and set out reciting the svastyayana mantra "pra" and "ā". Because by reciting this mantra the journey is accomplished without obstacle and the purpose is achieved, the gods recited it. Gāyatrī reached the region where Soma was without obstacle, took up Soma with her feet and her mouth, and also took the four syllables (3+1) that Triṣṭubh and Jagatī had left behind, and returned. But Kṛśānu, the guardian of Soma, cut off the nail of her left foot. It was transformed into a porcupine and became a śalya (quill). The blood that flowed from it became a barren cow, and the bone-frame became a serpent; but it did not come to spit poison and bite. In the same way the feather became the bat, and the sinew the earth-worm; thus the form of the arrow became such.

**6. The primacy of Gāyatrī in the times of the savanas.**

सा यद्दक्षिणेन पदा समगृभ्यात्तत्पातःसवनमभवत्तद्गायत्री स्वमायतनमकुरुत तस्मात्तत्समृद्धतमं मन्यंते सर्वॆषां सवनानामग्रियो मुख्यो भवति श्रेष्ठतामश्नुते य एवं वेदाथ यत्सव्येन पदा समगृभ्यात्तन्माध्यंदिनं सवनमभवत्तद्विस्स्रंसत तद्विस्स्रस्तं नान्वाप्पोत्तूर्वं सवनं ते देवाः प्राजिज्ञासंत तस्मिंस्किष्टुभं छंदसामदधुरिंद्रं देवतानां तेन तत्समावद्वीर्यमभवत्तूर्वेण सवनेनोभाभ्यां सवनाभ्यां समावद्वीर्याभ्यां समावज्जामाभ्यां राध्नोति य एवं वेदाथ यन्नुखेन समगृभ्यात्तृतीयसवनमभवत्तस्य पतंती रसमधयत्तद्धीतरसं नान्वाप्पोत्तूर्वे सवने ते देवाः प्राजिज्ञासंत तत्त्वशुष्पपश्यंस्तद्यदाशिरमवनयन्त्याज्येन पशुना चरंति तेन तत्समावद्वीर्यमभवत्तूर्वाभ्यां सवनाभ्यां सर्वैः सवनैः समावद्वीर्यैः समानाज्यामिभी राध्नोति य एवं वेद । (*sā yaddakṣiṇena padā samagṛbhyāttatpātaḥsavanamabhavattadgāyatrī svamāyatanamakuruta tasmāttatsamṛddhatamaṃ manyaṃte sarvèṣāṃ savanānāmagriyo mukhyo bhavati śreṣṭhatāmaśnute ya evaṃ vedātha yatsavyena padā samagṛbhyāttanmādhyaṃdinaṃ savanamabhavattadvissraṃsata tadvissrastaṃ nānvāppottūrvaṃ savanaṃ te devāḥ prājijñāsaṃta tasmiṃskiṣṭubhaṃ chaṃdasāmadadhuriṃdraṃ devatānāṃ tena tatsamāvadvīryamabhavattūrveṇa savanenobhābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ samāvadvīryābhyāṃ samāvajjāmābhyāṃ rādhnoti ya evaṃ vedātha yannukhena samagṛbhyāttṛtīyasavanamabhavattasya pataṃtī rasamadhayattaddhītarasaṃ nānvāppottūrve savane te devāḥ prājijñāsaṃta tattvaśuṣpapaśyaṃstadyadāśiramavanayantyājyena paśunā caraṃti tena tatsamāvadvīryamabhavattūrvābhyāṃ savanābhyāṃ sarvaiḥ savanaiḥ samāvadvīryaiḥ samānājyāmibhī rādhnoti ya evaṃ veda |*) (Ai. Brā. 13-22)

The portion of Soma that Gāyatrī seized with her right foot became the Prātaḥsavana. This morning savana became Gāyatrī's own dwelling. Therefore the morning savana is regarded as the most prosperous of the savanas. One who knows this truth becomes foremost and chief among sacrificers. The portion of Soma that Gāyatrī seized with her left foot became the Mādhyandina savana. Because it slipped away, it did not obtain the excellence of the morning savana. The gods tried to remedy this deficiency, and placed in it Triṣṭubh among the metres and Indra among the deities…

### Printed p. 577

…Thereafter it too obtained the vigour of the morning savana. The man who knows the equal strength and wealth of these two savanas prospers. The portion of Soma seized with the mouth became the third savana. While she was flying, the Śyena, in the form of Gāyatrī, drank it. Therefore it did not obtain the equality of strength of the first two savanas. The gods recognised that this deficiency must be remedied. They then looked for it among the animals, and then worshipped it with the āśira and the offering of ājya. Thereafter it too obtained the strength of the first two savanas. One who knows this truth prospers.

**7. The section on the division of the syllables of the metres.**

ते वा इमे इतरे छंदसी गायत्रीमभ्यवदेतां वित्तं नावक्षराण्यनुपर्यागुरिति नेत्यब्रवीद्गायत्री यथा वित्तमेव न इति ते देवेषु प्रश्नमैतां ते देवा अब्रुवन्यथावित्तमेव व इति तस्माद्याप्येतर्हि वित्तां व्याहुरथा वित्तमेव न इति ततो वा अष्टाक्षरा गायत्र्यभवत्र्यक्षरा त्रिष्टुबेकाक्षरा जगती साष्टाक्षरा गायत्री प्रातःसवनमुदयच्छन्नाशक्कोत्रिष्टुप् त्रक्षरा माध्यंदिनं समनमुद्यंतुं तां गायत्र्यब्रवीदायान्यपि मेऽत्रास्त्विति सा तथेत्यब्रवीत् त्रिष्टुप् तां वै मैत्रैरष्टाभिरक्षरैरुपसंधेहीति तथेति .... सा द्वादशाक्षरा भूत्वा तृतीयसवनमुदयच्छत्ततो वा अष्टाक्षरा गायत्र्यभवदेकादशाक्षरा त्रिष्टुब् द्वादशाक्षरा जगती सर्वॆश्चंदोभिः समावद्वीर्यैः समावज्ञामिभी राध्योति य एवं वेद ॥ (*te vā ime itare chaṃdasī gāyatrīmabhyavadetāṃ vittaṃ nāvakṣarāṇyanuparyāguriti netyabravīdgāyatrī yathā vittameva na iti te deveṣu praśnamaitāṃ te devā abruvanyathāvittameva va iti tasmādyāpyetarhi vittāṃ vyāhurathā vittameva na iti tato vā aṣṭākṣarā gāyatryabhavatryakṣarā triṣṭubekākṣarā jagatī sāṣṭākṣarā gāyatrī prātaḥsavanamudayacchannāśakkotriṣṭup trakṣarā mādhyaṃdinaṃ samanamudyaṃtuṃ tāṃ gāyatryabravīdāyānyapi me 'trāstviti sā tathetyabravīt triṣṭup tāṃ vai maitrairaṣṭābhirakṣarairupasaṃdhehīti tatheti .... sā dvādaśākṣarā bhūtvā tṛtīyasavanamudayacchattato vā aṣṭākṣarā gāyatryabhavadekādaśākṣarā triṣṭub dvādaśākṣarā jagatī sarvèścaṃdobhiḥ samāvadvīryaiḥ samāvajñāmibhī rādhyoti ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 13-28)

After Gāyatrī had returned with the three syllables of Triṣṭubh and the one syllable of Jagatī, those two approached her and begged: "The syllables, our wealth, have come along with you. Give them back." Gāyatrī replied: "No, they are not yours; since I brought them, they have become mine." Then the two approached the gods and told their complaint. The gods took Gāyatrī's side: "Since you brought them, those four syllables have become yours. Just as in worldly dealings it is the custom that whatever property we have obtained becomes ours, so you have the right to take them as your own." Then Gāyatrī became eight-syllabled, Triṣṭubh three-syllabled, and Jagatī one-syllabled. Then Gāyatrī with her eight syllables became able to take part in the morning savana.

### Printed p. 578

But Triṣṭubh, with her three syllables, could not take part in the Mādhyandina savana. Then Gāyatrī said: "I too shall take part in the Mādhyandina savana; let me too have a share of the sacrifice there." Triṣṭubh said: "So be it; join me with your eight syllables." Together, as eleven-syllabled, she became helpful to the Mādhyandina savana. Jagatī, being one-syllabled, was unable to carry out the third savana. Then Gāyatrī again asked that she join her and that she too have a share in the third savana. Jagatī agreed, "So be it," and Gāyatrī joined her at the time of the third savana. Then, as twelve-syllabled, she became helpful to the third savana. Then Gāyatrī became eight-syllabled, Triṣṭubh eleven-syllabled, and Jagatī twelve-syllabled. One who knows this truth obtains all wealth through the grace of these metres, which possess equal strength and splendour. Thus there is praise of Gāyatrī.

**1. The identity of Agni, Gāyatrī and Śyena; their place in the times of the savanas.**

In this way the story of the identity of this Gāyatrī with the Śyena is told in many places. Likewise in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa:

स वै खलु बर्हिः प्रथमं यजति । तद्वै कनिष्ठछंदः सद्गायत्री प्रथमा छंदसां युज्यते (*sa vai khalu barhiḥ prathamaṃ yajati | tadvai kaniṣṭhachaṃdaḥ sadgāyatrī prathamā chaṃdasāṃ yujyate*) (Śa. Brā 1-8-2-10)

Although she is the lowest of all the metres, Gāyatrī by her own greatness carried off Soma from the atmosphere. This was possible only through her own inner power. By this power she transformed herself into the Śyena and accomplished that task. For that reason the gods also showed her the first honour and revered her.

श्येनाय त्वा सोमभृते विष्णवेत्वति । तद्दायत्रीमन्वाभजति सा यद्दायत्री श्येन्नो भूत्वा दिवः सोममाभरत् ॥ (*śyenāya tvā somabhṛte viṣṇavetvati | taddāyatrīmanvābhajati sā yaddāyatrī śyenno bhūtvā divaḥ somamābharat ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 3-4-1-12)

Because Gāyatrī, in the form of the Śyena, carried off Soma from the atmosphere, the offering is addressed to the Śyena, the Soma-bearer, who has the nature of Viṣṇu; thus hospitality is offered to Gāyatrī. And so on.

### Printed p. 579

Since this is said in many places of the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa — 3-9-4-10; 4-3-2-7; 1-7-1-1; 11-7-2 8 and others — one point must be noted.**NOTE**

श्येनाय त्वा सोमभृत इति । तद्गायत्रै मिमितेऽग्नये त्वा रायस्पोषद इत्यग्निर्वै गायत्री तद्गायत्रै मिमिते स यद्गायत्री श्येनो भूत्वा । (*śyenāya tvā somabhṛta iti | tadgāyatrai mimite 'gnaye tvā rāyaspoṣada ityagnirvai gāyatrī tadgāyatrai mimite sa yadgāyatrī śyeno bhūtvā |*) …. (Śa. Brā 3-9-4-10)

Thus identity is stated among Gāyatrī, Śyena and Agni. This unity of Agni and Gāyatrī, in which Gāyatrī, being of the nature of Agni, fetched Soma in the form of the Śyena, is supported also by the passages of the Ṛk Saṃhitā:

अग्नेर्गायत्र्यभवत् सयुग्योष्ठिहया सविता सं बभूव । अनुष्टुभा सोम उक्थैर्महस्वान् बृहस्पतेर्बृहती वाचमावत् ॥ (*agnergāyatryabhavat sayugyoṣṭhihayā savitā saṃ babhūva | anuṣṭubhā soma ukthairmahasvān bṛhaspaterbṛhatī vācamāvat ‖*) (18-130-4)**NOTE**

Here it is stated that Gāyatrī, closely related to Agni, became Agni's helper. The same is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā: निरमिमीत तमग्निर्देवतान्नसृज्यत गायत्रि छंदः (*niramimīta tamagnirdevatānnasṛjyata gāyatri chaṃdaḥ*) (7-1-1-4). Not mere close relation only: there are abundant authorities such as गायत्रि वा अग्निः (*gāyatri vā agniḥ*); गायत्रोऽग्निः (*gāyatro 'gniḥ*); अग्निर्वै गायत्रि (*agnirvai gāyatri*); गायत्रमग्नेश्छंदः (*gāyatramagneśchaṃdaḥ*) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-3-19; Tai. Brā. 1-1-5-3; Tai. Saṃ. 2 2-5-5 and others)**NOTE**. In all these identity is stated. Moreover, Agni and Gāyatrī are both deities connected with the morning savana. Stating this, the Nirukta says:

तिस्र एव देवताः इत्युक्तं पुरस्तात् तासां भक्तिसाहचर्यं व्याख्यानस्यामः । अथैतान्यग्निभक्तान्ययं लोकः प्रातःसवनं वसंतो गायत्री । (*tisra eva devatāḥ ityuktaṃ purastāt tāsāṃ bhaktisāhacaryaṃ vyākhyānasyāmaḥ | athaitānyagnibhaktānyayaṃ lokaḥ prātaḥsavanaṃ vasaṃto gāyatrī |*) (Ni. 7-8)

Earlier, when speaking of the deities, it was stated that three deities are the chief ones and all the others are their special manifestations. Among them, as to Agni's association and who share in the sacrifice: this earth, the morning savana, spring, Gāyatrī and so on; thus the unity of Agni, Gāyatrī and the morning savana is stated. The Maitrī Upaniṣad too states the same matter:

अग्निर्गायत्रं त्रिवृद्रथंतरं वसंतः प्राणो नक्षत्राणि वसवः । (*agnirgāyatraṃ trivṛdrathaṃtaraṃ vasaṃtaḥ prāṇo nakṣatrāṇi vasavaḥ |*) (Mai. U. 7-1)

And further:

अग्ने जुषस्व नो हविः पुरोळाशं जातवेदः । प्रातःसावे धियावसो ॥ (*agne juṣasva no haviḥ puroḷāśaṃ jātavedaḥ | prātaḥsāve dhiyāvaso ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-28-1)

### Printed p. 580

The Agni-hymn (आग्नेयं हि प्रातः सवनं (*āgneyaṃ hi prātaḥ savanaṃ*) Śa. Brā. 3-4-9-12) and भूरग्निर्ज्योतिरग्निरिति (*bhūragnirjyotiragniriti*) and what follows (Ai. Brā. 2-32): in this way the direct connection between the morning pressing and Agni is well known from the Śruti. Further: वसवस्तर्हग्निः। तस्मिन् यस्य तथाविधे जुह्वति।वसुष्टेवास्याग्निहोत्रग्ं हुतं भवति । (*vasavastarhagniḥ| tasmin yasya tathāvidhe juhvati|vasuṣṭevāsyāgnihotragṃ hutaṃ bhavati |*) (Tai. Brā. 2-1-10-1). Having thus stated the identity of Agni and the Vasus, it praises the matter by saying that an oblation offered in Agni is as if offered to the Vasus. For this very reason the deity who takes part in the morning pressing along with the Gāyatrī is indicated in some places as Agni and in others as the Vasus.

चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रं प्रातःसवनं तदस्य वसवोऽन्वायत्ताः प्राणा एव वसव एते हीदं सर्वं वासयंति । ( (*caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī gāyatraṃ prātaḥsavanaṃ tadasya vasavo 'nvāyattāḥ prāṇā eva vasava ete hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vāsayaṃti | (*) (Bhā. 81, 3-6-1) **NOTE**

The morning pressing is offered together with the Gāyatrī mantra (metre) of twenty-four syllables; the Vasus are those entitled to this share of the sacrifice. In the context of stating in this way the direct connection of Agni and the Gāyatrī, what is relevant for us is to examine whether these three, Agni, Śyena and Gāyatrī, all indicate one identity, or are different principles.

नवं नु स्तोममग्नये दिवः श्वेनाय जीजनं । वस्वः कुविद्वनाति नः ॥ (*navaṃ nu stomamagnaye divaḥ śvenāya jījanaṃ | vasvaḥ kuvidvanāti naḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-15-4)

Here Agni is designated as the Śyena of the heaven-world. The same sentence is cited in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (Tai. Brā. 2-4-8-1). The words दिवः शैनः (*divaḥ śainaḥ*) are used in the Ṛk-Saṃhitā, besides the mantra cited above, in two Ṛks, 7-56-3 and 10-92-6; but in those passages the word Śyena tells the nature of the Marut deities. If, however, Agni is regarded as belonging to lightning, then this word Śyena can apply to Agni also; this conclusion can be drawn on the strength of sentences such as वैश्वानरो यदि वा वैद्युतोऽसि (*vaiśvānaro yadi vā vaidyuto 'si*) (Tai. Brā. 3-10-5). In the Ṛk-Saṃhitā too support for this conclusion is found: गर्भे मातुः ऒतुष्टिता विदिद्युतानो अक्षरे (*garbhe mātuḥ òtuṣṭitā vididyutāno akṣare*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-16 35) **NOTE**. The Gāyatrī, which has Agni as her food or accompaniment, is likewise described with the epithet विदिद्युदती (*vididyudatī*) (Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 12-1-) **NOTE**. The commentator, explaining this Brāhmaṇa sentence, says: गायत्री च अग्निना सरोत्पत्तेस्तेजोरूपत्वात् दीप्यमाना भवति । अतः .... .... गायत्री एवोपस्थाते ॥ (*gāyatrī ca agninā sarotpattestejorūpatvāt dīpyamānā bhavati | ataḥ .... .... gāyatrī evopasthāte ‖*)

Since the Gāyatrī too was born together with Agni, the epithet विदिद्युदती (*vididyudatī*) that applies to Agni applies to the Gāyatrī as well. As in the sentence तेजो गायत्री (*tejo gāyatrī*) (Tai. Brā. 3-8-4), just as Agni is of the form of brilliance, the Gāyatrī too has the form of brilliance. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-3-8 and 10-95-10 also the word दविद्योत् (*davidyot*) is connected with the word विद्युत् (*vidyut*)

### Printed p. 581

In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, in the context of the Divaḥ-Śyena offering (3-12-1, 2), the mantra तुभ्यं ता अंगिरस्तम (*tubhyaṃ tā aṃgirastama*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-43-18) clearly points to Agni; and in the same context the mantra अश्याम तं काममग्ने (*aśyāma taṃ kāmamagne*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-5-7) also is addressed to Agni. Therefore there is no doubt that the epithet दिवःशैन (*divaḥśaina*) is a description of Agni. Further, is there a context in which the word सुपर्ण (*suparṇa*) too, just as it indicates the Śyena, indicates Agni? If so, what its meaning is must also be examined. Although this word Suparṇa is merely a synonym of "bird", in many places it has a hidden meaning. For example:

सुपर्णं विप्राः कवयो वचोभिरेकं संतं बहुधा कल्पयंति । (*suparṇaṃ viprāḥ kavayo vacobhirekaṃ saṃtaṃ bahudhā kalpayaṃti |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114 5)

Here, according to Sāyaṇa, it is an epithet of the Supreme Self; he explains सुपर्णं सुपतनं एकं संतं परमात्मानं (*suparṇaṃ supatanaṃ ekaṃ saṃtaṃ paramātmānaṃ*). This meaning of the principle will have to be examined later. In the present context, where the word Suparṇa is used with reference to the Āditya or Agni, it is explained as "rays":

यत्रा सुपर्णा अमृतस्य भागमनिमेषं विदथाभिस्स्वरंति । (*yatrā suparṇā amṛtasya bhāgamanimeṣaṃ vidathābhissvaraṃti |*) (1-164-21)

यस्मिन्वृक्षे मध्वदः सुपर्णा निविशंते सुवते चाधिविश्वे ॥ (*yasminvṛkṣe madhvadaḥ suparṇā niviśaṃte suvate cādhiviśve ‖*) (1-164.22)

In such places, when the material meaning is given, they are called the rays of the Āditya. The word Suparṇa is also used as a synonym for Agni or the Āditya: दिव्यं सुपर्णं वायसं बृहंतमपां गर्भं दर्शतनोषधीनां । (*divyaṃ suparṇaṃ vāyasaṃ bṛhaṃtamapāṃ garbhaṃ darśatanoṣadhīnāṃ |*) (1-164-52); this description indicates Agni who dwells in the middle region. In the places दिवः श्येनः (*divaḥ śyenaḥ*) and दिव्यं सुपर्णं (*divyaṃ suparṇaṃ*) the identity of Agni and the Āditya is what is stated. Thus it is understood that Śyena, Suparṇa, Agni and Gāyatrī are all synonyms of one principle; but the technical meaning has to be explained according to each context.

Śrī Rāmacandra.

9. Soma is the brilliance of the Āditya; the Gāyatrī is the chief means for knowing this.

In the present context, if the word Śyena is taken to mean Agni of the middle region or the Āditya, then the word Soma comes to mean the seed (retas) of that Āditya. That is, for the Supreme Brahman who is in the form of the Āditya also, Soma is present in the form of seed. This Soma is the seed that produces the creation of all beings.

### Printed p. 582

अथ यत्किंचेदमार्द्रं तद्रेतसोऽसृजत तदु सोम एतवद्वा इदं सर्वमन्नं चैवान्नादश्च सोम एवान्नमग्निरन्नादः । (*atha yatkiṃcedamārdraṃ tadretaso 'sṛjata tadu soma etavadvā idaṃ sarvamannaṃ caivānnādaśca soma evānnamagnirannādaḥ |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-4-6)

The one Supreme Brahman created from his seed all the moist things in the world. That seed is Soma. This Soma, offered in Agni, becomes with it mutually food and eater. Explaining this very matter, the Maitrī Upaniṣad says:

रविमध्ये स्थितः सोमः सोममध्ये हुताशनः । (*ravimadhye sthitaḥ somaḥ somamadhye hutāśanaḥ |*) (Mai. U. 6-38) **NOTE**

It states that Soma stands in the middle of the orb of the Āditya, and Agni in the middle of Soma. The relation between the Āditya and Soma is stated in many places of the Ṛk-Saṃhitā. For example:

महत्तत्सोमो महिषश्च कारापां यद्दर्भोऽवृणीत देवान् । (*mahattatsomo mahiṣaśca kārāpāṃ yaddarbho 'vṛṇīta devān |*)
आदधादिंद्रे पवमान ओजोऽजनयत्सूर्ये ज्योतिरिंदुः ॥ (*ādadhādiṃdre pavamāna ojo 'janayatsūrye jyotiriṃduḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-97-41)

Soma, the embryo of the waters that are in the Āditya, brought satisfaction to the gods; being in the form of virile power, it created in the Āditya the light of the universe. And:

त्वं समुद्रो आसि विश्ववित्कवे तवेमाः पंच प्रदिशो विधर्मणि । (*tvaṃ samudro āsi viśvavitkave tavemāḥ paṃca pradiśo vidharmaṇi |*)
त्वं द्यां च पृथिवीं चाति जभ्रिषे तव ज्योतींषि पवमान सूर्यः ॥ (*tvaṃ dyāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ cāti jabhriṣe tava jyotīṃṣi pavamāna sūryaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-86-29)

Here it is stated that Soma is the ocean of the middle region, the support of all light, and that the Āditya shines by Soma's power. Explaining what principle Soma reflects here, the scholar Eggeling has said as follows:

"The poet of 9-86-29 while saying ' Thou art the heavenly ocean (Samudra), thine are the lights (ज्योतींषि (*jyotīṃṣi*)) O Pavamana, thine the Sun ' seems to conceive Soma, as the bright ether, the azure ' Sea of light ' generally ". [Sacred Books of the East. Vol. XXVI. p. XV.]

Thus, on the basis of Śruti sentences, they hold that Soma is the luminous essence of the Āditya. The purport is that the nature of such brilliance is obtainable only with the help of the Gāyatrī.

### Printed p. 583

Secondly, what is the place of the Gāyatrī in the story cited from the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa: सोमो वै राजा गंधर्वेष्वासीत्.... ....तया महानग्न्या भूतया सोमं राजानमक्रीणन् (*somo vai rājā gaṃdharveṣvāsīt.... ....tayā mahānagnyā bhūtayā somaṃ rājānamakrīṇan*) (Ai. Brā. 1-27)? There is no reason for the doubt that here the bringing of Soma was done by a woman in the form of Speech, and that the Gāyatrī has no connection with Soma. Here the word Gandharva must be taken to mean the Āditya, the word Soma the brilliance of the Āditya, and the word Vāk the Gāyatrī in the form of speech. If it is asked what is the authority for this, the Śruti sentences themselves are the authority.

10. The Gandharva who guarded the Soma, the brilliance of the Āditya, is Hiraṇyagarbha.

गंधर्व इत्था पदमस्य रक्षति पाति देवानां जनिमान्यद्भुतः । (*gaṃdharva itthā padamasya rakṣati pāti devānāṃ janimānyadbhutaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-83-4)

गंधर्वः उदकानां धारकः आदित्यः सोमस्य द्युसंबंधिस्थानं रक्षति । (*gaṃdharvaḥ udakānāṃ dhārakaḥ ādityaḥ somasya dyusaṃbaṃdhisthānaṃ rakṣati |*) The Āditya, the bearer of the waters, guards the dwelling-place of Soma. There is a praise of the Āditya saying that this Soma protects the gods. This same Gandharva is also designated as Hiraṇyagarbha. On the sentence पतंगो वाचं मनसा बिभर्ति तां गंधर्वोऽवदद्गर्भे अंतः (*pataṃgo vācaṃ manasā bibharti tāṃ gaṃdharvo 'vadadgarbhe aṃtaḥ*) (10-177-2) Sāyaṇa says: गर्भॆ हिरण्मये ब्रह्मांडेऽंतर्वर्तमानः गंधर्वः हिरण्यगर्भः तां वाचमवदत् । (*garbhè hiraṇmaye brahmāṃḍe 'ṃtarvartamānaḥ gaṃdharvaḥ hiraṇyagarbhaḥ tāṃ vācamavadat |*)

The Gandharva, of the form of Hiraṇyagarbha, who is within the Brahmāṇḍa, first uttered the Speech lodged in himself; afterwards the gods, seers of the end (of things), placed that Speech in the place of truth. Thus the relation between the Supreme Self, of the nature of the Āditya, and Speech is described. The story of the bringing of Soma told in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa tells of the relation between this Supreme Person, who is within the Āditya, and the principle of Speech, and afterwards how Soma, the brilliance of the Āditya, became the protector of the gods.

दिवि वै सोम आसीत् ।....गंधर्वो विश्वावसुः पर्यमुष्णात् ।....सोमो वै भ्राट् । (*divi vai soma āsīt |....gaṃdharvo viśvāvasuḥ paryamuṣṇāt |....somo vai bhrāṭ |*) (Śa. Brā. 3-2-4-4)

By these sentences the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa tells the story cited earlier from the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. Here too it tells the manner in which the Gāyatrī, in the form of speech, carried off the Soma; the manner in which this Soma, in the form of brilliance, was contained within the Gandharva in the form of the Āditya; and that afterwards this brilliance is obtained by the man who worships the goddess Speech. By sentences such as सोमो वै भ्राट् (*somo vai bhrāṭ*) Soma is described as brilliance itself. The meaning is that the brilliance of the nature of Soma, from the Gandharva in the form of the Āditya, becomes obtainable through the Gāyatrī, which is of the nature of speech, and by means of this Gāyatrī, to the man who performs the worship. Thus, with Śruti sentences as proofs, for the words Suparṇa, Soma, Gandharva,

### Printed p. 584

Vāk and so on, the purport stated is not improper; this can be shown by citing it together with Sāyaṇa's commentary, and the explanation above can also be shown to be consistent.

चतुष्कपर्दा युवतिः सुपेशा धृतप्रतीका वयुनानि वस्ते । (*catuṣkapardā yuvatiḥ supeśā dhṛtapratīkā vayunāni vaste |*)
तस्यां सुपर्णा वृषणा नि षेदतुर्यत्र देवा दधिरे भागधेयं ॥ (*tasyāṃ suparṇā vṛṣaṇā ni ṣedaturyatra devā dadhire bhāgadheyaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114-3)

Here, and in the following mantras of this same sūkta, Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of purport: one an explanation that tells a material principle, the other one that explains a spiritual principle. In this cited mantra the meaning is that the Suparṇas are established in Speech. The woman who has four braids (kaparda), namely noun, verb, preposition and particle, who is of ever-youthful form, of the nature of the shining Upaniṣad and the like, adorns herself with garments in the form of knowledge. In such a beautiful woman the individual self and the Supreme Self are established. The meaning is that the principle of light, described as of the nature of Suparṇa and Gandharva, can be realised only through the woman in the form of Speech. Sāyaṇa holds that this is what is described by योषित्कामा वै गंधर्वाः (*yoṣitkāmā vai gaṃdharvāḥ*) and the like (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa commentary 3-2-4-5).

सुपर्णं विप्राः कवयो वचोभिरेकं संतं बहुधा कल्पयंति । (*suparṇaṃ viprāḥ kavayo vacobhirekaṃ saṃtaṃ bahudhā kalpayaṃti |*)
छंदांसि च दधतो अध्वरेषु ग्रहान्त्सोमस्य मिमते द्वादश ॥ (*chaṃdāṃsi ca dadhato adhvareṣu grahāntsomasya mimate dvādaśa ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114-2)

In Ṛks of this kind also the above view is what is explained. Stating the relation among the Supreme Self in the form of Suparṇa, the metres such as Gāyatrī, and Soma as the means of worship, the purport is that the nature of the Supreme Self can be known with the help of metres such as Gāyatrī and by the means in the form of Soma. In all such contexts there is a praise of the Gāyatrī, which possesses a special power either as the direct means of knowledge or as a supporter of the rite that is a means of knowledge.

It was stated earlier that the Ācārya says in the Śaṅkara-bhāṣya that the Gāyatrī is the most important means for realising the Supreme Brahman, and that the greatness of the Gāyatrī is known from three points. Of these, the first, namely the manner of the bringing of Soma and its purpose, and the purport of the statement that the Gāyatrī carried off Soma, has been stated along with proofs from Śruti sentences. Of the points stated by Śaṅkarācārya, the second must now be examined.

### Printed p. 585

The distinctiveness of the Gāyatrī among the metres.

इतश्चंदोक्षराहरणेन.... अनेकेषु छंदस्सु गायत्रा एव ब्रह्मज्ञानद्वारतयोपादानं प्राधान्यं । (*itaścaṃdokṣarāharaṇena.... anekeṣu chaṃdassu gāyatrā eva brahmajñānadvāratayopādānaṃ prādhānyaṃ |*) **NOTE**

The praise that the Gāyatrī is pre-eminent because it pervades all the other metres and has unified everything in itself is well known in the Śruti sentences themselves.

तद्वै कनिष्ठं छंदः सद्गायत्री प्रथमा छंदसां युज्यते तदु तद्विर्येणैव यच्छ्येनो भूत्वा दिवः सोममाभरत् । (*tadvai kaniṣṭhaṃ chaṃdaḥ sadgāyatrī prathamā chaṃdasāṃ yujyate tadu tadviryeṇaiva yacchyeno bhūtvā divaḥ somamābharat |*) (Śa. Brā. 1-6-2-10)

Although it is the smallest in form among all metres, the Gāyatrī holds the foremost place among all metres. The explanation that by its own power it was transformed into the form of the Śyena and brought the Soma has been given above. Moreover, it has been stated earlier, citing sentences of the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa, that it added its own eight syllables to the Triṣṭubh, which remained with three syllables, and made it of eleven syllables; and that the Jagatī, which remained with one syllable, joined with the Triṣṭubh united with the Gāyatrī and was made to become of twelve syllables (Ai.
